Sports.title: Fulham 1 Newcastle 1: Rodrigo Muniz rescues a point for struggling Cottagers after Jacob Murphy’s moment of magic
Sports.content:
Next

TAKE A BOW Rodrigo Muniz – as the Brazilian rescued a point for Fulham and gave under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle an uncomfortable fortnight on Tyneside.

A bizarre week for Newcastle fans – in which they learned one of their players was a real life Robin Hood – ended with the first Premier League stalemate between these two sides at Craven Cottage.



On 80 minutes, Jacob Murphy had scored a stunner for the visitors, a goal that looked like it might give the beleaguered German a much-needed victory heading into the November international break.

But three minutes later, Fulham sub Muniz silenced the Toon Army in West London with an ingenious goal that eased the pressure on his own gaffer, Alvaro Arbeola.





On reflection, Newcastle – who had a first-half goal by Dan Burn ruled out for a foul – will feel more aggrieved with this point, given that they had surrendered the lead so cheaply.

But it would have been a long journey back to the North East for fuming Jaissle, who was seen complaining routinely about the on-field decisions, particularly in the tunnel at half-time.

And on the full-time whistle he was engaged in a long conversation with the fourth official.

Jaissle’s first big call of the afternoon had been to field Dedic and not remove him from the firing line following a crazy week for the player.



Days ago it emerged that Dedic had incredibly sparked a police manhunt after he was spotted by a walker carrying a BOW AND ARROW in the countryside.

Dedic and his friend were questioned by coppers but when it was felt there was no threat to the public, the Bosnia international was allowed on his way – though his archery equipment was confiscated.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Austrian-born right-back has since tried to laugh off the controversy by posting a gif online of Legolas, the fictional character from the Lord of the Rings saga, who kills enemies with arrows.

Yet in truth, there was no need to rest him or keep him hidden from the spotlight – after all, this is Craven Cottage, not exactly a bearpit of English football, nor the same gauntlet as Anfield or Elland Road.



For beleaguered Jaissle and his side, there were some comforts in being away from home for a change.

The Toon have been wretched at St James’ Park and were booed off the pitch by unhappy souls when they lost 1-0 on Monday night to Everton.

And had it not been for star man Lukas Hornicek on 12 minutes, there would have been more grumbles from the Newcastle faithful.

Oscar Bobb tried his luck from inside the box, controlling with his right foot and then shooting with his left, yet the Czech goalkeeper produced an acrobatic save.

From the resultant corner, there was mild panic in the Newcastle box when Gonzalo Garcia was found unmarked at the back post but the Spaniard could not keep down his header.



Harvey Barnes – known for his bow-and-arrow celebration – was more accurate for the visitors on 19 minutes but Fulham goalie Bernd Leno was alert to the goalbound flick.

The next time Barnes went forward with intention he was released free on goal by William Osula’s pinpoint pass and he should have scored but his attempt slammed against the head of Leno.

From the next corner, when the ball was delivered into the box by Murphy, Newcastle skipper Dan Burn thought he had scored with a clever tap-in at the near post.



Yet a foul was given against Newcastle because in the build-up, Yoane Wissa was caught holding back Timothy Castagne, who had played Burn onside, and referee Robert Jones deemed it to be a “deliberate foul”.

Down the other end, Josh King could have marked his England call-up with a spectacular goal but his exceptional first-time strike from outside the box on 37 minutes, executed with wonderful technique, was parried by Hornicek.

Minutes into the second half, Barnes was at it again, trying his luck from distance, but his powerful strike flew wide from Wissa’s pass – his third opportunity to break the deadlock.

Fulham fans were off their seats screaming for a penalty on 74 minutes when Sander Berge was brought down by Burn but the referee did not see much of an infringement as the Norwegian went tumbling.

Shortly after that, Berge’s loose pass in midfield contributed to the opener as Murphy collected the ball and he accelerated forward before beating Leno with a brilliant strike.



It was a goal worthy of winning any Premier League match but Newcastle’s defensive demons resurfaced and when they failed to clear possession, Muniz flicked his attempt beyond Hornicek with the outside of his boot.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Perhaps a point was the justified result in the end but Hornicek ensured it was not a loss with the best save of all – a brilliant stop from Fulham sub Ryan Sessegnon in stoppage time.

Sports.title: Arsenal ratings: Captain Fantastic Odegaard takes matters into his own hands after Havertz froze in front of goal
Sports.content:
Next

MARTIN ODEGAARD snatched all three points for Arsenal as they ensured they will go into the International break on top of the table.

The Gunners had to fight hard to topple a feisty Hull side, but Odegaard’s second-half winner was enough to keep breathing space between them and their title rivals.



The Arsenal capatain tidily tucked home from inside the box after Noni Madueke‘s drilled effort was parried by Hull stopper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Here’s how SunSport Arsenal Reporter Joshua Hall rated each individual Arsenal performance…



DAVID RAYA – 7

A shaky moment when he couldn’t get hold of a loose ball in the box from a first-half corner, but an otherwise assured performance.

Made a few good saved down low to stop a shock from the visitors.

JURRIEN TIMBER – 7

The Dutchman’s defensive strengths help balance Arsenal out at the back when Calafiori is playing and this game was no different.

Although, Timber still looked like he could cause problems in the opposition’s half with some smart runs to stretch the Hull defence.

EZRI KONSA – 7

William Saliba‘s omission from the match-day squad silenced any talk of Konsa displacing the Frenchman for now.

But another strong showing from the defender evidenced why Saliba will have a tall task on his hands to get back into the team when he is back to full fitness.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 7

Assured as always, with some nice passing to help break through Hull’s press at times.

Credit has to go to Gabriel for the way he has adapted to Konsa too, not just the other way around.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 6

A few of his signature marauding runs helped cause havoc in the Hull box in the first half.

Arteta ultimately sacrificed the Italian for Piero Hincapie in the second half to offer more defensive stability when rolling the dice on some other attacking changes.



BRUNO GUIMARAES – 7

A good showing from the Brazilian, who is settling into this Arsenal team now.

His desire to be a difference-maker and match-winner is admirable, but can sometimes lead to him making rash decisions and taking unnecessary pop-shots.

DECLAN RICE – 7

Another commanding performance from Arsenal’s midfield general.

His powerful runs from deep helped Arsenal to progress the ball forward at times, while his defensive contribution is always invaluable.



However, his passing was wayward at times and Arsenal could have done with Myles Lewis-Skelly alongside him.

MARTIN ODEGAARD – 8

A lot of pressure is lumped on the Arsenal captain to find the answer against teams that try and starve the Gunners of chances.

He made some clever passes in-behind that could have amassed to more if it wasn’t for some sloppy forward play.

Ultimately, he had to take matters into his own hands and took the winner like a veteran striker.



NONI MADUEKE – 8

The winger has a point to prove after being left out of Thomas Tuchel‘s England squad and he played like it too.

Madueke was always looking to find a route into the box, whether it was by carrying it in himself or delivering a ball into the danger zone.

Bukayo Saka‘s injury was always going to be a huge loss for the Gunners, but Madueke has stepped up in a big way to full the gap.

CHRISTOS TZOLIS – 7

Kept popping up in dangerous areas, but was snatching at his efforts and never managed to make the most of the chances he did get.



He still offered more threat on the left wing than Eberechi Eze has in recent weeks, but looks like he needs more time to return to his early-season form.

KAI HAVERTZ – 5

Kept making the right runs in-behind the Hull back line, but seemed to freeze when he got in front of goal.

His tendency to drift offside has become a point of frustration for a lot of Arsenal fans and was evident when VAR ruled out a first-half penalty shout for his early run.

Havertz has now been offside SEVEN more times than any other Premier League player this season.



SUBSTITUTES

VIKTOR GYOKERES (for Havertz, 63 mins) – 6

Not given enough time to fully settle into the side, but made some good runs when Arsenal broke from the back.

MIKEL MERINO (for Rice, 63 mins) – 6

Helped gain more control in midfield and offered threat in the box.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

EBERECHI EZE (for Tzolis, 68 mins) – 7

A positive cameo in which he was looking to create whenever he had the ball.

PIERO HINCAPIE (for Calafiori, 68 mins) – 7

Shored things up at the back to see out the three points.



MARTIN ZUBIMENDI (for Guimaraes, 89 mins) – N/A

Sports.title: Arsenal 1 Hull 0: Martin Odegaard saves the day after Tigers frustrate champions and controversial penalty decision
Sports.content:
Next

MARTIN ODEGAARD spent much of last season watching on as Arsenal won the Premier League.

But afternoons like this one underline how the Gunners skipper will be key to them retaining their crown.



Mikel Arteta’s side had looked on course to drop points until Odegaard’s goal in the 72nd minute.

Up until that moment, Hull had frustrated Arsenal and shown why they are not doomed for relegation as so many predicted before this season.



Kai Havertz having a penalty turned down because he was controversially offside in the build-up only added to the feeling it would be one of those days for the reigning champions.

That was until Odegaard stepped up.



And how sweet it must have been for the Norwegian, who was dogged by injuries for so much of last season.

The Gunners skipper lifted the Prem trophy on that famous day at Selhurst Park in May, yet for much of the title race he felt like a passenger.

One goal over the course of last season was a poor return for a player of his quality, and he would admit that himself.

This campaign looks like a different story and Odegaard’s fifth goal of the season ensured Arsenal would go into the international break top of the Prem.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The midfielder was perhaps so fresh because he came into this off the back of a rest in midweek.

Odegaard was on the bench for Arsenal’s 2-1 win at Slavia Prague in the Champions League, but restored to the team for this as one of six changes.

Arteta reverted to the side that beat Liverpool 1-0 last Sunday, with Ezri Konsa overcoming knee discomfort to start.

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic made just two changes to his side after a 2-2 draw with Ipswich last week.



Lucas Gourna-Douath and Mohamed-Ali Cho came into the XI, with Ryan Giles and Mohamed Belloumi making way.

Jakirovic had been punchy ahead of this trip to London and vowed the Tigers would attack.

The Bosnian said: “You don’t have a chance if you sit back in a 5-4-1. If you are passive, they will destroy you.”

The Hull boss also compared Arsenal to Paris Saint-Germain, though, so it felt debatable whether his side would really go on the attack at the Emirates.



In fairness to the visitors, they came out of the blocks well and finished the first half with six shots on goals.

The Gunners weren’t mauled by the Tigers – as their fans may like to sing – but they were frustrated.

Much of that was their own doing, however, as Arsenal were flat for so much of the opening 45 minutes.

Perhaps it was a hangover from five of their last six games being on the road, but either way it was a tough watch.



Christos Tzolis sent one volley from a Jurrien Timber cross into the middle tier of the Emirates – which just about summed it all up.

The frustration was slowly creeping up inside the Emirates, and Havertz was the focus for much of it.

When Odegaard finally opened up the Hull defence to find the striker in the 40th minute, he tried to cut back inside rather than getting a shot away.

The groans as he was tackled were about the loudest the home fans had been in the first half, until they thought a penalty was going their way.



Havertz was, again, at the centre of the action. The German went down after Hull defender Nobel Mendy pulled his shirt.

Immediately, it brought back memories of Timber grabbing Alexander Isak at Anfield last week.

On that occasion, VAR did not intervene. This time it did, but the decision to give a penalty was scrapped after Havertz was judged to be offside in the build-up.

There was some confusion as to whether the spot-kick should have been given anyway, and it summed up a messy first half.



Arsenal tried to click through the gears after the break and there was an added pace to their play.

Hull continued with their aggressive approach and they were lucky to not go down to 10 men eight minutes into the second half.

Lewie Coyle caught Tzolis late and it could easily have been a second yellow card for the wing-back, who was sensibly subbed minutes later.



Arteta made changes, too, throwing on Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres with under 30 minutes to play.

They were swiftly followed by Eberechi Eze and Piero Hincape, as the Gunners looked for their finishers to bail them out.

But when the breakthrough came, it was thanks to their captain.

Madueke’s snap shot was spilled by Tzolakis and Odegaard reacted fastest to finish the rebound.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Credit to Hull, who did not lie down after going behind.



But there was no way through Arsenal’s solid defence.

Non-league clash postponed as ex-Forest starlet rushed to hospital in warm-up

Truro City's National League South clash at Folkestone Invicta was postponed when City player Yassine En-Neyah suffered a medical emergency in the warm-up

Truro City's trip to Folkestone Invicta was postponed due to a medical emergency for one of the visiting players.

City star Yassine En-Neyah, a Nottingham Forest youth product, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after the episode prior to the National League South clash.

‌



The 26-year-old is said to have collapsed on the pitch before the ambulance drove on to the playing surface in order to take him to hospital.

‌



Both sides released a short statement confirming the postponement, before a further post from Truro confirmed En-Neyah was the player involved and that he was receiving further treatment.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard sends Michael Carrick sack warning ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard sends Michael Carrick sack warning ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash

Michael Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Manchester United's home game against Aston Villa on Sunday and Steven Gerrard has spelled out the consequences of defeat

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard has assessed Michael Carrick's situation (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Steven Gerrard has warned Michael Carrick that he must beat Aston Villa on Sunday or Manchester United's hierarchy will pull the trigger heading into the international break.

‌



‌



Carrick eased the pressure with a 3-2 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night. It snapped a nine-match winless run in all competitions, but Carrick knows he needs to back it up against Villa.

‌



United come into the weekend 17th in the Premier League table, outside of the relegation on goal difference having taken just seven points from their opening nine games. It represents United's worst start to a league campaign in 40 years and has seen club chiefs identify possible replacements.

‌



Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada have sounded out Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte, but have so far opted to stick by Carrick. They have held fire for now, but the looming two-week break is an obvious concern for the United boss if he can't beat Villa.

Sports.title: Leeds beat Spurs to leave Roberto De Zerbi fuming at red card controversy
Sports.content:
Leeds beat Spurs to leave Roberto De Zerbi fuming at red card controversy

LEEDS 1-0 TOTTENHAM: Jayden Bogle was lucky to stay on the pitch as VAR decided his reckless challenge on Mathys Tel was not worth of a red card

View 2 Images Noah Okafor scored the winner for Leeds against Spurs (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

Roberto De Zerbi was left seeing red after Jayden Bogle escaped a card of the same colour in this crushing defeat for Tottenham at Elland Road.

‌



‌



De Zerbi stormed down the tunnel at half time, having seen VAR refuse to deem Bogle's dangerous tackle on Mathys Tel worthy of a sending off.

‌



The challenge, which saw Bogle stand on the Achilles of the Spurs winger and force him to limp out of the game, didn't even result in the Leeds defender getting booked.

‌



And De Zerbi's mood went from bad to worse when substitute Noah Okafor won the game for Leeds in the final 10 minutes, just 97 seconds after going on.

Spurs had arrived in Yorkshire high on confidence following three straight wins. The run had even lifted a team which made a shambolic start to this campaign, into the top half of the table.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And in the process overtaking a Leeds side which had started to struggle, following a bright opening. Daniel Farke's men took on Spurs without a win in their last five league outings.

‌



But the German also knew his side had the longest unbeaten home run in the Premier League. One spanning 23 games and stretching back to March.

And Spurs were fortunate not to find themselves behind inside the opening five minutes. Mateus Fernandes did his best to handle a cross and concede a penalty, before VAR bailed him out, while Ao Tanaka blazed a shot just wide.

‌



Ethan Ampadu then sliced an effort well wide as Spurs continued to hang on. Having weathered the storm, Spurs threatened themselves when a lightening break from Tel down the left resulted in Omar Marmoush shooting straight at James Trafford.

Moments later Mohammed Kudus tested Trafford again, but these were rare moments of quality in a game badly lacking the stuff.

‌



Ten minutes before half time VAR took four minutes to review that challenge by Bogle on Tel. De Zerbi couldn't believe the outcome of the dithering.

Bogle then set up a chance for Lukas Nmecha, who headed straight at Antonin Kinsky from close range. A comical collision between team-mates Ampadu and Tarik Muharemovic kind of summed up the first half.

‌



View 2 Images Tel had to be replaced after the challenge by Bogle (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

Things could only get better. And they did. Ampadu had a shot blocked, while Micky van de Ven almost sliced an interception into his own goal.

‌



Dominic Solanke blocked a header from Dominic Calvert-Lewin close to his own line as Leeds continued to push for a breakthrough. Tempers continued to simmer, and De Zerbi was booked after objecting to a yellow card shown to Pedro Porro.

A break from Calvert-Lewin saw him tee-up Tanaka, who ballooned his effort over the crossbar when he should have scored.

‌



Ampadu then had an effort deflected wide, while substitute Conor Gallagher was a whisker from snatching a winner for Spurs at the opposite end.

But with 10 minutes remaining Okafor burst into the box to beat Kinsky and bring Spurs' recent momentum to a shuddering halt.

View 2 Images Manchester United fans protested against their owners on Tuesday - and will do so again on Sunday (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Manchester United fans are being urged not to spend money inside Old Trafford on Sunday, with another protest being staged against the club's owners.

‌



United host Aston Villa in the Premier League desperate for a result before a potentially decisive two-week international break for Michael Carrick. With United making a dreadful start to the campaign on the pitch, anger at the way the club is run has bubbled up off it once more.

‌



Tuesday brought a much-needed morale-boosting comeback win over Roma, but it also saw fans make their feelings towards the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe clear. Three supporters were arrested for throwing tennis balls onto the pitch in a protest which saw play halted.

‌



The match also saw green and gold balloons released and chants aimed at the Glazers and INEOS chief Ratcliffe sung. Now United fan groups are keen to keep the momentum up for Sunday's game against Villa.

‌



Groups including Reclaim the Stretford End, The 1958, The Red Army, Manchester United Youth Supporters’ Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds have come together to mobilise fans. The 'Reclaim our colours' protests asks fans not to buy booze inside Old Trafford and release balloons when the players come out to warm up pre-match.

Its stated gripes are: the ownership, the club's massive debt, the decision to demolish Old Trafford to build a new 100,000-seater stadium, the "disrespect" shown to fans, the erosion of match-going culture and the general "decline in standards" around United.

‌



Another graphic being circulated on social media calls for fans to leave the stadium in the 21st minute - a nod to the 21 years of Glazer ownership.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch during the Roma game (Image: Oli SCARFF / AFP via Getty Images)

Supporters have been urged to respect the minute's silence before kick-off for Remembrance Sunday. But the 4.30pm kick-off, which will be live on Sky Sports, will be played amid a ferocious atmosphere at Old Trafford.

‌



The match is an extremely important one for United, who go into the weekend sitting 17th in the Premier League table, outside of the relegation zone on goal difference. United are on their worst start to a league campaign since 1986 and have won just one of their nine matches so far.

Despite snapping a nine-match winless streak in mid-week, Carrick remains under huge pressure. Club chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have considered possible replacements for the 45-year-old, with Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte sounded out.

Article continues below

Carrick kept his job in the wake of the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth, but knows defeat on Sunday could spell the end of his time as manager, with the international break giving time for a replacement to be found.

Sports.title: Premier League star breaks his silence after bow and arrow incident and police operation
Sports.content:
Premier League star breaks his silence after bow and arrow incident and police operation

A Premier League player subject to a police operation this week over a very strange incident involving a bow and arrow has now broken his silence on social media

View 2 Images Amar Dedic was questioned by Northumbria Police (Image: Serena Taylor, Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle United player Amar Dedic has compared himself to the Lord of the Rings character Legolas after being quizzed by Northumbria Police for carrying a bow and arrows in public. Officers confiscated the weapon on Wednesday after pulling over a vehicle seven-and-a-half miles northwest of Newcastle upon Tyne in Darras Hall, one of the North East's most exclusive areas.

‌



‌



Two men - one of whom was Dedic, the other being his friend - were reported to the force after being seen near a reservoir in Northumberland with the weapon. Six police vehicles, including armed units, were deployed in response, and the footballer was interviewed after being located in the civil parish of Ponteland.

‌



Newcastle were reportedly not pursuing any disciplinary measures against their player in response. A spokesperson for Northumbria Police said on Wednesday that "enquiries are ongoing".

‌



Another Premier League star robbed DURING match as partner shares 'distressing' statement READ MORE :

Premier League star sparks huge police operation after being spotted with BOW AND ARROW READ MORE :

"Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

"Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use, and there was no threat to the public."

Dedic has since responded in the comments section of a Newcastle Instagram post, in which the club celebrated his latest call-up for Bosnia and Herzegovina. The club's post reads: "Amar Dedic has been named in the Bosnia and Herzegovina squad for their games against Sweden and Romania over the international break. Congrats, @amar_dc!"

‌



View 2 Images Amar Dedic commented on Newcastle United's Instagram post

Responding to the post, Dedic shared a GIF of Legolas, an elf portrayed by Orlando Bloom in The Lord of the Rings film trilogy. The footage depicts the fictional archer with a quiver of arrows slung across their shoulder.

‌



The defender's response has garnered over 20,000 likes and more than 300 replies at the time of reporting. Predictably, many included bow-and-arrow emojis after reports of the incident spread rapidly across social media this week.

Numerous other responses beneath the post are dubbing Dedic the "Bosnian Robin Hood", with one saying the "Sheriff of Nottingham will be relieved". Parallels have also been drawn with Marvel superhero Hawkeye, who wields a bow and arrow.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Dedic has made 10 appearances for Newcastle since arriving from Benfica during the summer transfer window for approximately £30million. The defender penned a five-year deal and had previously collaborated with head coach Matthias Jaissle at Liefering and Red Bull Salzburg in Austria.

‌



At international level, he has earned 31 caps for Bosnia. The full-back featured in three of their four fixtures at this summer's World Cup.

However, he has not played for them since then after re-aggravating a hamstring injury before this season's first international break. Bosnia went unbeaten through their first four Nations League games and are second in League B, Group 4.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard outlines crucial role for Coventry City's 12th man this season
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard outlines crucial role for Coventry City's 12th man this season

Coventry City have made a decent start to life in the Premier League despite Friday night's loss at Everton

View Image Frank Lampard believes Coventry City's fans are key to their Premier League survival

Frank Lampard believes the connection between Coventry City's players and supporters can be a major strength as the Sky Blues navigate life back in the Premier League.

‌



‌



The Coventry boss has praised the club's fanbase for the role they have played in the team's recent successes and insisted their backing has acted like having a 12th man on the pitch.

‌



Having guided Coventry back to the top flight after a 25-year absence, Lampard has seen a special relationship forged between the players and supporters during his time at the club.

‌



"The connection between players and fans is a huge thing," he said. “It's a two-way thing, with the players performing with passion and energy. Once that engages the fans and we have their backing, it can really heighten [the team’s] performance and make [the Coventry Building Society Arena] a very difficult place for opposition teams to come.

"Also, in certain tough moments, when the fans are behind the players, they can lift them and help them find renewed confidence. We've got an incredible fanbase and it's one of the biggest strengths of the football club.

“I'm certainly very appreciative of the support they've given me, and I try to keep working as hard as I can to keep getting it and paying my bit back.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Coventry's return to the Premier League was confirmed following a 1-1 draw away at Blackburn Rovers in April, ending a journey that had lasted a quarter of a century and had seen the club drop to League Two in 2017, before winning three promotions in nine years.

‌



And for Lampard, what Coventry achieved in Lancashire seven months ago carried extra significance because of the struggles the club and its supporters had endured before his arrival.

"I saw the Coventry story from the outside, and it was obviously a difficult story in football,” he continued. “A top-tier club that was going through so many challenges.

‌



"They have a certain robustness and resilience because of what they've been through, which is relatively unique. It's added to the story. It's brought not just a football club, but a city together.

"We really felt that in the celebrations at the end of last season. It shows you the power of football.”

‌



Lampard also acknowledged the bond between players and fans has been strengthened by the genuine commitment to the club shown on the pitch.

"I must give credit to the players too,” he said. “When fans see players who give everything for the club and buy into the connection and what the club is, and show that they're not just passing through and they're actually loving being at Coventry, that starts the connection.”

‌



"It's something that's been very, very good for us over the last two years. It's going to be tested more this season in the Premier League. But that connection can be a real strength of ours that will help us try to succeed in whatever way we can."

Lampard was speaking during filming to promote Coventry Building Society’s Sky Blue Line – a telephone that functions as a direct contact between friends, family and fans to help motivate and support Lampard and his players.

Article continues below

“When you hear personal messages, you realise how far football can reach beyond the pitch,” he added. “It is people's lives. It hits even harder, in a good way. They're a good reminder of why you do the job."

Sports.title: Error-prone Gianluigi Donnarumma could cost Man City with Arsenal boasting rock-solid David Raya
Sports.content:
The more Enzo Maresca protests, the less convincing he sounds.

The Manchester City manager must prefer to answer questions about Gianluigi Donnarumma than the looming question marks over the club's guilty verdict, but only just.

They have been a recurring theme this season - and for good reason. The stats show that Donnarumma has made three errors leading to goals in all competitions this season and there have been plenty of other moments of peril to go with them.

City's giant goalkeeper was beaten at the near post by Ridle Baku's attempted cross due to his poor positioning in their 3-2 win over RB Leipzig on Wednesday. In the 2-1 defeat by Aston Villa 11 days prior, he let Nicolas Jackson's low shot squirm through his grasp.

‌



Sir Alex Ferguson is a painful reminder of Man Utd's glory days 40 years on from his arrival READ MORE :

These are not isolated incidents. In the 1-0 win over Coventry in early September, Donnarumma nearly allowed a routine back-pass from Abdukodir Khusanov over the goalline. He was forced to scramble it off the line in a near-calamitous moment that was the headline of a jittery performance.

And yet Maresca has refused to even entertain the topic as one open to debate. "It's not a concern, but it's a mistake," Maresca said after the Leipzig error. "We recognise that; he knows that it's a mistake, but now it's Nottingham Forest away, we need to be focused on that."

The City boss was echoing his previous comments after the Villa defeat. "Gigio, since we started, is doing well," he insisted. "Like any player or any manager at some point, he is making some mistakes, but it's part of the season.

View 4 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma has struggled at times this season (Image: Maja Hitij/Getty Images)

‌



"They are playing so many games and minutes that sometimes it's impossible not to make some mistakes. He's quite a strong guy. He knows when he makes some mistakes. He doesn't need us to tell him. Sometimes it's so clear, so they recognise that. It's part of the game."

Of course, mistakes are part of the game. But currently they are not a part of David Raya's game: the Arsenal goalkeeper is yet to make an error leading to a goal in the Premier League this season. And in a title race that could be decided by tiny margins, it is a difference worth exploring, even if Maresca doesn't want to.

Donnarumma 'confusing himself'

Former City goalkeeper Joe Hart launched an impassioned defence of Donnarumma on The Overlap Daily, insisting that the Italian was trying to cut out Baku's cross and be a team player when he was beaten by a freak goal. He also pointed out that Donnarumma made a world-class save only he was capable of in the same game.

Yet even the staunch City supporter conceded Donnarumma was "confusing himself" through his positioning and should instead be more focused on preventing "the worst-case scenario", rather than being constantly on the front foot being proactive.

‌



There is another factor that should be laid out in Donnarumma's defence: the age-old truism that a goalkeeper is only as good as his defence. Donnarumma has faced 33 shots on target in the Premier League this season, which is 11 more than Raya.

City, and in particular Marc Guehi, have been error-prone and unusually shaky at the back this season, while Arsenal - with their beefed-up backline thanks to the signing of Ezri Konsa - have been typically resolute. Arsenal therefore have six clean sheets to City's three in the Premier League, having conceded five goals to City's 10.

View 4 Images Marc Guehi has also been at fault for goals this season (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

Square peg in a round hole

Concerns over Donnarumma are nothing new. As soon as City decided to sign him from Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2025, there were question marks over how he'd fit into Pep Guardiola's playing style. The Italy international is renowned as a fantastic shot-stopper, not a ball-playing keeper of the modern era.

‌



Donnarumma only ended up playing one season under Guardiola before Maresca arrived, but those question marks remain. Despite his repeated defending of his goalkeeper and admission that Geronimo Rulli isn't really an option as a replacement, it is something Maresca is aware of.

"I think a few times tonight it's not Gigio's mistake, it's more the wrong decisions to go back to Gigio," he said after the 2-0 win over Porto in September. "Sometimes we go too many times back to Gigio when we don't need."

View 4 Images David Raya has been rock-solid for Arsenal (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/Getty Images)

Former Premier League goalkeeper Brad Friedel believes that while Raya was recruited specifically to fit Mikel Arteta's style, Donnarumma is more of a square peg in a round hole.

‌



"They're completely different goalkeepers, and it's about how you want to play," Friedel told Mirror Football on behalf of Grosvenor Sport. "I mean, Donnarumma stands at six foot five and Raya's barely six foot.

"I would say Raya is probably better on crosses than Donnarumma, believe it or not, because he has great timing and great spring when he comes out for a ball. I think Donnarumma is a huge presence in goal. If you're a striker and you look up, you're probably thinking, where can I strike to score?

"Whereas Raya is a little bit different. He uses his quickness for his saves. So as a striker, you probably think the corner's free, and then before you know it, Raya's hand's there."

‌



Raya has the edge

"They're completely different goalkeepers," Friedel added. "Playing out of the back, I would say Raya has the advantage. Certain shot-stopping areas, probably Donnarumma has a little advantage because of his size.

"But it's really what you want from your goalkeeper, too. With Raya, he fits perfectly in Arteta's style and system, and looks like a character as well, and he has been a huge part of that.

"With Donnarumma, I don't have that many games to go by yet to know if he's the perfect fit for Maresca's style or not. But he's definitely a quality goalkeeper. But I would probably give Raya a little bit of an advantage over him with everything that I just said, as far as fitting in a system."

Arsenal, it seems, have the best of both worlds in Raya. City, however, may need to adapt their playing style to avoid more costly errors from Donnarumma.

‌

Sports.title: Taurus Bay dents some lofty reputations in Rising Stars
Sports.content:
Harry Redknapp could have another top prospect on his hands after Taurus Bay made a winning chasing debut in the Boodles Rising Stars Novices’ Chase at Aintree.

A lot of the pre-race chatter revolved around Paul Nicholls' No Drama This End making his eagerly-awaited fences bow and he was sent off the 8-11 favourite.

However, Ben Pauling's five-year-old was a more than useful hurdler in his own right last term and always seen as more of a chasing prospect.

With No Drama This End's tank flashing empty on the run to the last it was left to Ben Jones on board Taurus Bay to outbattle the match-fit Dan Skelton runner Talk To The Man after the last, edging a one-and-a-quarter-length verdict at odds of 13-2.

With Redknapp and Pauling's King George hero The Jukebox Man currently sidelined with injury, Taurus Bay could very much fill the void in the silks of the former West Ham and Tottenham Hotspur manager as the season progresses, having scooped Grade Two honours at the first attempt over fences.

Pauling said: "He won his two novice hurdles as he liked last season and then ran in the gloom at Cheltenham, when he ran a mighty race.

"That race left its mark, and I didn't think we were going to get to the Festival but I said to Harry and Geoff, let's go for some experience. He wasn't in the form I needed him to be, but I wanted him to get the big occasion and get some experience. He travelled until two out (in the Turners Novices' Hurdle), he then rooted two out and Ben just stood up on him after that.

"We always knew he had the ability but today was a good race. Ben said he just took a blow like all mine do, so he will improve a lot for it.

"I was amazed with his performance today. So far this season, ours have just needed it when they get into a battle against horses who are more prepared than we are.

"This horse hadn't had an away day and is not a big, burly horse so you wouldn't want to do much early doors in the season with him. Today was very much to get him where we wanted him and, hopefully, we can go on from here.

"I was very keen to keep him over two miles, but it was just finding a race that was safe for him to run in. We had no ambitions to come straight for a Grade Two but that's where we've ended up. I do think he's a very quick horse - he's not a fast horse at home but shows lots of speed on the track.

"I don't know whether we will go to two or two and a half miles next. He seems very versatile and we'll play it by ear."

Alexei makes winning return at Aintree

Alexei justified 4-7 favouritism in the William Hill Molyneux Hurdle at Aintree to make both a winning return to action and lay down an early Champion Hurdle marker in the process.

Fourth in the Cheltenham Festival showpiece last season, he arrived on Merseyside ready to confirm he was one of the leading names in Britain this term, with his task in the Grade Two event made easier with the absence of Dan Skelton's Mydaddypaddy, who was withdrawn on Friday.

Joe Tizzard's six-year-old was being ridden for the first time by Harry Cobden who was deputising for the injured Brendan Powell, and he tracked the early pace set by Nicky Henderson's Lucky Place in third place, with Gordon Elliott's Mange Tout closest to the leader in second.

Nudged closer by Cobden entering the straight, Mange Tout was left in front after a mistake two out from Lucky Place but Alexei breezed alongside and as the two main protagonists jumped the last in unison, Cobden soon asked his mount to assert with an instant response.

Alexei was kept up to his work for a four-length success over the Irish raider and saw his odds for the Champion Hurdle shortened to 12-1 from 20s by Paddy Power.

Tizzard said: "That was smashing and a lovely reappearance, you couldn't ask for much more really.

"I thought he was a bit sleepy for the first half of the race but then came alive and got the job done well giving plenty of weight to a good mare.

"He looked to have Gordon's mare covered and I think a better run race will suit us better as he's a good traveller through a race.

"I couldn't have wished for a nicer start and I think he'll improve no end physically for that run and I think it will really sharpen him up."

Alexei will now head to Newcastle at the end of the month for the Fighting Fifth, with the Venn Farm handler charting a path back to the Festival in March for another crack at the opening day feature.

Tizzard added: "We've got three weeks now until the Fighting Fifth and then after that we'll go to the Christmas Hurdle. We're going to treat him as a Champion Hurdle horse.

"He ran well in the race last year and going back there is what we want to do. We've said that throughout the summer and he only needs a little bit of progression and he is right in the mix."

Sports.title: All Blacks power on to leave Scotland well short of history
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - Scotland 21-43 New Zealand: All Blacks power on to leave hosts well short of history at Murrayfield

New Zealand's All Blacks surged past Scotland at Murrayfield in the second half to secure Nations Championship victory

Scotland remain winless against New Zealand in 121 years of contests as the All Blacks proved too strong to record a 43-21 Nations Championship victory at Murrayfield.

The All Blacks scored seven tries in the Scottish capital through No 8 Wallace Sititi, loosehead Ethan de Groot, hooker Codie Taylor, full-back Beauden Barrett (two), wing Josh Moorby and replacement hooker Asafo Aumua, and despite sin-binings to back-rows Peter Lakai and Sititi, demonstrated their lethal ability in attack.

Scotland battled from 10 points behind to narrow to within three by the break after a madcap opening 40 minutes which saw hooker Ewan Ashman score a hat-trick, but New Zealand emerged to dominate the second half.

Scotland 21-43 New Zealand - Score summary Scotland - Tries: Ashman (8,26,38). Cons: Russell (9, 27, 39). New Zealand - Tries: Sititi (4), de Groot (16), Lakai (20), B Barrett (31,51), Moorby (49), Aumua (68). Cons: McKenzie (17,32,52,69).

The net result means Gregor Townsend's side remain searching for a first success over the All Blacks, with Scotland's winless run against New Zealand now at 34 Tests.

Scotland remain without a victory over the All Blacks in their history, and failed to score a point in the second half

The All Blacks paid tribute to long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader pre-match, who passed away suddenly last week

With Scotland caught offside less than three minutes in, New Zealand turned down a potential kick for points in favour of a lineout attack in the 22, and struck for the opening try through a clever set-piece play filled with disguise as Sititi spun and raced over.

Back-row Wallace Sititi scored the opening try in the fourth minute following a clever lineout move

McKenzie poorly missed the conversion and within four minutes, Scotland had their first try: a rolling maul seeing the hosts plunge the majority of their outfield players in, rendering it unstoppable, with Ashman finishing.

Russell converted for an early lead, but the All Blacks replied with two bouts of sustained phase-attack in the Scotland 22: the first seeing Will Jordan held up, but the second bringing a try for De Groot as the prop grounded on the line.

Scotland responded quickly as Ewan Ashman touched down following a rolling maul

McKenzie converted this time for a 12-7 lead, and it was soon extended further when Scotland No 8 Jack Dempsey gave away an extremely costly neck-roll penalty within his own 22 - the All Blacks making him pay with a rapid maul drive off a flat and sharp Taylor lineout delivery - the hooker adding the scoring touch.

McKenzie proved off target again with the conversion to leave the difference a 10-point one, and when the visitors conceded five penalties in quick succession to invite Scottish pressure in their 22, Lakai was sent to the sin-bin and Russell kicked back into the corner.

Incisive Scotland centre Huw Jones - outstanding in the first half - was held up in-goal when a try looked a certainty, but Scotland did notch their second in the 26th minute when Ashman ran a superb line to charge past Sititi to finish.

Ashman charged over for his second as Scotland get fighting back in the first half

Russell tapped over the extras to narrow within three points, but the 14-player All Blacks were next to cross when Barrett sliced through following a trademark slick attack.

Beauden Barrett sliced through for New Zealand's fourth try of the first half

Scotland's response was to make another line-break off a restart, with the All Blacks guilty of yet more penalties and temporarily reduced to 13 with Sititi sin-binned.

Yet, in the home side's only attack facing 13 players, they saw a five-metre lineout maul sacked and the ball forced unplayable in a huge lost opportunity, which was then compounded when the All Blacks won a dominant scrum penalty to clear.

Another Jones break saw New Zealand infringe to present a five-metre lineout chance once more, and this time Scotland got it right two minutes before the break as backs piled into the maul again and Ashman completed his hat-trick.

Ashman (left) completed his hat-trick via a second maul try, bringing Scotland within three points by half-time

Russell's conversion brought Scotland within three again by the half-time break, and an early chance fell their way in the second half on the cusp of the New Zealand 22 with ball in hand, but poor execution saw the ball fall to floor.

Instead, Scotland captain Tuipulotu was caught offside to invite New Zealand onto the attack, pinning the hosts into their 22. When a crooked lineout throw followed, New Zealand turned the screw at the scrum and scored out wide through Moorby.

Josh Moorby scored early in the second half for the All Blacks as they took control

The All Blacks quickly built into the 22 moments later, with Tuipulotu sin-binned for repeat team infringements and Barrett finishing his second in the 51st minute after ruthless New Zealand backline attack vs 14.

McKenzie converted for a substantial 15-point lead, which felt even greater when Scotland passed up their next try chance: wing Kyle Steyn knocking on after Jordan failed to get a hand to a long pass just in front of him.

Barrett's second try saw the All Blacks strike for two tries in two minutes

Russell was subbed off for Scotland just past the hour having struggled to influence things, while breakdown penalties won by Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea sniffed out the home side's next two possessions.

With 12 minutes to play, New Zealand chalked up their seventh try of the Test as Aumua sprinted through untouched past poor Scotland defence.

Replacement Asafo Aumua charged over for New Zealand's seventh and final try

Searching for a fourth try which would at least have brought Scotland a bonus point in defeat, New Zealand's closing defence proved too good, leaving those in blue with a familiar deflating feeling.

'Disappointed' Townsend: Accuracy, indiscipline cost us

Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend said:

"Disappointing. Obviously they are one of the best teams in the world and they converted opportunities.

"Some of our attacking play was excellent in that first half, but we couldn't get the ball in that third quarter.

"Going down to 14 men, it was difficult to wrestle that momentum back, so a disappointing day.

"I thought we had enough play in the first-half to build on and cause some problems, but we didn't do that in the second-half.

"Those two things [accuracy, discipline]. I think if you can hold onto the ball in the modern game, then you can get points and we did that in the first-half, three tries.

"We didn't do that in the second-half and New Zealand had more ball and did well with it."

Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend cut a frustrated figure at full-time, as another chance at history passed his side by

Tuipulotu: Our discipline wasn't good enough

Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu said post-match:

"Disappointed, to be honest. I thought we were playing our rugby in the first-half and, to be honest, we probably left points out there, which was a little bit disappointing.

"We were just nowhere near accurate enough in the second-half. They picked it up on us, we couldn't stick with them. It's really disappointing.

"I don't think our discipline wasn't good enough, and it probably starts with me. I got sent to the bin. 10 minutes with your captain off is not going to be good for any team.

"I take full responsibility for that."

What's next?

For Scotland, they next face Australia in their second Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Murrayfield on Sunday November 15 (3.10pm kick-off).

Scotland's Nations Championship fixtures and results Argentina 38-47 Scotland July 4 South Africa 42-28 Scotland July 11 Fiji 17-33 Scotland July 18 Scotland 21-43 New Zealand November 7 Scotland vs Australia Sunday, November 15 (3.10pm) Scotland vs Japan Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm)

New Zealand travel to face Wales in Cardiff for their next Test, on Saturday November 14 (2.10pm kick-off).

Sports.title: Verstappen fastest in final practice but faces grid penalties with Ferraris
Sports.content:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen was fastest in final practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix but will serve grid penalties along with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

Verstappen pipped new Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli by 0.025s but will start at the back of the grid for a complete power unit change, while Hamilton and Leclerc have 10-grid place penalties for exceeding their internal combustion engine allocation.

Mercedes had already announced on Friday that George Russell will have a five-place penalty for a new internal combustion engine, the second time he has exceeded that part's limit, while the Ferrari drivers are being penalised for the first time, so have a bigger penalty.

It means Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris are favourites for pole position in qualifying later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5pm), live on Sky Sports F1, when rain is expected.

Norris was just 0.106s slower than Antonelli in third and also traded top spot with the Mercedes driver throughout Friday's practice sessions, as McLaren's upgrades in Brazil appear to have made an immediate performance impact.

Russell was fourth quickest and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc had much stronger pace compared to Friday, after making significant changes to his car's setup, and was just 0.274s off the pace.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari is into the garage after engine issues during the third practice session at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix

His team-mate Hamilton was limited to just seven laps due to an engine issue, which Ferrari are in a race to rectify ahead of qualifying.

Hamilton initially complained about engine vibrations, and later, his engine started smoking, which brought his session to an early end.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri has struggled in the second half of the season but has an opportunity to start high up the grid with all of the penalties for his rivals, and he was sixth in final practice.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane says the team wants to 'apply science' to their decision on the 2027 driver line-up

Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson were seventh and eighth while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was ninth, and all three drivers could be fighting for spots on the second row.

Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto continues to have a strong weekend on home soil in 10th while compatriot Rafael Camara was 15th and beat Haas team-mate Oliver Bearman for the first time in a practice session.

Camara is making his F1 debut in Brazil after Haas announced Esteban Ocon will not drive for the team in the remaining races after a dispute week in Mexico.

Haas are yet to announce who will drive in the final rounds in Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest v Manchester City: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
24s ago 13.05 EST 31 mins Haaland has City first effort on target, easy enough for Sels. Maresca will be concerned that has taken more than half an hour. Share Updated at 13.06 EST

5m ago 13.01 EST 27 mins This is more like the Delap we saw at Ipswich. He’s been a nuisance for the City backline and has a deceptive turn of pace. Here he wins a free-kick from Guéhi by getting in front of the defender and drawing the contact. Forest launch it into the box and it’s nervously flicked away by a City defender. Share

8m ago 12.58 EST 24 mins Big chance for Fernández as he gets on the end of an well-angled Guéhi cross from the City left, but the midfielder can’t keep his header down. He should have scored. Share

9m ago 12.56 EST 23 mins Another Forest corner, this one from the left, is only half cleared by City and Murillo has a shot from the edge of the box. It’s tame and Donnarumma gathers easily. Share Updated at 12.57 EST

12m ago 12.53 EST 20 min McAtee should make it 3-0! Another turnover and drive upfield this time the low ball in from left finds the former City man on the edge of the box but his shot high and not very handsome. Share Updated at 12.56 EST

14m ago 12.52 EST Goal! Nottingham Forest 2-0 Manchester City (Delap 18) Wow! That is some goal from Liam Delap. Again Forest turn it over in midfield and the strikes picks it up just inside his own half before driving at the heart of the City defence before rifling it past Donnarumma. No frills, but that was a great finish from a striker lacking in confidence. View image in fullscreen Liam Delap fires in Forest’s second! Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Delap runs to celebrate after beating Donnarumma. Photograph: Maddy Grassy/AP Share Updated at 12.57 EST

17m ago 12.49 EST 15 min Forest turn the ball over in midfield and go early into the right channel to find Delap, who links nicely with Muñoz to win a corner. Donnarumma is not convincing under it, but McAtee’s ball curls over him and out of play. Share Updated at 12.56 EST

18m ago 12.47 EST 14 min There’s a lovely edge to this game thanks to that early goal. Forest have their tails up and biting into tackles, while City are moving the ball around nicely on the slick pitch. Share Updated at 12.56 EST

20m ago 12.46 EST 11 min For all Doku offers going forward, he can be exploited going the other way and in Muñoz Forest have the perfect player to take advantage. Gvardiol will need to be far better than he was for the first goal as he will be given a hefty defensive responsibility. Share Updated at 12.57 EST

24m ago 12.41 EST 8 min Lovely sweeping break from City and Doku really should do better. Cherki slides in Ndiaye who pulls it back to the Belgian, who jinks past one but has his shot blocked by a retreating defender. The corner comes to nothing. Forest were really opened up there. Share Updated at 12.57 EST

26m ago 12.40 EST Goal! Nottingham Forest 1-0 Manchester City (Cunha 6) Gvardiol dithers on the ball and has his pocket picked by Jair Cunha who sees it open up in front of him and keeps going. The defender shows excellent composure to slot home and end more than seven hours of goalless football for Forest at the City Ground. View image in fullscreen Jair Cunha gives Forest an early lead! Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock Share Updated at 12.42 EST

29m ago 12.36 EST 3 min Daniel Muñoz takes the first opportunity to heave a long throw into the box, Forest win the flick on but Donnarumma claims easily. Share Updated at 12.57 EST

31m ago 12.35 EST 2 min A couple of minutes in and Forest have already launched a trio of long bombs forward. That probably signals how they’re going to approach this one. Share Updated at 12.57 EST

37m ago 12.29 EST Before kick-off, we’ll hear The Last Post. Remembrance Sunday is tomorrow. Share

40m ago 12.26 EST Here we go. The teams are emerging from the tunnel. Share

45m ago 12.20 EST How do you lot see this one? Drop me an email via the link at the top of the page. Share

54m ago 12.11 EST Are you ready for some data? The Opta supercomputer has backed City to find their form and return to winning ways after they took all three points in 51.5% of the 10,000 pre-match simulations. Forest are handed a 25.4% chance of causing an upset, while the points were shared in the remaining 23.1% of simulations. Some more Opta stats: in English top-flight history, only Sheffield Wednesday in have ever won their first seven matches and then lost their next three. That happened in 1904-05. For a variety of reasons, City don’t lose consecutive matches very often. They had lost only twice in previous 33 Premier League matches prior to the defeats against Aston Villa and Brighton. Only once in the last 10 years have City been beaten in more consecutive league matches, when they lost four between November and December 2024 as their title defence fell apart. For Forest, the underlying numbers suggest they are performing better than their current league position of 19th suggests. Forest have attempted the second-most shots in the league this season (152), but scored just six goals – the fewest of any team – and have the lowest shot-conversion rate (4%). Share

1h ago 11.50 EST Enzo Maresca’s pre-match press briefing centred on goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma’s form, with the Manchester City manager insisting the Italian will get back to his best with little guidance in his native language. Maresca has continued to back his first choice throughout his troubles and has no plans for in-depth conversations with his fellow Italian. “It’s much easier for me with the language,” said Maresca. “We are [having conversations] but there are players who when they make mistakes, you need conversations with them and there are players that when they make a mistake you just need eye contact to understand that he recognises and he knows. “With Gigio it’s quite easy because every time he has made some mistake or something that was not correct, he recognises immediately. “I spoke with Gigio but sometimes you don’t need to be so deep with some players because they know they have made a mistake and recognise that. Just try to avoid that and move on. Overall he’s good. He’s quite relaxed in terms of he recognises that he has done some mistakes but at the same time he has also made some good saves. “It’s just a matter of balance – try to avoid mistakes and continue to do the right things.” The fixture also marks Elliot Anderson’s first return to the City Ground since his £116m summer move from Forest. Anderson has been in good form and Maresca has been impressed with how the midfielder has settled at the club. Maresca said: “It’s a big game for Elliot but it’s a big game for all of us. He wants to understand, he wants to learn and improve and for a manager it’s a dream because you know that he wants to learn.” Share

1h ago 11.45 EST Michael Butler From this week’s 10 things to look out for this weekend: Will Glasner’s risky words inspire Forest? Oliver Glasner has previous. He led Wolfsburg from mid-table to the Champions League but fell out with the club hierarchy and left in 2021. Glasner next guided Eintracht Frankfurt to Europa League glory but was openly critical of the squad’s imbalance and quality in four separate outbursts and departed in 2023. His time at Crystal Palace was a great success but after accusing the Eagles’ board in January of “abandoning” his team with the sale of Marc Guéhi to Manchester City, the Austrian left this summer for Nottingham Forest, where he became the fifth head coach in less than a year. You can probably guess where this is going. After Saturday’s defeat by Brentford left Forest 19th, Glasner was typically abrasive: “If the players buy in [to my methods], I think we can have a turnaround. And if not, the sixth manager will come in.” We’ll soon find out if Glasner has won the players around with City visiting Nottingham this weekend. If Forest’s woeful form continues, Glasner may either walk or get his marching orders from trigger-happy owner Evangelos Marinakis. Share

1h ago 11.36 EST Andrew Beasley Nottingham Forest’s historic goal drought at home is part of longstanding problem Nottingham Forest and Schalke are yet to score at home in 2026-27. The former are one of only five teams in the history of the English top flight to have failed to score in their first four home league matches. Three of the preceding four also drew a blank in game five, which will be deflating news for Oliver Glasner with Manchester City heading to the City Ground on Saturday looking for a win after consecutive league defeats. Forest’s expected goals total implies they should have scored but a flaw in their data shows a reason why. They also failed to find the net in a Carabao Cup home game with Leeds, meaning they have amassed 70 shots in all competitions without giving the home fans a goal to celebrate. As extreme as this situation has become, Forest scored only two goals more than the lowest home scorers in the Premier League last season (Burnley), drawing a blank on nine occasions. This is a longstanding issue. Sports.title: Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance
Sports.content:
As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull team. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes still to play, there was every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season.

Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping the same crime against Liverpool at Anfield in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. But Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the break, with Arsenal having now matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest.

Yet they were made to work for the points throughout by their newly promoted opponents, who for all their endeavour are without a league win since August. Jakirovic had promised beforehand that his side would go on the front foot. “If you are passive, they will destroy you,” said the Bosnian. He duly selected Mohamed-Ali Cho alongside Oli McBurnie in a bold 5-3-2 formation and it was Hull who made the brighter start as John Egan headed wide from a corner.

View image in fullscreen Martin Ødegaard scores the decisive goal from close range. Photograph: Simon Dael/Shutterstock

After losing to Brighton before the last international break, Arteta was taking no chances and reverted to the side that won at Liverpool last weekend. There was no William Saliba on the bench, with the France defender set to play for the under-21s on Sunday instead as he continues his comeback from a back injury. Yet aside from a set piece when Gabriel Magalhães just failed to connect with Ezri Konsa’s flick-on, the visitors’ low block frustrated Arsenal and they continued to cause problems on the break. Elliot Stroud forced David Raya into a save after Riccardo Calafiori surrendered possession cheaply.

With Bruno Guimarães preferred to Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martín Zubimendi, the lack of a natural No 6 can leave Arsenal vulnerable to counterattacks. Hull’s bench was outraged after Ødegaard brought down Cho just inside the Arsenal half as he threatened to race clear but the referee waved away their protests.

View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz is pulled back by Nobel Mendy but no penalty was awarded. Photograph: Simon Dael/Shutterstock

Declan Rice volleyed wide as Arsenal tried to lift the tempo but Christos Tzolis could only hammer the ball into row Z when it dropped kindly for him in the box. Havertz’s failure to take a shot after being played in by a slide-rule pass from Ødegaard drew groans of frustration. Arsenal thought all their prayers had been answered just before half-time when the referee, Farai Hallam, was sent to the big screen by the VAR. Nobel Mendy was clearly pulling Havertz’s shirt inside the area yet the German was offside so the penalty was not awarded, even though it should have been according to the rules. They state that Havertz must be “attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball” to be penalised and because Mendy’s offence came first, that should have taken precedence.

Quick Guide How do I 

Arsenal’s bench certainly felt hard done by. Arteta’s annoyance levels continued to rise when Havertz could only head straight at Konstantinos Tzolakis on the stroke of half-time. Hull came out for the second half with a similar attitude and Jakirovic picked up a yellow card for protesting against another decision that went against his team. Noni Madueke found space after a flowing Arsenal move but again his effort was straight down the throat of Tzolakis.

Arteta emptied his bench and Eberechi Eze fired over from long range with one of his first touches. The feeling of desperation was growing. But Ødegaard has made a habit of coming to Arsenal’s rescue this season and the captain was quickest to react when Tzolakis spilled Madueke’s shot to finally break Hull’s brave resistance.

Sports.title: Muniz rescues late point for Fulham against Newcastle after Murphy stunner
Sports.content:
Rodrigo Muniz came off the bench to rescue a point for Fulham and deny Matthias Jaissle a welcome victory after a difficult week. Newcastle produced an improved display after a run of four defeats in five games in all competitions but they could not hold out after going 1-0 up thanks to a vicious late strike from Jacob Murphy.

Muniz stretched Fulham’s unbeaten run to four games after scoring his first league goal of the season. Álvaro Arbeloa will be pleased with César Palacios’s role in the goal given that the midfielder was culpable when Murphy scored.

Jaissle, who has faced awkward questions over his tactics and training methods, will look back at William Osula not holding the ball up before Muniz’s equaliser. But it was a forgettable game between two sides who are too close to the bottom three for comfort.

Jaissle made four changes after accusing his players of not following instructions during last Monday’s defeat by Everton. This time the plan was for Newcastle to sit deep, denying Fulham space in behind, and the plan worked moderately well during a poor first half.

Both sides lacked fluency. Arbeloa wants Fulham to play at a brisk pace and dominate possession but they were lethargic at first. Gonzalo García, ineffective against Newcastle’s towering centre-back pairing of Dan Burn and Malick Thiaw, wanted too many touches and although Josh King was as urgent as ever the 19-year-old often found himself dropping into unthreatening areas in an attempt to lose Sean Steur and Nico González in midfield.

Newcastle paid a lot of attention to King. Yet the teenager, who has earned his first England call-up after a fine start to the season, still had his moments before half-time. King tested Lukas Hornicek with a stinging volley from the edge of the area and was later unable to rise high enough to land a free header on target.

Fulham’s frustration grew. Oscar Bobb and García had chances after an early error from Steur but Newcastle were comfortable without the ball. Their problem was more knowing what to do when they had it. Jaissle’s wingers often tucked in, leaving the visitors without enough width, and William Osula and Yoane Wissa were not doing enough to hold the ball up.

Newcastle, predictable without a No 10 to make their 4-2-3-1 system work, did not create much. Harvey Barnes was their most dangerous player and drew two smart saves from Bernd Leno. Newcastle started to assert themselves and were aggrieved to have a goal ruled out in the 33rd minute. Burn did nothing wrong when he swept past Leno from close range but Rob Jones had blown his whistle after spotting Wissa grappling with Timothy Castagne at the far post.

View image in fullscreen Jacob Murphy roars in delight after giving Newcastle the lead. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

While it felt harsh it was explained as a “clear holding offence” by the Premier League’s Match Centre. Newcastle moved on and dominated the second half. Barnes rammed a shot wide from the edge of the area and Wissa drove an effort into the side netting from a tight angle.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fulham brought on Muniz for García but they could not build any momentum. Newcastle’s pressing was more forceful and King going off injured was a big moment.

Palacios came on and was at fault when Newcastle broke the deadlock in the 80th minute. The Spaniard played an aimless pass across his own half and was punished by Murphy, who seized possession before driving forward to cut inside and wallop a brilliant shot past Leno from 25 yards.

It seemed Newcastle were set for a second consecutive away win in the league. Fulham had other ideas. Palacios displayed character after his mistake. The youngster linked with Alex Iwobi and smuggled the ball to Muniz, whose shot looped past Hornicek thanks to a deflection.

Fulham poured forward in search of a winner. Lewis Hall almost snatched the points for Newcastle, only for Leno to deny the left-back. A draw was fair.

Sports.title: Okafor’s Leeds winner adds insult to Tel’s injury for Tottenham as Bogle escapes red
Sports.content:
It is almost one year to the day when the Leeds manager, Daniel Farke, produced the tactical overhaul many observers believe saved his job. That day, Farke abandoned his trusted 4-3-3 when Leeds were 2-0 down at Manchester City and although they lost the game, the 3-5-2 he reverted to was the bedrock for the success that followed.

To suggest Farke was under similar pressure going into this game would be a stretch, but without a win in five Premier League games it was not unreasonable to suggest the Elland Road natives were getting slightly restless. Defeat going into the international break would have firmly extinguished what had been a positive start, with eight points from the first four.

So how fitting that with the stakes high once again, Farke’s tactical flexibility which he appears to have developed over the past 12 months laid the platform for a much-needed win for Leeds. His decision to go back to 3-5-2 heading into this meeting with Tottenham led to a largely stalemate opening 45 minutes, with the hosts cancelling out an in-form opponent.

But what happened at half-time was significant. Just like a year ago, Farke changed shape and breathed new life into his side. He switched first to a 4-2-3-1 and then into a 3-4-3, with a mountain of pressure ultimately producing the goal Leeds’ play deserved, as the substitute Noah Okafor’s late strike proved to be the difference.

It was a moment that clearly meant as much to Farke as it did the Elland Road faithful, the German punching the air in delight as his tactical tweaks paid off, with another substitute Harry Wilson the man to tee up Okafor for the winner. It was a successful afternoon for Leeds, who can look ahead with optimism once again after a tricky period.

“There’s no replacement for this winning feeling,” Farke said after. “All my credit goes to the boys for a terrific performance against an in-form Spurs side. It was important to be tactically spot on against their processes.”

Spurs may look back on this as a frustrating afternoon. They failed to create enough opportunities to trouble a well-organised Leeds side, but they will consider whether a crucial moment as half-time approached could have shifted the momentum firmly their way, with Jayden Bogle perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

View image in fullscreen Noah Okafor slots home the Leeds winner in the 79th minute. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

Bogle caught Mathys Tel on the achilles, with replays showing a nasty contact that left the forward unable to continue. A lengthy video assistant referee stoppage led many to assume Bogle would follow Jean-Philippe Mateta in seeing red against the same opposition, but it was deemed the Leeds wing-back did not commit serious foul play.

In both halves Spurs’ attacking potency let them down and they never really truly tested James Trafford in the Leeds goal as their bid to win four successive Premier League games for the first time in three years came grinding to a halt.

“The second half we didn’t show the same spirit,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “We didn’t show the hunger we need for these types of big games. We have to analyse. Many games like this can be a problem for us.”

There were few clearcut opportunities in the first half, with the Bogle-Tel incident the undoubted talking point. But Farke reverted to a back four after the restart, and it led to a huge spell of Leeds pressure. Both Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ao Tanaka had glorious opportunities, with Spurs struggling to contain Leeds’ new shape.

Quick Guide How do I 

The momentum remained with the hosts as the hour mark arrived, which prompted De Zerbi into a triple substitution to attempt to wrestle back control. The result was almost immediate as Conor Gallagher shot wide while at the other end Sean Longstaff was next to spurn a huge chance for the hosts.

It looked as though it would end goalless but Farke rolled the dice again. His next move was another change of shape with Wilson and Okafor introduced to support Calvert-Lewin. Within two minutes the two substitutes combined and Okafor rifled home past Kinsky to send Elland Road into uproar with a goal – and a result – their second-half performance undeniably merited. Leeds navigated any late drama with minimal fuss.

Sports.title: Manchester City break clear of Chelsea in WSL after Bronze’s freak own goal
Sports.content:
An own goal by defender Lucy Bronze ⁠against Everton cost Chelsea top spot in the Women’s ⁠Super League as ⁠they ​were held to a 1-1 draw at home, allowing Manchester City ⁠to leapfrog them with a 5-0 drubbing of West Ham.

Bronze headed ⁠the ball back across the goal to tee ​up Sandy Baltimore ‌to score ‌from close range in the 28th minute, but ‌five minutes later her attempted clearance rolled into her own net to put Everton level. The visitors held on for a draw as Chelsea dropped points for the ‌first time since the opening day of the season.

Manchester City made the most ​of that slip-up as Bunny Shaw’s superb goalscoring form continued, the Jamaican striker netting a hat-trick as her side cantered to a comprehensive win against West Ham, with Aoba ​Fujino ​and Iman Beney also on target.

The WSL’s top scorer gave City the lead six minutes before the break. City then ran riot after the interval as Shaw grabbed another couple for the match ball while Beney and Fujino scored their first goals of the campaign.

West Ham were happy to sit in and soak up the pressure from their opponents, and Constance Picaud-Inconnu was relieved when she parried Kerstin Casparij’s effort straight back into danger but no one was on hand to tap home. The visitors had the woodwork to thank for not going a goal down when Fujino’s effort hit a post.

It seemed only a matter of time before City made the breakthrough and they did just that five minutes before the break. Hemp stole possession as West Ham tried to play out from the back and the ball was worked to Shaw to finish expertly.

View image in fullscreen Sandy Baltimore opens the scoring for Chelsea against Everton. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

City doubled their advantage eight minutes after the break as Shaw directed Hemp’s cross past Picaud-Inconnu. Fujino hit the crossbar but was not to be denied minutes later to make it 3-0.
