Sports.title: Moses Itauma Wants Hrgovic Revenge, Warren Requires Top-10 Test
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma wants another shot at Filip Hrgovic, but Frank Warren says he must reestablish himself first. The promoter is targeting a top-10 heavyweight for Itauma’s comeback, although the opponent’s style will reveal far more than a ranking number about how effectively that fight prepares him for revenge.

Warren hopes to announce Itauma’s return next week. Hrgovic also has mandatory business to complete against Frank Sanchez, leaving Itauma with a rebuilding job while the title picture plays out.

“Well, that’s what he’d like. He asked for that immediately, and it’d be a big event. There’s no doubt about it,” Warren told BoxNation regarding an Itauma-Hrgovic rematch. “Sold out last time. I’m sure if we put it on again, it was so exciting a fight, it would sell out again. But first of all, he’s got to reestablish himself, and Filip’s got to get rid of his mandatory against Sanchez.”

Asked what level of opponent he wanted for Itauma’s return, Warren answered: “Top 10.”

That sets a high bar on paper, yet it reveals little about the specific technical hurdles Itauma will need to clear. A top-10 ranking covers vastly different tactical challenges. Pairing him with someone like Bakhodir Jalolov would force Itauma to solve height, reach, and distance management against a towering southpaw who dictates range behind a long jab. That offers a valuable puzzle, but it represents a different examination from the physical pressure that broke him down against Hrgovic.

A veteran like Joseph Parker represents the opposite stylistic end. Parker possesses the durability to absorb clean contact, the veteran craft to work on the inside, and the sustained output to test whether Itauma can defend while moving. Backing up in straight lines leaves a fighter vulnerable to being marched into the ropes. An opponent with Parker’s engine would compel Itauma to pivot off the centerline, escape off the back foot, and reset ring position rather than settling into a simple linear retreat.

A useful return bout must also address what happens at the end of his combinations. Against an opponent who fires back through incoming punches, Itauma cannot afford to admire his work with his chin exposed or his guard down. A fighter who punches between exchanges will compel him to roll, tuck his chin, or slip out of range the moment his offense concludes.

Pacing remains just as central to his development. Itauma built his reputation on early knockouts, but burning through his reserves trying to blast out a durable contender carries obvious hazards. A test against someone capable of taking solid contact would force Itauma to establish his jab, vary his punch selection, and bank rounds without exhausting himself in search of a single finish.

Warren does not need to throw him into another firefight to achieve those ends. Another loss would derail the rematch entirely. The trick is finding an opponent who makes Itauma solve the specific stylistic puzzles Hrgovic presented while still offering a clear route to a confidence-building win.

Sanchez could alter that landscape before Itauma gets his second chance. Warren noted that Sanchez previously stepped aside to permit the initial bout and now holds mandatory status. Should Sanchez take the belt, avenging the loss to Hrgovic and pursuing the world title will point in different directions.

Queensberry would then have to weigh whether a grudge match carries enough commercial appeal without the hardware on the line. For Itauma, the immediate priority remains narrower: overcome an opponent who asks enough difficult questions to make a second meeting with Hrgovic truly winnable.

Putting Itauma right back in with Hrgovic after a single confidence builder is a classic promotional trap, and history shows that rush rarely ends well for a young fighter.

At 21, Itauma suffered the exact kind of loss that leaves scar tissue. Being carried out on a stretcher after emptying his entire gas tank through eight rounds reveals a deficit you cannot patch up in one training camp. Hrgovic did not just beat him on points; he broke him physically and mentally by weaponizing his granite chin, size, and steady, chopping output.

Hrgovic’s pre-fight psychological read proved spot on: he openly predicted that Itauma had never faced real adversity, had never felt what happens when his best shots fail to stop a man, and would drown in deep water. Itauma swept early rounds, but by round eight, he had completely redlined trying to force a finish.

Once Hrgovic survived the storm, Itauma had zero tactical fallback. Going back into the ring with a 6’6″ puncher who now knows he can absorb everything Itauma throws and outlast him is handing Hrgovic the psychological blueprint on a silver platter.

One tune-up does not solve that kind of problem. A single soft touch or showcase fight lets a fighter look explosive again, but it teaches him nothing about pacing in rounds nine through twelve, managing energy against someone who refuses to go down, or handling heavy incoming shots when fatigued.

If Warren matches him with a hand-picked opponent who folds inside four rounds, Itauma steps right back into a Hrgovic rematch with the same structural flaws that got him stopped in August.

Itauma needs two or three genuine developmental bouts against durable, grinding heavyweights who make him work every minute of ten or twelve rounds without handing him an early exit. He has plenty of time on his side. Rushing him into an immediate rematch to salvage a narrative risks cutting a potentially elite career short before it even gets off the ground.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Opens Rematch Door, Norman Jr Must Deliver
Sports.content:
Brian Norman Jr. has a long road ahead if he wants a second crack at Devin Haney, and taking out Abel Ramos on December 19 is merely step one. With Haney eyeing massive paydays elsewhere, Norman must string together dominant wins to convince the public that a return bout would play out any differently.

“Handle your business, and you might get what you’re looking for again,” said Bill Haney on social media, aiming the message squarely at Brian Norman Sr.

Norman (29-1, 23 KOs) meets Ramos (29-6-3, 22 KOs) in a 10-round co-feature at Chase Center in San Francisco. Haney headlines against IBF champion Liam Paro, targeting another belt to sit alongside the WBO strap he lifted from Norman last November on DAZN PPV.

Bill left plenty of wiggle room. Even a destructive win over Ramos does not guarantee a return date, especially if Haney handles Paro and targets full unification. Norman likely needs multiple statement victories to build real commercial appeal.

Ramos alone will not create that demand. The real opening is the platform: fighting directly in front of Haney’s crowd and proving that the glaring flaws from the first encounter have been corrected.

Norman looked gun-shy after eating an early flash knockdown he never saw coming. He spent round after round letting Haney flick the jab at will from distance, failing to make the fight ugly or cut the ring. By the time Norman showed genuine urgency in the championship rounds, the scorecards were long gone.

The blueprint for a return requires relentless, disciplined pressure from the opening bell. Norman cannot surrender minutes watching Haney reset behind the jab and dictate the terms of engagement. He has to march inside behind hard combinations, force Haney into sustained defensive shells, and stay alert to incoming counters.

Norman must also solve the clinching problem. Haney repeatedly tied him up inside to stall offensive rhythm before sliding back out to safety. Norman was far too passive in those moments, content to wait for the referee to separate them.

David Haye understood how to make fighters pay for holding. Instead of waiting around, Haye would free an arm and unload rapid, clubbing headshots over the top to force guys to let go. Norman needs that exact type of spite: cracking Haney with fast, cuffing punches around the guard the second he reaches in, continuing to fire until the referee breaks them up.

That approach might not stop the holding completely, but it punishes the tactic. Tying up a fighter who continues to batter the body burns far more stamina than holding someone who politely stands still. Norman has to turn every clinch into an exhausting chore.

Ramos provides a live test for that engine. He dropped Mario Barrios in their spirited draw and handed Tahmir Smalls his first career defeat. Norman bounced back by halting Josh Wagner, but Ramos will force him to stay sharp under fire.

A win over Ramos will not erase questions about how Norman handles the jab and grab. Stringing together stoppages over seasoned contenders is his only route to forcing Haney back into the ring.

The fathers can talk all they want. Norman has to show in the ring that he can make Haney fight instead of coasting.

Sports.title: Canelo Fought Kovalev, So Why Rule Out Beterbiev?
Sports.content:
Sergio Mora argues that Canelo Alvarez is simply too small for Dmitry Bivol or Artur Beterbiev, but that claim collides with Canelo’s track record. Moving up to light heavyweight did not stop Canelo from taking on Sergey Kovalev, so physical scale alone should not close the book on either matchup.

When Chris Mannix asked what should happen if Bivol gets past Callum Smith, Mora chose a third meeting between Bivol and Beterbiev over a Canelo rematch. He dismissed Canelo’s prospects, pointing to edges that reach beyond the 175-pound limit.

“Bivol’s bigger, he has faster feet, and he has one of the best jabs in boxing that gives Canelo issues. And Beterbiev is just way too big, way too strong, and he has smart footwork as well. Not in and out like Bivol, but it’s smart fundamentally. No, both of those guys are too big for him,” Mora told DAZN Boxing.

The technical points Mora raises hold far more substance than simple scale. Canelo climbed to 175 in November 2019, stopping the 36-year-old Kovalev in the eleventh round to capture the WBO belt. That victory remains a cornerstone of his four-division resume, keeping any future venture at light heavyweight open to legitimate discussion.

If Canelo truly cleaned out 168 and sits on a throne where nobody at super middleweight is worthy, then stepping up to fight Artur Beterbiev is the exact test he should take.

The critics who instantly rule out a Beterbiev clash point to size, power, and danger. Yet those same excuses vanish whenever people praise Canelo for jumping straight to light heavyweight in 2019 to take out Sergey Kovalev. If handling the physical jump to 175 was good enough to claim a belt back then, using size as a shield today doesn’t work. Canelo already established that he will willingly step into the ring against a light heavyweight champion when an opportunity presents itself.

The timing makes the matchup entirely fair game. Beterbiev is past 40, carrying the heavy mileage, wear, and physical toll of a brutal, extended career. When Canelo moved up to dethrone Kovalev, he targeted a 36-year-old champion with clear vulnerabilities. Facing a 41-year-old Beterbiev fits the identical blueprint. If Canelo’s supporters argue that Beterbiev’s age is catching up to him, then Canelo has zero excuses to avoid testing those waters.

Ruling the fight out gives Canelo a convenient pass to linger in safe territory. Instead of entertaining another slow, uneventful outing against Terence Crawford or settling for predictable matchups at super middleweight, Canelo ought to prove his greatness where the stakes are genuine. If he were brave enough to hunt Kovalev at 175, ruling out an aging Beterbiev looks less like caution and more like dodging a fight that would truly test his limits.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Calls Haney’s Knockout Talk A Bluff
Sports.content:
Liam Paro expects Devin Haney to abandon his knockout talk once they fight, leaving the Australian needing to create punching opportunities against an opponent he believes will avoid sustained trading.

Paro would welcome Haney standing with him. His preparations, however, must account for the cautious approach he expects rather than the aggressive one Haney has promised.

“I believe Haney is one of the hardest tasks, just his style. He’s not going to be there to engage. But look, he said that he’s looking for a knockout. I guarantee I’ll beat him in a firefight, but I know he’s not going to do that. He’s a good boxer,” said Paro to the Punch Podcast.

The first problem is getting past Haney’s jab without spending rounds following him. As a southpaw, Paro can contest that punch with his lead right hand, tapping or occupying Haney’s left to disrupt his ability to judge distance. That could help Paro bring his rear left into range without having to rush through a clean jab.

There is a cost to reaching for that control. If Paro becomes preoccupied with Haney’s lead hand, he can leave an opening for the straight right. His hand fighting needs to accompany his footwork, giving him a route to attack rather than becoming an exercise Haney can read.

Paro also needs to distinguish pressure from pursuit. Following Haney around the perimeter would allow the American to choose when to stop, punch, and move again. Short diagonal steps across his route would make Haney change direction or surrender space toward the ropes.

The straight left to the body could help there. Paro does not have to reach Haney’s head with every attack to make his movement less comfortable. Targeting the torso gives him a chance to score beneath the jab and draw a defensive reaction that creates his next opening. Overreaching would leave him vulnerable to a counter or a clinch.

What happens after Haney punches could be just as valuable. Paro needs to position himself to answer before Haney has completed his retreat. A short right hook or a straight left may catch an exit, but only if Paro remains balanced enough to throw immediately. Loading up would let the opportunity disappear.

Paro estimates they have shared close to 100 rounds of sparring. That experience could help him recognize when Haney intends to move, hold, or counter. It also means Haney has substantial knowledge of Paro’s approach. Familiarity becomes an advantage only if Paro can disguise what he does next.

His first-round knockout of Brock Jarvis demonstrates the danger when he lands cleanly. It does less to explain how he will manufacture that opening against Haney.

Paro’s clearest route is to make brief encounters productive: interfere with the jab, close space without reaching, and score before Haney gets clear. If he can do that consistently, he can win rounds without needing Haney to accept the firefight he expects him to refuse.

Sports.title: Melikuziev Crushes Sharipov To Keep Munguia Fight On Track
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev cleared his final obstacle before an expected world-title shot, knocking out Karomatullo Sharipov in the second round Friday night at Nikki Beach Resort in Dubai. The WBA mandatory challenger finished his overmatched opponent quickly, keeping his pursuit of super middleweight champion Jaime Munguia on course.

Uzbekistan’s Melikuziev (18-1, 12 KOs) needed less than two rounds to finish Tajikistan’s Sharipov (4-4-1, 3 KOs) in the main event of MUKA Boxing’s “Fury by the Sea” card. The scheduled four-round bout marked Melikuziev’s return after more than eight months out of the ring.

The decisive moment came late in the second round. Melikuziev landed a heavy shot that sent Sharipov flat onto his back, bringing the fight to an end. There was no recovery from the knockdown, and the 30-year-old southpaw had completed the immediate task in front of him.

Melikuziev pressed forward in the available second-round footage, finding opportunities to land clean power punches despite brief clinches and return fire. Sharipov could not keep the more experienced contender from getting into punching range, and the difference in their power became decisive before the round ended.

It was the result Melikuziev needed from a fight with limited competitive upside. Sharipov entered with only four professional victories, making this a substantial drop from the opposition the Uzbek contender must beat to become a world champion. A quick knockout met expectations, although it offered little evidence about how Melikuziev will handle a sustained fight against Munguia.

The practical benefit was ending his inactivity. Melikuziev had not fought since stopping Sena Agbeko in seven rounds in February. With his championship opportunity still awaiting a date, Friday’s appearance gave him another training camp and a short spell under fight conditions without committing him to a lengthy contest.

His title claim was already established. The WBA ranks Melikuziev No. 1 at super middleweight and previously ordered Munguia to defend against him. The organization subsequently permitted Munguia to face Nikita Zon on October 31, with the requirement that the winner face Melikuziev next.

Munguia retained his belt by unanimous decision, but his difficult sixth round against Zon gives the mandatory challenger reason for encouragement. Zon hurt the champion badly before Munguia recovered and took control over the second half. Melikuziev’s power makes those defensive openings a concern for Munguia, even allowing for the considerable difference between Friday’s opponent and a reigning champion.

The Ring reported earlier this week that a deal is in place for Munguia to face Melikuziev, although a date and venue have yet to be determined. Friday’s knockout leaves the challenger available to move toward that fight.

For Melikuziev, the title opportunity would represent the biggest step in a rebuilding run that began after Gabriel Rosado knocked him out in 2021. The 2016 Olympic silver medalist later avenged that defeat on points and has now won 11 consecutive fights.

Sharipov was never likely to provide the examination Munguia will. Melikuziev nevertheless did what a leading contender should against this level of opponent: he ended the fight early. The next question is whether he can produce the same damaging offense against a champion capable of surviving trouble and fighting back.

Sports.title: Johnny Fisher’s Kristian Prenga Target Could Backfire Horribly
Sports.content:
Johnny Fisher is flirting with disaster by targeting Kristian Prenga for his planned late-February return. Two confidence-building wins against Ivan Balaz and Michael Pirotton may have steadied the ship after his May 2025 stoppage loss to Dave Allen, but stepping straight into the pocket with the man who put Anthony Joshua on the canvas twice is a massive leap in lethality.

Fisher openly favors Prenga over former IBF titleholder Charles Martin, drawn primarily to the marquee value of the Albanian’s recent high-profile outing.

“I think Prenga would be a good one because he’s fought recently against Joshua,” Fisher told EverythingBoxing.

While that Joshua link offers undeniable promotional appeal, it also provides every reason for his corner to slam the brakes on. Prenga proved in July that he possesses sudden, fight-altering power by flooring Joshua twice in the opening round before being halted in the second. If Joshua struggled to stay upright under that initial barrage, Fisher’s punch resistance will face immediate trial.

The issue stems directly from how Fisher operates inside the ropes. His trademark front-foot assault demands constant forward momentum, letting his hands go in high-volume bursts. That aggressive approach requires meticulous defensive exits. Every exchange demands a snapped-back high guard, a sharp change of angle, or a clean exit out of range. Fisher cannot afford to linger in the pocket to hunt for an extra punch. Lingering against Prenga is an invitation for disaster.

Prenga’s failure to finish Joshua in the second round exposed his own tactical flaws, notably an apparent reluctance to press his advantage when his opponent needed time to clear the fog. Some attributed that hesitation to early fatigue from emptying the tank, while others saw it as costly indecision. Fisher cannot build an entire game plan on the hope that Prenga lets another hurt man off the hook. Slipping shots, disrupting Prenga’s rhythm, and forcing misses remain far safer than trading bombs in the pocket.

Martin offers an entirely different, perhaps more educational test. Dealing with Martin’s southpaw stance, deceptive reach, and straight left hand would force Fisher to sharpen his footwork and spatial awareness. While Martin still carries punch power, his style tests tactical discipline rather than delivering the raw, explosive trauma Prenga brings to the opening bell.

Fisher deserves praise for targeting a live wire, but Zuffa must weigh whether his defensive adjustments are genuinely ready for this level of fire. Another devastating stoppage loss would undo his rebuilding progress, leaving the promotion with a badly damaged asset whose flaws were exposed by the very first puncher capable of exploiting them.

Ghana News.title: The Pathology in Ghana Politics: Examining institutional governance and the non-aligned citizen
Ghana News.content:
By Kwabena Kyere PMP

To the international community, Ghana’s Fourth Republic is a democratic success story—a peaceful vanguard of stability in West Africa defined by smooth transitions of power. But for those of us observing from the diaspora, the diagnosis is far more troubling. Even writing from Lebanon, Tennessee, the structural fractures of our homeland are impossible to ignore. Our democracy is suffering from a chronic political pathology. It is a systemic disease where the state machinery has been captured by a hyper-partisan duopoly, turning the rights of citizenship into a conditional privilege.

I do not write this as a typical political commentator or an opposition operative. Historically, my values have aligned with the New Patriotic Party (NPP). I have traditionally voted for the elephant, believing in its foundational promises of property-owning democracy, free-market capitalism, and individual liberty. But I am not a politician. I do not carry a party card, I do not attend rallies, and I refuse to engage in blind partisan foot-soldiering. My perspective is shaped by my professional background in construction—built on a foundation in Building Technology from KNUST, a Master’s in Quantity Surveying from the University College of Estate Management (UCEM), and a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

I look at our country not through the lens of political bias, but through the objective metrics of cost, value for money, structural integrity, and project viability. And from a strictly professional standpoint, the way our built environment and national resources are managed is deeply alarming. Independent citizens—who refuse to wear party colours—are facing systematic economic, institutional, and civic marginalisation.

The Post-Independence Genesis

This political illness is historically path-dependent. The fierce, toxic rivalry we see today between the NPP and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) is the modern mutation of the existential rifts that fractured our nation immediately after independence in 1957. The ideological divide between the Danquah-Busia-Dombo tradition and the Nkrumaist camp was not just a debate over policy; it became an all-or-nothing struggle over the identity of the state.

When the First Republic weaponised the Preventive Detention Act (PDA) in 1958 to lock up political opponents without trial, it set a dangerous precedent: state power was not a tool to serve the collective public, but a shield to protect your allies and a sword to destroy your rivals. Decades of military interventions only reinforced this survivalist mindset. By the time the Fourth Republic was established in 1993, our political parties had evolved from policy-oriented civil associations into militarised patronage machines designed to capture the executive branch at all costs.

The Symptoms: From Policy-Driven Governance to Project-Driven Extraction

As a project manager, it is impossible to ignore the pathological symptoms currently draining the wealth of our nation under this duopoly. Chief among these is a fundamental shift in the very purpose of governance: our governments have completely ceased to be run on long-term sustainable policies and are instead run entirely on short-term infrastructure projects.

In an ideal framework, capital projects are born out of holistic national policies designed to solve institutional problems. In Ghana's pathological landscape, this project lifecycle has been completely inverted. Sound policies are abandoned because they require rigorous, transparent planning. Infrastructure projects, on the other hand, are highly visible, easily manipulated, and perfectly structured to feed a predatory economic loop.

This project-driven extraction operates as a criminal, unwritten convention. It is an open secret within the political class—understood, executed, and relied upon by actors across the partisan divide, even as they vehemently deny its existence in public forums.

This unlawful convention serves three destructive functions:

Rewarding the Financiers: Modern election campaigns are obscurely funded multi-million-dollar ventures, which civil society groups estimate cost an astronomical $200 million for a viable presidential run. When a party captures power, they do not look at policy frameworks to fix the country; they look at procurement lines to pay back the informal, wealthy kingmakers who financed their path to power. Enriching Party Insiders: Public contracts are routinely distributed via non-competitive single-sourcing directly to party loyalists. These political actors often possess no technical capacity, machinery, or engineering background. They are handed the contract purely as a partisan token of appreciation. The "10% Brokerage" and Extraction Racket: Because these party insiders cannot execute the work, they simply act as predatory brokers. They turn around and sell the state contract to actual, qualified independent contractors in exchange for a mandatory, upfront 10% commission. To hide this transaction and protect their margins, the original contract values are heavily inflated at the ministry level by at least that same 10%. As a quantity surveyor, it is painful to watch: the taxpayer loses twice—once through the direct extraction of public funds to line partisan pockets, and again through the substandard infrastructure that results from a depleted, compromised project budget.

Monumental Sickness: Case Studies in Housing and Road Sectors

This project-driven extraction loop is not a theoretical concept; it is written into the concrete, unquantified variations, and abandoned iron rods across the country. Both parties have mastered this art, and the history of our housing and road sectors tells the full story.

Look no further than the Kufuor Affordable Housing Project. Initiated with noble intentions under the NPP, it was systematically abandoned when power shifted in 2009. The incoming NDC administration left those structures to rot in the bush, purely out of partisan spite, to ensure the NPP received no retrospective credit. But when the NDC launched its own Saglemi Housing Project, the pathology mutated from spite to hyper-extraction. Millions of dollars were expended on a project that became an incomplete ghost town, plagued by allegations of altered contract specifications and massive financial inflation, rendering it completely useless to the desperate Ghanaian family.

The transportation corridor between our two largest cities is the ultimate testament to this cyclical extraction. Decades ago, the Accra-Kumasi Expansion Project was launched to dualise the highway. Over the years, the project was fragmented into endless, non-competitive bypasses distributed to local party elites, ballooning costs by billions of cedis while leaving the road a treacherous, incomplete death trap. Yet, rather than completing what was started, the government introduced the Accra-Kumasi Expressway—an ambitious megaproject projected to cost billions of dollars. We know that under the current winner-takes-all architecture, a multi-billion-dollar budget serves as the ultimate honeypot for contract inflation and campaign financier repayments.

The Educational Capture: Free SHS, Community Day Schools, and Partisan Sabotage

Nowhere has this project-extraction pathology dealt a heavier blow to Ghana’s future than in the education sector. Education, which should be protected as a sacred public good, has instead been turned into a vector for political point-scoring and capital extraction.

Consider the previous NDC administration's Community Day School Projects (E-Blocks). Marketed as an ambitious policy to expand access, it quickly devolved into a textbook example of project-driven profiteering. Contracts were awarded to political favourites for massive capital outlays, only for dozens of these structures to be left completely abandoned or structurally incomplete when power shifted. Rather than serving students, the physical buildings were treated as extraction vectors for mobilisation fees, leaving a trail of half-built concrete monuments in remote areas where students had no means to commute.

When the NPP assumed power and executed the Free SHS educational transformation, it was a monumental policy shift that undeniably opened secondary education to millions of underprivileged Ghanaian children. However, the sheer volume of enrollment immediately overran our existing infrastructure. To prevent mass exclusions, the government had to implement the temporary double-track system.

Instead of a constructive, policy-focused national dialogue on how to build the required capacity to phase it out, the double-track system was instantly weaponised by the opposition. Driven by the desperate desire to recapture power, opposition leaders flooded the airwaves to bastardise the policy, launching aggressive campaigns promising its immediate cancellation within one year. It was pure political opportunism: promising to yank away a structural shock absorber without having the physical classrooms in place to absorb the children. The health, stability, and psychological well-being of Ghanaian teenage learners were callously gambled with just to win an election.

The Ultimate Eco-Cide: Galamsey as the Ultimate Cartel Exploitation

The pathology expresses itself with equal clarity in the weaponisation and hyper-profiteering of galamsey (illegal small-scale gold mining). Galamsey has long ceased to be a simple story of desperate, unemployed youth scratching the earth for survival. It has been systematically transformed into a highly organised, multibillion-dollar illicit cartel ecosystem fully protected by the NPP-NDC political duopoly.

Investigations confirm that galamsey proceeds serve as a primary liquid engine fueling Ghanaian political campaigns. When in opposition, both parties weaponise the crisis. They demonise the ruling government’s enforcement measures in urban centres while quietly visiting mining enclaves to assure illegal operators that they will be protected once a power shift occurs. When they achieve power, state-led military raids are deployed not to eradicate the illegality, but to clear out independent actors and secure the lucrative mining rents exclusively for the ruling party’s elites and financiers.

While politicians, constituency executives, and foreign criminal networks cash in on billions of dollars in untaxed gold, the ordinary citizen pays the ultimate price with their health and their future:

The Death of Our Waters: Over 60% of Ghana's water bodies—including the Pra, Ankobra, and Offin rivers—have been transformed into thick, mustard-colored channels of toxic sludge. Water treatment plants are shutting down because the turbidity is too severe to filter, forcing the nation toward a terrifying future where we must import drinking water.

Over 60% of Ghana's water bodies—including the Pra, Ankobra, and Offin rivers—have been transformed into thick, mustard-colored channels of toxic sludge. Water treatment plants are shutting down because the turbidity is too severe to filter, forcing the nation toward a terrifying future where we must import drinking water. The Chemical Poisoning of the State: The indiscriminate use of mercury and cyanide in alluvial mining has entered the food chain. It is poisoning our lands, crippling cocoa production, and showing up in high concentrations in local crops. Medical practitioners in mining areas are sounding the alarm over a horrifying spike in severe kidney failures, respiratory illnesses, and congenital deformities in newborns.

The duopoly is literally trading the biological and ecological future of the Ghanaian child for quick liquidity to print campaign posters and buy votes.

The Multidimensional Exclusion of the Non-Aligned Citizen

The ultimate victims of this structural violence are the non-aligned citizens—the growing demographic of Ghanaians who refuse to pledge blind allegiance to party colours. In Ghana’s pathological system, access to the state is mediated entirely by partisan identity.

For the independent citizen, this marginalisation is experienced in three distinct ways:

Economic Starvation: Independent entrepreneurs who refuse to pay kickbacks into party coffers or publicly display loyalty find themselves locked out of public procurement entirely, left to watch less qualified but politically connected entities monopolise the market.

Independent entrepreneurs who refuse to pay kickbacks into party coffers or publicly display loyalty find themselves locked out of public procurement entirely, left to watch less qualified but politically connected entities monopolise the market. The Death of Meritocracy: Our public sector has been heavily compromised by informal "protocol lists"—political rosters that bypass standard Civil Service entry criteria. A brilliant graduate without a political godfather is systematically passed over for a well-connected partisan client, driving a massive brain drain as our best minds leave the country.

Our public sector has been heavily compromised by informal "protocol lists"—political rosters that bypass standard Civil Service entry criteria. A brilliant graduate without a political godfather is systematically passed over for a well-connected partisan client, driving a massive brain drain as our best minds leave the country. Civic Exhaustion: Our public square has been completely saturated by the duopoly. National discourse on critical crises is reduced to a media spectacle of mutual blame. Objective critics are instantly labelled as agents of the opposition, pushing the most rational segments of the population into total apathy.

The Imperative for Structural Surgery

The pathology in Ghana's politics is an integrated, self-sustaining systemic disease. It thrives by consuming public resources, destroying the ecosystem, and marginalising the independent observer. Our current stability is deceptive; a system that systematically poisons its own water, alienates its youth, and starves its independent businesses cannot endure indefinitely. Even as someone who has traditionally supported the NPP's philosophy, I recognise that the current path is unsustainable.

Healing this country requires structural surgery, not moral appeals:

We must structurally curtail the sweeping appointment powers of the Executive to ensure public institutional heads are selected through independent, merit-based processes.

Only by dismantling this neo-patrimonial duopoly can Ghana transition from a nominal electoral democracy to a genuinely inclusive republic where citizenship, not a party card, dictates a person's worth.

Ghana News.title: Michael Baidoo returns from injury to score in Plymouth win over Alvechurch
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian midfielder Michael Baidoo made his injury return for Plymouth Argyle in their heavy win over Alvechurch in the English FA Cup on Saturday.

Baidoo returned with a bang as he scored in his side's 4-0 hammering of the lower-tier side in the cup competition.

The midfielder had been out of action since August, when he came off injured after 30 minutes in the friendly against Bristol City following an injury.

The 27-year-old had missed the last 18 games of his club due to his time on the sidelines.

However, he made a comeback in the FA Cup first-round victory, which sees them advance into the next stage of th competition.

Baidoo was introduced into the game in the 61st minute of the encounter and scored 17 minutes later to make it 3-0 after Will Evans' second half double.

The Ghanaian will be hoping to get more game time following his return from injury.

Ghana News.title: Politician and businessman Kofi Wayo passes on at 71
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian politician and businessman Charles Eric Kofi Wayo, popularly known as Kofi Wayo or ‘Chuck’, has died at the age of 71.

A death announcement circulated on Saturday, November 7, 2026, indicated that he passed away in the early hours of the day at Nyaho Clinic in Accra.

Kofi Wayo, who resided in East Legon, was widely known for his outspoken views on national politics and his criticism of successive governments.

Although he never held high political office, he established himself as a distinctive voice in Ghana's political landscape, attracting public attention through his blunt commentary on governance, corruption and the country's economic direction.

He also ventured into active party politics, founding the United Renaissance Party (URP) after engagements with other political parties.

His unconventional style and willingness to challenge political leaders across the political divide made him a recognisable figure in Ghanaian public discourse.

His death marks the passing of a public figure whose political views and outspoken approach often generated considerable debate.

The family is yet to announce funeral arrangements.

Political background

Kofi Wayo first gained national attention in the early 2000s through his outspoken criticism of the government of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and later became associated with the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP).

He contested the Ayawaso East parliamentary seat on the NPP ticket in the 2000 general elections but lost to the incumbent.

His relationship with the NPP became strained after the party assumed office in 2001, as he frequently criticised the Kufuor administration over governance and economic management. He subsequently broke away from the party, associated with the People's National Convention (PNC) and later established the United Renaissance Party (URP), for which he served as founder and leader.

Mr Wayo also expressed interest in contesting the presidency and was endorsed as the URP's presidential candidate in 2012. Beyond politics, he advocated agricultural development and supported farmers through the distribution of farming tools, including cutlasses.

In 2017, he announced his intention to leave active politics and focus on farming, saying he wanted to support rural farmers.

Ghana News.title: Alfred Woyome files nomination to contest NDC National Vice Chairmanship
Ghana News.content:
Businessman and National Democratic Congress (NDC) member, Alfred Agbesi Woyome, has filed his nomination to contest the position of National Vice Chairperson of the party.

His nomination was submitted by former Deputy National Women’s Organiser of the NDC, Dr Catherine Deynu, who said Mr Woyome’s ambition was to strengthen the party’s organisational structures and build its capacity ahead of future elections.

She said he intended to prioritise the empowerment of party members, particularly at the grassroots and constituency levels, to help sustain the NDC’s electoral fortunes.

According to Dr Deynu, Mr Woyome’s contributions to the party over the years had positioned him to play a greater role in consolidating its structures and improving its organisational capacity.

“Many people can attest to these facts. He has done a lot for the party, and this is the time for him to be at the helm of affairs to ensure that our grassroots members are empowered and that those at the constituency level have their capacity built. He can also help build a strong party that will sustain electoral victories for years to come,” she told Accra-based Citi FM.

Dr Deynu added that Mr Woyome’s vision also included prioritising sustainable job creation as part of efforts to strengthen the party and improve the capacity of its members.

The NDC is scheduled to elect its national executives at its National Delegates Congress on Saturday, December 19, 2026, as part of its reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Ghana News.title: Seven companies shortlisted for Keta Port development – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has announced that seven companies have been shortlisted for the development of the Keta Port in the Volta Region.

The companies were selected from 47 that submitted expressions of interest to partner with the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) as strategic partners for the project.

Addressing the 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival, President Mahama said the shortlisted companies have successfully completed the due diligence stage and will now proceed to the next phase of the process.

He explained that the next stage would involve completing the designs and securing financing to pave the way for construction to begin.

“Due diligence has been conducted, and the list has been shortlisted to seven companies. These seven companies are proceeding to the next stage, which involves completing the designs and arranging the financing for the project to commence,” he said.

The President also disclosed that the administration block for the port, which was started under the previous administration, is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

“Government remains committed to advancing the project on a credible foundation,” he assured.

On other development projects in the Volta Region, President Mahama announced that the Sogakope-Agodome-Keta Water Project, which stalled following Ghana's debt restructuring, is expected to resume.

He said the government signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the contractors in October to facilitate their return to site and the completion of the first phase.

On road infrastructure, President Mahama said the Ho-Denu Road is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed in 2027.

He added that procurement processes are underway for the reconstruction of the road from Central University at Miotso, near Dawhenya, to Aflao.

The government is also working to secure a contractor for the Dabala-Savietula-Keta-Denu Highway.

President Mahama further disclosed that several roads in the Anlo area, including the Abor-Atiavi road, has been captured under the World Bank Feeder Roads Project, with procurement expected to begin soon.

On healthcare, he said discussions have been initiated during his recent visit to Korea for the resumption of financing for the upgrade of the Volta Regional Hospital in Ho.

He said the upgrade would ensure that the facility is befitting of a teaching hospital.

The President also announced progress towards establishing a School of Pharmacy under the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS), saying land had been secured and inspected by the committee overseeing its establishment.

He said the next steps would involve designing the campus and proceeding to procurement.

President Mahama also pledged to support other educational infrastructure requests in the region, including a new dormitory block for Anlo-Afiadenyigba Senior High School, proposed E-Blocks for Shime and Anlo Senior High Schools, and infrastructure improvements at Atiavi Senior High School and Technical School.

He further acknowledged calls for the upgrading of Ohawu Agricultural College into a university. On housing, the President said an additional GH¢500 million has been allocated for district housing projects and assured the people of Anlo that the area would benefit.

He also said the Anloga 24-hour market project is on track, while preparations for the proposed Aflao Ashigame market have advanced, with land secured and designs completed.

According to him, a technical team from China, financed through a grant from the Chinese Government, is expected to visit the project sites to confirm the designs before the release of a US$30 million grant to commence the project.

President Mahama urged the Volta Regional Coordinating Council to closely monitor the implementation of the various projects to ensure their timely delivery.

Ghana News.title: Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II outdoored as Dorimon chief after four-year dispute
Ghana News.content:
Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II has been outdoored as the new chief of Dorimon in the Wa West District of the Upper West Region.

He was first enskinned on June 3, 2022, but was not outdoored following a protracted dispute, which was later settled in his favour by the Upper West Regional House of Chiefs and the National House of Chiefs.

Thursday's colourful ceremony was unique and grand, with the new chief being outdoored in accordance with the customs and traditional rites of the area. These included jumping over a cow in the presence of chiefs, Imams, queen mothers, security personnel and residents.

The Imams, who served as his spiritual godfathers, accompanied him as he walked around the cow while reciting verses from the Holy Quran before he leaped over it.

The ceremony was followed by a durbar attended by delegations from Dagbon, Mamprugu, Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire.

In his acceptance speech, Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II thanked the people of Dorimon for the honour and appealed to the government to address the numerous challenges facing the area.

He said children and generations yet unborn wanted a community united around a common vision.

The Member of Parliament for Wa West, retired Superintendent Peter Lanchene Toobu, spoke about roads, culture and peace.

He said the roads linking Wa to Dorimon, Dorimon to Wechiau, and Wechiau to Ga had received the attention of the President.

Mr Toobu said that during the President's visit to Wa West, he instructed the Minister for Roads and Highways to ensure that the road was constructed.

"Three days ago, I met the Minister for Roads and Highways in Parliament and I asked him what is happening to our road and he said go and tell your chiefs that His Excellency has instructed me to make sure that road is done and I'm making sure that that road is constructed," he said.

He said development was coming and that all that was needed was cooperation and collaboration.

A message from the Speaker of Parliament was read by his Principal Marshal, Wing Commander Frederick Bawa.

The Speaker urged the new chief to create space for dissent and embrace all those whose perspectives might differ from his.

A 60-member delegation from Dagbon, led by the Dalunlanaa, Tafah Mahamudu III, attended the ceremony on behalf of the Kampakuya-Naa, Yakubu Abukari II.

The Dalunlanaa said the people of Dagbon stood side by side with Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II.

A statement from the Mamprugu Kingdom said the new chief was one of their own, sharing a common lineage, tradition, culture and destiny.

It said his forefathers migrated from Mamprugu, settled for some time in Dagbon and eventually moved to Dorimon.

Delegations from Gbonaa and Goua in Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire also attended the ceremony.

The leader of the delegation from Burkina Faso, Chief Canton de Gaoua, Albert Bifaate II, urged the Presidents of Ghana and Burkina Faso to construct a bridge over the Black Volta.

He said the bridge would ensure the easy movement of goods and services and boost trade and commerce between the two countries.

Ghana News.title: Lawra Municipal Assembly outlines 2027 development priorities, commits to education and security
Ghana News.content:
The Lawra Municipal Assembly has held its third ordinary meeting, bringing together key stakeholders to assess the municipality's progress and outline its development priorities for 2027.

Led by the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Cecilia Soyele Nuratu, and the Member of Parliament (MP) for Lawra, Bede Anwataazumo Ziedeng, the meeting highlighted a shared commitment to increased investment in education, improved security and agricultural interventions.

Education remains a core priority

Education featured prominently as the two municipal leaders outlined extensive support for students in the area.

Mr Ziedeng said his office had disbursed more than GH¢785,000 in partial scholarships to support over 660 tertiary students since he began his first term.

He added that the individual tertiary scholarship grants had been increased from GH¢1,000 to GH¢2,000 between January 2025 and October 2026, benefiting more than 165 students.

At the basic and secondary levels, the MP said he funded mock examinations for Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) candidates at a cost of GH¢84,000 in 2026. He also spent GH¢11,172 on feeding students of Brifoh Senior High School during their examinations.

Complementing these efforts, the MCE announced that the Assembly had procured and was distributing essential school furniture.

The items include 260 mono desks, 250 dual desks and 100 tables with chairs, aimed at improving the teaching and learning environment across the municipality.

Financial commitments and infrastructure updates

On the financial well-being of the Assembly's workforce, Madam Nuratu confirmed receipt of GH¢294,840, which has been earmarked to clear outstanding arrears and cover two quarters' allowances for Assembly members.

The Assembly also presented its 2027 composite budget, fee-fixing resolution and annual action plan for consideration to guide development in the municipality.

On infrastructure, the MCE provided an update on the 24-hour economy market project.

While acknowledging delays by the contractor, she said the Ministry of Local Government was reviewing the contract to ensure the project's successful completion.

Agricultural interventions and social protection

Agriculture, a major contributor to Lawra's local economy, recorded encouraging results despite some weather-related setbacks.

Farmers reported positive harvests, although late rains affected some crops, particularly groundnuts.

To support local livelihoods, the government introduced interventions, including the distribution of free fertiliser, drip irrigation equipment and 10,000 chicks to farmers.

However, the MCE expressed concern about the high mortality rate among the poultry distributed to beneficiaries.

In the area of social protection, the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme continues to extend support to vulnerable residents.

The Assembly is processing payments and onboarding approximately 4,700 beneficiaries in the municipality.

Health and security surveillance

Although Lawra remains generally peaceful, the MCE raised concerns about recent security incidents, particularly two robbery cases reported along the Nandom road.

She said the police had arrested two suspects and recovered a weapon, while efforts were ongoing to track down the main suspect, who remains at large.

Security agencies are expected to intensify day and night patrols to maintain law and order during the upcoming festive season and the funeral rites of the late Paramount Chief of Lawra.

Health officials have also stepped up surveillance following reports of yellow fever outbreaks in neighbouring districts.

The management of the municipal hospital has urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report symptoms of acute fever or jaundice to the nearest health facility to help prevent an outbreak in the municipality.

As Assembly members deliberated on the 2027 budget, the meeting highlighted the need for continued collaboration among local government officials and stakeholders to address infrastructure challenges, improve education and healthcare, support livelihoods and strengthen security across the municipality.

Ghana News.title: WPL 2026/27: Hasaacas Ladies come from behind to beat Epiphany Warriors
Ghana News.content:
Hasaacas Ladies continued their impressive start to the 2026/27 GoldFields Women's Premier League following their victory over Epiphany Warriors.

Hasaacas came from a goal down to claim all three points at the Madina Astro Turf, securing a 2-1 victory over the Katamanso-based side.

Epiphany came into the fixture looking for their first win of the season after picking up two draws in their opening two games in league.

Hasaacas, on the other hand, are breaming with confidence following back-to-back wins over Army Ladies and Jonina Ladies in the first two games of the campaign.

Making her first appearance following her involvement in the 2026 U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, Jessica Appiah Asamoah opened the scoring for Epiphany after just two minutes. The winger burst forward on the right flank, setting up a one-on-one situation with Grace Banwaa before putting the ball past the goalkeeper.

Epiphany took control of the game and continued possession but failed to add to their lead.

Seventeen minutes after taking the lead, the home side conceded a penalty which was converted by Belinda Kpoglo to draw the Hasmal Ladies level.

Hasaacas grew into the game and for a brief moment had the upper hand over Epiphany and was rewarded for it when Comfort Owusu was fouled in the opposition's box.

Kpoglo stepped up once again to hand the Takoradi-based side the lead in the 31st minute.

Despite their spirited attempts, Epiphany were unable to get back on level terms and were handed their first defeat of the season.

The victory means Hasaacas have won all of their three games this season, staying on level terms with Police Ladies, who also came from a goal down to beat newly promoted Roots Sistaz.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Guatemalan lawmaker and three police officers killed in armed attack
World.content:
It happened in a region of the country known to have drug trafficking activity.

Share Guatemalan lawmaker and three police officers killed in armed attack on social media

A Guatemalan lawmaker and three police officers have been killed in an armed attack, according to the country’s authorities.

The attack on Friday targeted Congressman Julio Portillo, who was in the town of Rio Hondo, in the eastern Zacapa department, which is known for drug trafficking activity.

Portillo was initially taken to a hospital with serious injuries. His death was ‌later confirmed by the National Unity of Hope party, or UNE, to which he belonged.

“President Luis Contreras, members of the Board of Directors and lawmakers mourn the tragic passing of Congressman Julio Cesar Portillo Paz, representative of the Zacapa district,” Guatemala’s Congress posted late Friday on X.

President Bernardo Arevalo said the three National Civil Police officers killed in the attack had died in the line of duty and instructed security forces to ⁠cooperate with prosecutors investigating the killings.

Authorities have not disclosed a motive for the attack or identified ⁠who was responsible.

The Lorenzana family cartel, which has links to Mexico’s Sinaloa cartel, controls the drug trade in Zacapa.

Portillo won his seat in 2023 for the opposition party Cabal, but has since switched to the National Unity of Hope party led by former First Lady Sandra Torres.

She is expected to run for president in Guatemala’s elections next year.

The killings come ⁠about three weeks after former anticorruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa was shot dead in Guatemala City, a case that ‌heightened concerns about organised crime’s influence and the possible return of politically motivated assassinations.



Authorities have not established ‌a ‌connection between the two attacks.
