World.title: Iran’s IRGC says building underground sites for weapons production, storage
World.content:
IRGC says underground military complexes allow missile production to continue even under heavy bombardment.

Iran is building underground military complexes able to sustain weapons production and storage even under heavy bombardment, according to the country’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC).

IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi made a series of announcements on Saturday about the military’s capabilities during a news conference in Tehran, Iranian media reported.

Among the achievements listed were an “underground missile city” set to be unveiled, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported.

Mohebbi said the IRGC had rapidly transferred its missile and drone production lines from the surface to underground facilities. This allows Iran to continue producing missiles while its adversaries assumed its stockpiles were dwindling, he explained.

The spokesperson also outlined advances in stealth technology. He maintained that such improvements had allowed Iran’s missiles and drones to pierce air defence systems and accurately strike targets during previous rounds of fighting with the United States and Israel.

“Today, every weapon used by the IRGC Aerospace Force is manufactured using homegrown knowledge and expertise. Moreover, our products are not even derived from reverse-engineering captured enemy war material,” Iran’s IRNA news agency quoted Mohebbi as saying.

A recent report by US newspaper, The Wall Street Journal, shows that Iran caused billions of dollars in damage to US bases throughout the Middle East during previous rounds of fighting.

Meanwhile, a separate report by the Reuters news agency found that Iran had successfully targeted Gulf infrastructure on at least 135 occasions during the same period, causing billions of dollars in damage and lost revenues.



Mohebbi also warned on Saturday that restrictions on the range of Iranian missiles had been lifted. The warning follows a statement from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who said that there would be “no geographical limits” to Iran’s response if it were attacked again by the US and Israel.

The US-Israeli war on Iran was launched on February 28, prompting Tehran to close the Strait of Hormuz and triggering a global energy crisis. Mediation efforts have stepped up recently, as regional countries hope to bring the war to an end.

On Friday, President Donald Trump said the US military launched limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island, while also claiming Washington had made “a lot of progress” in talks with Iran.

Tehran has repeatedly warned that it will target Gulf energy infrastructure if the fighting resumes. Such attacks would likely push energy prices even higher.

Meanwhile, Washington has also imposed additional sanctions on Iran as it seeks to force Tehran to concede to its demands. The restrictions have further strained the country’s economy, forcing Iran to adopt new trade routes.

On Saturday, US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced it was establishing a new task force that will support ongoing US efforts to prevent Iran from using land routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials.

The US has also imposed a naval blockade on Iran to prevent it from exporting oil.

World.title: What we know about Krakow mass shooting so far
World.content:
The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city.

Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car".

Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard.

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker.

The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested.

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times.

The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself.

City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.

World.title: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
World.content:
There was no clear winner following New Zealand's election on Saturday, as the leaders of its two major parties preparing for negotiations to form a coalition government.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right National Party won 42 seats but was 19 short of the simple majority needed to form a government, despite being the largest party, preliminary results show.

Combined with their coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, they would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc if a deal could be reached.

But opposition leader Chris Hipkins, whose Labour Party won 36 seats, showed no signs of conceding, saying the "shape of the next government" will remain uncertain "for a while".

The tight result followed a campaign shaped by the cost of living and unemployment.

Projections show the National Party on 42 seats and Labour on 36. The Greens are on 16, with ACT on 13, New Zealand First on 12, the Opportunity Party on 7 and Te PÄti MÄori, which represents MÄori interests, on 5.

World.title: Houthis say at least 25 killed in Saudi air strike
World.content:
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say that at least 25 people, including women and children, have been killed in airstrikes by Saudi Arabia.

There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.

The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.

The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.

Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia.

The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.

A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plan landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.

Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.

The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.

The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.

Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.

A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

World.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
World.content:
The EU's former Brexit negotiator has warned that the UK cannot "cherry pick" which elements of the single market to which it subscribes, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to explore closer economic ties with Europe.

The prime minister has said rejoining the bloc's internal market was among options he could pursue as part of a reshaping of ties since the UK's exit from the EU nearly six years ago.

But Michel Barnier told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that EU members would insist on the UK readopting certain conditions, such as the free movement of people, to gain access.

He said there was not a "single market Ã la carte" menu from which the UK could pick and choose what elements it wanted to adopt.

Barnier - who led the EU delegation during Brexit talks between 2016 and 2021, and had a three-month spell as French prime minister in 2024 - said the "door is open" within Europe to the UK rejoining as an EU member.

But he insisted that any move to rejoin the single market - which allows for goods to be freely traded without border controls - would require the UK to follow the same terms as other members.

He added that this included compliance with regulations designed to promote the circulation of goods, services, capital and people, referred to collectively within EU institutions as the "four freedoms".

"There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market."

Since becoming prime minister in July, Burnham has suggested he could commit Labour to pursuing a much closer future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member, though he has ruled out major changes before the next election.

His predecessors have struck a series of deals with the EU on different aspects of how the UK and EU interact post-Brexit.

Both sides are hoping to use a meeting in Brussels in 10 days' time to unveil deals on food standards, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.

World.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
World.content:
In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress.

On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job.

One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests.

"Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it."

World.title: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
World.content:
Paraguay's President Santiago PeÃ±a has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

PeÃ±a was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.

He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached PeÃ±a and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.

PeÃ±a, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.

The impeachment charges that led to PeÃ±a's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

He is due to be questioned on Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester said.

PeÃ±a's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal.

"Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028.

The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.

Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday.

An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, AsunciÃ³n.

Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money.

Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.

PeÃ±a's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.

"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," PeÃ±a said in a video posted on X announcing his resignation, adding his priority was "the peace of mind of Paraguayans who entrusted their savings to our financial system".

Afterwards, senate president Basilio NÃºÃ±ez said PeÃ±a was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".

World.title: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.

The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.

The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.

The tour will cover Argentina and a much anticipated return to Peru, which the Vatican described as a "homecoming" as the Pope was based there for many years as a missionary, then a bishop.

"I must confess that, from the very first day, I never had any doubts; I was convinced that this journey had to go forward," the Pope told journalists on his plane to Uruguay.

"Thanks to the marvellous medical staff... I believe I am in quite good health," Pope Leo confirmed.

Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.

On Friday, he arrived in Monetevideo to a seafront lined with crowds shouting his name as his Popemobile passed.

In his first speech of the trip, the Pope said universal healthcare should be "accessible to everyone".

He told the crowd in Plaza Independencia the care he received made him think of the "many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment.

He capped his day with a prayer at the Montevideo Cathedral.

Pope Leo will cover more than 20,000 miles on his sixth international tour.

On Sunday he will travel to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor Pope Francis who did not return during his own papacy.

The Pope said his visit was about being near the people who were looking to the Church for a message of "hope".

World.title: Italian foreign minister says hackers leaked his personal data
World.content:
Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says he has been targeted by "cyber-criminals" who published his personal data online because of his country's support for Ukraine.

"For days now, cyber-criminals have been publishing my personal data on the dark web and seeking further information, effectively exposing me to new threats and intimidation," Tajani wrote on X.

He did not specify the nature of the threats, but said the hackers were also targeting his family.

The dark web is a hidden part of the internet that is not indexed by common search engines and can only be accessed with specialist software.

"Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted," Tajani said.

"Defending the freedom of a sovereign state, taking a clear stand in support of a nation's democracy and independence, is dangerous in the eyes of these criminal entities."

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed the incident on pro-Russian hackers and offered Tajani her "full solidarity".

"The sale of confidential information about institutional representatives is a cause of serious concern and must be tackled with the utmost determination," she said in a statement.

Moscow has not publicly responded to the allegations.

Meloni also expressed concern about "circulation of false images" which she said were shared by members of Italy's opposition. She did not give details about the content of the images.

The Italian government has provided humanitarian and military support to Ukraine in its war against Russia.

Tajani, who is also the deputy prime minister, said the government was taking the threats seriously.

World.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo becomes largest in country’s history – WHO
World.content:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is experiencing the largest Ebola outbreak in its history, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO).

The country has recorded 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths as of 3 November 2026.

The outbreak has spread across 67 health zones in eight provinces, with active transmission continuing in 51 health zones as of 3 November 2026.

The WHO disclosed this in its Disease Outbreak News report published on 6 November, adding that the country has also recorded 2,881 recoveries.

According to the report, 964 additional confirmed cases, including 511 deaths, had been reported since WHO’s previous outbreak update of 23 October.

Five countries affected

Since the outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, was declared on 15 May 2026, five countries have reported cases: DRC, France, Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

However, the outbreaks in France and Uganda have been brought under control since August, while Kenya and Nigeria continue their response efforts.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The latest WHO report said no new cases had been reported in Kenya or Nigeria since its previous update of 23 October.

Describing the scale of the outbreak in the DRC, WHO said it had become “the largest Ebola disease outbreak ever recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo irrespective of virus species.”

Community deaths raise concern

The WHO expressed concern over the high number of deaths occurring outside treatment centres, particularly among young children, highlighting the difficulties in identifying cases early and ensuring patients receive timely medical care.

Of the 512 deaths reported in the DRC since 21 October, 335 occurred in communities, while 177 were recorded in treatment centres.

“The high proportion of deaths occurring in communities, especially among young children, continues to highlight challenges in early case detection and timely access to appropriate care,” WHO said.

WHO noted that the outbreak remains concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu provinces, which account for most confirmed cases and deaths.

Ituri has recorded 7,485 cases and 3,532 deaths, while North Kivu has reported 2,593 cases and 1,422 deaths.

The WHO said 1,463 new confirmed cases were recorded across the DRC in the 21 days leading up to 3 November, with Ituri and North Kivu accounting for most of the infections.

Nigeria’s Ebola response

In Nigeria, the WHO reported one laboratory-confirmed imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on 20 October.

The patient was medically evacuated to Switzerland on 26 October and remains in isolation while receiving medical care in Geneva.

As of 3 November, WHO noted that 62 contacts had been identified in Nigeria, with six completing the mandatory 21-day follow-up period.

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), in its situation report published on 4 November, also confirmed that six contacts had completed their follow-up, while 56 remained under monitoring.

The agency reported no newly identified contacts or symptomatic contacts during the preceding 24 hours.

The WHO said Nigerian authorities, with support from the organisation and other partners, had intensified contact tracing, case investigations and infection prevention measures.

ALSO READ: WHO recommends two new Ebola vaccines for clinical trials as DRC battles Bundibugyo outbreak

Investigations are also ongoing to establish the likely source of the infection and reconstruct the patient’s travel and exposure history.

What is Bundibugyo virus disease?

Bundibugyo virus disease is a severe form of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus, one of the viruses in the Orthoebolavirus genus.

According to the WHO, it is a zoonotic disease, meaning it can spread from animals to humans. Fruit bats are suspected to be its natural reservoir.

Initial human infections are thought to occur through contact with the blood or secretions of infected wildlife, including bats and non-human primates.

The virus subsequently spreads between people through direct contact with the blood, secretions, organs and other bodily fluids of infected individuals. It can also spread through contaminated surfaces and materials.

The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, and infected people are not infectious before symptoms appear. Early symptoms include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat. These may progress to vomiting, diarrhoea, organ dysfunction and, in some cases, bleeding.

The WHO noted that early symptoms can resemble other illnesses, including malaria, so laboratory testing is important to confirm the diagnosis.

No vaccines or specific treatments are currently approved for Bundibugyo virus disease. The WHO said controlling the outbreak depends on early identification and isolation of cases, medical care, contact tracing, safe burial practices and community engagement.

World.title: FG scraps NTI’s university affiliations nationwide
World.content:
The Federal Ministry of Education has cancelled all 2026 admissions into the National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, over breaches of mission and accreditation requirements.

In a statement, the ministry’s spokesperson, Boriowo Folasade, also directed the institution to stop all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements.

The ministry explained that the NTI will no longer process any admissions into full-time, part-time or Distance Learning Studies (DLS) for NCE or Bachelor’s degree programmes.

It also advised the public not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes.

“All admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees,” the statement reads in part.

“The Ministry emphasises that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted.”

The violations

According to the ministry, the decision followed violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued to the institute in September 2025.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It said NCE admissions must meet the requirements of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and the accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).

The ministry said the National Universities Commission (NUC) will inform the affected universities and ensure they comply with the order ending NTI’s degree-awarding arrangements.

To protect students already in the system, the ministry said the NCCE will fully accredit existing NCE II to IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones.

It said eligible students may finish their programmes, depending on the accreditation results and regulatory requirements.

NTI’s mandate

The ministry said NTI’s legal mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development.

“This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-Education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations,” it said.

The ministry urged the public to check a programme’s accreditation and admission status with the relevant regulators and official government channels before enrolling or paying.

It added that the intervention is meant to protect students, uphold academic standards and stop prospective applicants from being exposed to unapproved programmes.

World.title: Imo criticises NJC’s directive to shortlist acting chief judge for substantive appointment
World.content:
The Imo State Government has rejected the directive of the National Judicial Council (NJC) to include the state’s acting chief judge, Ijeoma Agugua, on its shortlist for substantive chief judge appointment.

Punch newspaper reported that the state’s Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Paul Obinatu, criticised the NJC’s directive in a statement on Friday.

Mr Obinatu’s remarks, which pass as the state government’s stance on the matter, questioned what it described as NJC’s interference in the chief judge appointment process.

While Mr Obinatu acknowledged the NJC’s constitutional authority to review the state’s list of suitable candidates, he maintained that the council cannot “dictate, control or substitute its preferred candidate.”

The state government’s response to the NJC may be a signal for another stalemate which previously left the state’s judiciary practically without a leader for months.

Without the state government and the NJC agreeing on nominees’ list, it is impossible to renew the appointment of the acting chief judge and ultimately appoint a substantive chief judge for the state.

The NJC, at its latest meeting held on 3 November, ordered the Imo State Judicial Service Commission, the body with statutory authority to initiate the process of appointing judicial officers in the state, to include Ms Agugua on its shortlist for the substantive chief judge of the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

​Ms Agugua, whom Governor Hope Uzodimma reluctantly inaugurated as Imo State’s acting chief Judge following NJC’s intervention earlier this year, was excluded from the list of candidates the state’s judicial service committee submitted for full-fledged appointment as the chief judge.

​The NJC rejected Ms Agugua’s exclusion from the shortlist, insisting that skipping her name despite her being the most senior High Court judge in the state, was a violation of the appointment by seniority principle prescribed by the Nigerian constitution.

Imo’s objection to NJC’s directive

But Mr Obinatu argued that the NJC cannot dictate the names to be shortlisted for the role.

“The NJC’s constitutional responsibility to recommend a candidate to the governor does not confer on it the additional power to determine or dictate the candidate the State Judicial Service Commission must submit to it,” the attorney general said.

​He cited Section 202 of the Nigerian constitution, stating that the judicial service committee constitutionally shielded from external interference.

​“The State Judicial Service Commission shall not be subject to the direction or control of any other authority or person in exercising its constitutionally assigned powers.

​“This provision establishes a clear constitutional safeguard against external interference in the commission’s responsibilities and cannot be overridden by the NJC through administrative directives or procedural guidelines,” he insisted.

​Mr Obinatu stressed that the NJC should not use its national status to interfere with the commission.

​“The NJC cannot invoke its national institutional status or its recommendation powers to exercise control over the Imo State JSC in a manner inconsistent with the Constitution,” he stated.

​Mr Obinatu advised the NJC to maintain institutional boundaries within the confines of the law.

​“The issue is not a contest for institutional superiority between the NJC and the State JSC, but the need for each institution to respect the constitutional boundaries of its authority,” he said.

​Persistent crisis

The attempt to fill the Imo chief judge position has been a major bone of contention between the NJC and Imo State authorities since former Chief Judge T. E. Chukwuemeka Chikeka was compulsorily retired over age falsification two years ago, in November 2024.

The NJC’s latest decision on the matter signalled the state government’s persistent disapproval of Ms Agugua for the position.

​Despite Ms Agugua being the most senior Imo State High Court judge, the state authorities passed over her to pick a lower-ranking judge to act as the chief judge.

​The controversial decision, which paralysed the state High Court for months, was criticised by the Nigerian Bar Association and rejected by the NJC for disregarding the seniority principle.

​In April 2025, the NJC roundly rejected the appointment of Theophilus Nzeukwu, who was the number four in the hierarchy of judges of the state, as acting chief judge.

​The NJC said Mr Nzeukwu’s appointment violated Section 271(4) of the Nigerian Constitution, which mandates the governor to “appoint the most senior judge of the High Court” to temporarily perform the functions of the chief judge whenever the office becomes vacant.

​It also ordered that Mr Nzeukwu should be issued a query for accepting the appointment by Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma as the acting chief judge in violation of the constitution.

In June, about two months after rejecting Mr Nzeukwu’s appointment and issuing him a query, the NJC sent him on compulsory retirement for accepting to be sworn in for the acting chief judge role.

​The council also restated its stance, directing Governor Uzodimma to comply with its directive to swear in the state’s most senior judge.

​The governor had justified picking Mr Nzeukwu, which he said was based on “credible reports available to him at the time.”

​He said in a statement that reports submitted to him indicated Mr Nzeukwu was the “most senior judicial officer not encumbered by unresolved issues.”

​But the NJC stressed that the constitutional provision on acting appointments of state chief judges did not leave room for discretion.

​Mr Uzodimma subsequently agreed to comply with the directives of the NJC.

​But while the state government bowed to the NJC’s directive, it remained resolute in only allowing Ms Agugua to occupy the office in an acting capacity.

​Why NJC took latest decision on Imo chief judge position

​The NJC said it directed the Imo State Judicial Commission to include Ms Agugua’s name in the list of nominees for appointment as the substantive chief judge in the state, following a petition dated 11 June by Bob Kay Njemanze.

​It said Mr Njemanze’s petition challenged the exclusion of Ms Agugua from the shortlist submitted by the Judicial Service Commission.

​Imo judiciary at the centre of attention

The Imo State judiciary has been at the centre of attention for the wrong reasons for two years.

In November 2024, its then chief judge, Mr Chikeka, was sent on compulsory retirement over age falsification, setting off the leadership crisis that has dogged the state judiciary since then.

​In June last year, the NJC recommended Mr Nzeukwu for compulsory retirement for making himself available to be sworn in as the acting chief judge “knowing fully well that he was number four in the hierarchy of Judges of the Imo State Judiciary and contrary to Section 271 (4) of the Nigerian constitution.”

​At the same meeting, the council recommended the compulsory retirement of a set of nine judges of the Imo State High Court found to be culpable of age falsifications.

​But the council absolved the President of the Customary Court of Appeal, Imo State, V. U. Okorie, who chaired the commission that nominated Mr Nzeukwu as the acting chief judge.

World.title: Japan vs Nigeria LIVE UPDATES: Flamingos chase historic U-17 World Cup title
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flamingos are all set to take on Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup tonight at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat, Morocco.

The Coach Akeem Busari-led Falmingos team are seeking to win the country’s and indeed the continet’s first-ever title in the competition.

The Nigerian side made history by reaching the final after a remarkable 3-1 victory over Brazil in the semi-finals, guaranteeing at least a silver medal and surpassing their previous best finish of third place in 2022.

Japan, meanwhile, stand between the Flamingos and a historic triumph as both teams pursue their maiden title.

Follow PREMIUM TIMES for live updates, goals and key moments as Nigeria chase their first U-17 Women’s World Cup crown.

Kickoff is 7.30pm

Flamingos retain winning XI, Japan make four changes for final

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Team news

Nigeria’s Flamingos have retained the starting XI that defeated Brazil 3-1 in the semi-finals as they prepare to face Japan in the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup final in Rabat, Morocco.

Coach Akeem Busari has kept faith with the team that secured Nigeria’s historic place in the final, with Awawu Bashiru retaining her starting spot after scoring twice against Brazil.

Captain Azeezat Oduntan will continue to lead the defence, while Jane Ijirigho starts in goal.

Japan, meanwhile, have made four changes to the side that drew 1-1 with Korea DPR before advancing 4-1 on penalties.

Wara Shimizu, Sayana Oshita, Rara Higuchi and Yuka Kishida come into the starting XI, replacing Anri Ito, Himari Nishi, Keiko Kitajima and Nanami Kurita.

Substitutes: Mikan Yamanaka, Riruha Wakatsuki, Anri Ito, Himari Nishi, Asuka Tanaka, Keiko Kitajima, Runa Sumiya, Arisu Ota, Kotone Sato, Nanami Kurita.

The final kicks off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3.

World.title: Amaechi challenges Wike on Atiku’s Rivers campaign rally
World.content:
Former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi has challenged the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and the Rivers State authorities to provide a venue for an African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign rally, expressing confidence that Atiku Abubakar would win the state in the 2027 election.

Mr Amaechi, the ADC’s vice-presidential candidate, issued the challenge during an interview on Mainland 98.3 FM’s The Situation Room on Friday, 6 November.

“Atiku will come to Rivers State. Tell them to give us a venue,” he said, adding that the opposition party’s supporters could fill a large-capacity facility.

His remarks came ahead of Saturday’s rally at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, organised by the Rainbow Coalition, an alliance of politicians from the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

As PREMIUM TIMES previously reported, Mr Wike’s coalition has endorsed the president while backing candidates from both parties for other elective offices.

Stadium capacity claims and history of disruption

Mr Wike said on Friday that organisers expected at least 70,000 people at the president’s rally. That was his projected turnout, not an independently verified attendance figure.

Speaking during an inspection of the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, he said the facility had a seating capacity of 40,000, compared with 16,000 at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, where the coalition had previously unveiled its candidates.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Amaechi, who governed Rivers between 2007 and 2015, did not identify a formal application the ADC submitted for a campaign venue or say any facility had refused the party access.

His challenge comes against a history of disruptions involving ADC activities in the state.

In March, PREMIUM TIMES reported that suspected political thugs disrupted an ADC women’s gathering in Eleme Local Government Area, destroying equipment and dispersing participants.

The report also referred to an earlier attack on the party’s ward secretariat in Ubima, Mr Amaechi’s hometown, where gunmen allegedly attempted to block his convoy during a registration exercise.

Those incidents did not establish that the Rivers State Government had refused the ADC access to a campaign venue.

Mr Wike and Mr Amaechi have remained political rivals since the former succeeded the latter as governor in 2015.

At the Rainbow Coalition’s October unveiling, Mr Wike criticised his predecessor’s record in office and questioned his administration’s handling of public projects and funds.

The former governor made his latest comments during a wider Mainland 98.3 FM interview covering the ADC leadership dispute, the 2027 presidential campaign and the party’s economic proposals.

PREMIUM TIMES sought clarification from Mr Amaechi on whether the ADC had formally requested a campaign venue in Rivers, which facility it intended to use and whether any request had been rejected.

His campaign spokesperson, Phrank Shaibu, confirmed that the questions had been forwarded to Mr Amaechi. A response was still being awaited at the time of filing.

World.title: Chelle leaves Okoye, in-form Iheanacho out of Super Eagles squad for Tanzania ties
World.content:
Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle has left out goalkeeper Maduka Okoye and forward Kelechi Iheanacho from his 24-man squad for Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Tanzania.

The omissions are among the major talking points in the squad announced ahead of the two fixtures, scheduled for 13 and 17 November.

Okoye’s absence comes after a difficult spell with Italian club Udinese, while Iheanacho has been in prolific scoring form for Turkish side Bursaspor.

Chelle has instead selected Stanley Nwabali, Francis Uzoho and Arthur Okonkwo as his goalkeeping options for the double-header.

Okoye was part of Nigeria’s squad for the September qualifiers against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau. However, his absence from the latest selection follows a period in which his availability for national team duties attracted attention.

During the September international window, the goalkeeper arrived after the opening of camp following his involvement in Udinese’s third-kit presentation in Milan during Fashion Week. Chelle subsequently explained that he had granted the player permission to attend to the club activity.

The latest omission comes as Udinese struggle in Serie A. Okoye was in goal on Friday when his side lost 2-1 away to Akor Adams’ Venezia, conceding twice in a result that left Udinese at the bottom of the table.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The defeat was Udinese’s eighth in their last nine league matches. Okoye had also conceded five goals in the club’s 5-2 loss to Roma on 31 October.

Venezia, meanwhile, ended a run of three consecutive defeats with the victory. Adams played the full match but did not score.

Iheanacho’s scoring form not enough

Iheanacho’s omission is another notable decision, given his recent performances for Bursaspor.

The former Leicester City forward has been among the goals in Turkey, recording 17 league goals for the club. He also scored in Nigeria’s 3-3 international friendly draw against Russia in October.

His return to scoring form, however, was not enough to earn him a place in Chelle’s squad for the Tanzania matches.

The forward had featured in the separate group selected for the Russia friendly, but has now been left out of the coach’s latest competitive selection.

Ndidi, Iwobi lead 24-man squad

Captain Wilfred Ndidi, Alex Iwobi, Ademola Lookman, Moses Simon and Calvin Bassey are among the established players retained for the qualifiers.

The squad also includes defender Chibuike Nwaiwu and midfielder Mubarak Suleiman, while Arthur Okonkwo retains his place among the goalkeepers.

The full squad is:

Goalkeepers: Stanley Nwabali (Chippa United, South Africa); Francis Uzoho (Omonia FC, Cyprus); Arthur Okonkwo (Charlton Athletic, England).

Defenders: Bruno Onyemaechi (Olympiakos, Greece); Ola Aina (Nottingham Forest, England); Benjamin Fredricks (Brentford, England); Semi Ajayi (Hull City, England); Calvin Bassey (Fulham, England); Chibuike Nwaiwu (Trabzonspor, Turkey); Bright Osayi-Samuel (Birmingham City, England); Abdullahi Bewene (Banik Ostrava, Czechia).
