The Super Eagles are seeking maximum points from the two matches to strengthen their chances of qualifying for the 2027 AFCON, which will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

World.title: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran’s nuclear programme
World.content:
The US is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for any Iranian who provides useful information on Iran’s nuclear programme

The Central Command announced the offer on Friday in a statement shared on X. It said it seeks information about Iran’s nuclear programme, facilities, equipment, and personnel.

The reward is being administered through the State Department’s Rewards for Justice national security program.

“Rewards for Justice (RFJ), a program dedicated to gathering information on terrorism and foreign operations against the US, issued a new offer for information including facilities, equipment, and personnel connected to Iran’s nuclear program,” the statement read.

This comes despite US President Donald Trump’s oft-repeated claim that Tehran’s nuclear sites and operations have been obliterated.

Mr Trump first said this in June 2025, after the US struck Iran’s nuclear facilities. The attack targeted Iran’s Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan facilities.

Mr Trump told the nation the key enrichment sites had been “completely and totally obliterated.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But PREMIUM TIMES reported that a leaked preliminary Pentagon assessment found that the strikes sealed the entrances to two facilities without collapsing the underground buildings, and that much of the enriched uranium had been moved beforehand.

However, the US president reiterated the claim many times since another 28 February strike, which protracted into an 8-month war. During an interview in March, he said Iran’s capabilities were “totally obliterated.”

Last month, he also claimed the US Central Command obliterated Iran’s nuclear programme, and that war will end ‘very soon.’

“If they had nuclear power, they would have used nuclear power. They would have obliterated the Middle East “ he also said.

According to CENTCOM, Iran’s lack of compliance with the International Atomic Energy Agency on safeguards obligations has led to the “agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components such as centrifuges.”

It also said, “Iran’s uranium stockpile is believed to include uranium that has been enriched to 60 per cent purity – ‘a level that is a short technical step from the 90 per cent level required to produce nuclear weapons.”

“Iran is the only non-nuclear-weapon state to produce uranium at such a high enrichment level. Experts estimate this quantity, if enriched further, could be enough for several nuclear weapons,” the statement read.

Meanwhile, President Trump also confirmed that the US carried out “minor strikes” in Iran.

“We do minor strikes. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device, and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe 5,” he told reporters.

Iranian media have reported missiles striking Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has also said it has brought down some US battle drones in recent weeks.

World.title: ADC Judgement: Amaechi reveals talks with Atiku, David Mark to avert unrest
World.content:
Former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi has warned that the Federal High Court judgement against the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) could trigger unrest, saying Atiku Abubakar and other senior party officials discussed how to prevent an angry reaction from supporters.

Mr Amaechi said the discussion followed Thursday’s ruling by Justice Peter Lifu, which invalidated the David Mark-led leadership and the party’s nominations for the 2027 elections.

“It could cause a civil war if not properly managed,” he said during an interview on Mainland 98.3 FM’s The Situation Room on Friday.

The former transportation minister, who is the ADC’s vice-presidential candidate, said he was in Kebbi State when he and other party leaders learnt of the judgement.

“When we heard this, we quickly met, myself and the presidential candidate and the chairman of the party, and we said, ‘Please, lower the tempo down,'” he said.

Mr Amaechi said he appeared on the radio programme partly to reassure party members that the ruling would be challenged through the courts.

The interview was broadcast on Mainland 98.3 FM, which also shared excerpts on Facebook.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Court ruling and ADC’s appeal

Justice Lifu delivered the judgement on Thursday in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the ADC, who challenged the emergence of Mr Mark and other members of the party’s national executive.

Mr Gombe claimed he was entitled to assume the chairmanship following the resignation of Ralph Nwosu, the party’s former national chairman.

As PREMIUM TIMES reported, the judge directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) not to recognise decisions taken at the ADC’s 99th National Executive Committee meeting of 27 July 2025 and subsequent actions, including the nomination of candidates for the 2027 elections.

Mr Amaechi criticised the court’s intervention, arguing that the dispute concerned the ADC’s internal affairs.

“I know that one of the things they will teach you in law school is that internal affairs of the party are not justiciable,” he said.

Justice Lifu rejected the defendants’ jurisdictional objection, a decision the ADC is challenging.

During the interview, Mr Amaechi said he expected the party’s lawyers to have filed an appeal and an application for a stay of execution.

The ADC subsequently confirmed the filings. As PREMIUM TIMES reported in its Saturday politics roundup, a letter bearing INEC’s receipt stamp showed that the party’s lawyers asked the commission not to implement the ruling while the appeal was pending.

The stay application had not been determined when the lawyers wrote to INEC. Filing an appeal does not, by itself, suspend a judgment.

APC denies interference

Mr Amaechi accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of encouraging the leadership dispute to weaken the ADC ahead of the presidential election.

He rejected suggestions of an internal rift, citing what he described as a signed resignation document and video footage showing Mr Nwosu handing over to Mr Mark.

“No, no, there’s no internal rift in our party. None. Absolutely none. It is just the fear of APC,” he said.

He offered no evidence during the interview linking the ruling party to the litigation.

The APC has denied interfering in the dispute.

As PREMIUM TIMES reported on Friday, its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said the case arose from disagreements among ADC officials over the emergence of the Mark-led leadership.

Mr Morka maintained that the APC was neither a party to the litigation nor involved in the dispute.

“If ADC is dissatisfied with that decision, it should exercise its constitutional right of appeal rather than engage in partisan mudslinging against our great Party and issuing threats to incite anarchy against the same Nigerians they claim they desire to govern,” he said.

Mr Amaechi, meanwhile, insisted the party would continue its campaign despite the ruling.

“We will be on the ballot. Be rest assured we will be on the ballot,” he said.

The assurance remains subject to the outcome of the legal proceedings and any applicable court orders.

World.title: Hunger: Tinubu tackles Atiku, asks how he built university as VP
World.content:
Collage of Atiku Abubakar and Bola Tinubu

By Ayobami Okerinde

President Bola Tinubu has hit back at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and others criticising his administration over hardship and hunger, accusing them of contributing to the problems he inherited.

Tinubu spoke on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

Responding to those raising concerns about hunger, Tinubu said his administration was working to address the problems left behind by previous governments.

“Those people talking of hunger, I’m cleaning the mess they created. Atiku was one of them,” Tinubu said.

He then questioned how Atiku, who served as vice president and was involved in economic affairs during the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, was able to establish a university while in office.

“Ask him how he built a university while in office as vice president in charge of our economy. Who built the university for him? It’s your money. It’s your effort,” he said.

He further questioned Atiku’s moral standing to criticise his administration, describing him as a man lacking the integrity and ethical standards required for public office.

Tinubu also expressed appreciation to Rivers residents for the support they gave him during the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his emergence as president.

“Thank you for the last election. In 2022, 2023, I looked very hopeless, but you trooped out to support me and gave me the mandate,” Tinubu said.

“I’m seeking a second term because you believe in me and that I care for you,” he said.

World.title: Tinubu: Yari sets 2.3m votes target for Rivers APC
World.content:
Yari

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Sen. Abdulaziz Yari, on Saturday set a target of 2.3 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in Rivers state in the January 16 election.

Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Yari said the party would mobilize its supporters to achieve the feat.

“The message here, we are looking for at least nothing less than 2.3 million votes,” he said.

He asked the crowd to raise their hands if they were ready to support the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to deliver Tinubu at that figure.

Yari said the figure was within reach, citing voter data he obtained from the coalition’s leaders in the state.

“Out of 3.3 million voters registered and about 2.8 million PVCs collected, we should be aiming at nothing less than 2.3 million,” he said.

He told the President that Rivers was one of the states from which the party expected “nothing less than 80 percent, by God’s grace.”

Yari also took aim at the opposition, saying those seeking power had themselves been in government without achieving anything tangible.

“From Atiku, to Peter Obi, to Amaechi, down to vice president Atiku Abubakar. He was elected as a governor before becoming a vice president,” he said.

The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, said Rivers was the only state in the South-South that Tinubu won convincingly in 2023, and that the state was ready to repeat the feat.

He equally added that under Tinubu, Nigeria now gets more revenue from taxation than from crude oil.

National Chairman of the APC, Nentawe Yilwatda, described the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as “the best for now in Nigeria.”

“Here, we have the numbers. Here, we have the voters,” he said of Rivers.

Senator Magnus Abe, who spoke on behalf of Rivers stakeholders, defended the Rainbow Coalition, whose members, he said, have diverse interests but “whose main interest is to return the president to power.”

Abe said he was surprised to hear some party members talking down on the coalition.

World.title: Why I ditched Atiku – Okowa
World.content:
Senator Ifeanyi Okowa

Former Delta State Governor and 2023 running mate to Atiku Abubakar, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, has explained why he is now supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Speaking on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Okowa said he had “seen the light.”

“I have seen the light. Today, we are on the right track because the president is laying a solid foundation,” he declared.

Okowa warned against any return of the fuel subsidy, stating that those who previously destroyed Nigeria’s foundation through the subsidy regime must not be allowed to “destroy the future of our children.”

At the same rally, Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, set a target of 2.3 million votes for Tinubu in Rivers State in the January 16 election. He said the figure was achievable, noting that about 2.8 million Permanent Voter Cards had been collected out of 3.3 million registered voters in the state.

Yari asked supporters to back Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike in delivering the votes and described Rivers as a state from which the party expected “nothing less than 80 percent.”

Senate President Godswill Akpabio noted that Rivers was the only South-South state Tinubu won convincingly in 2023 and expressed confidence that the feat would be repeated. He also claimed that under Tinubu, Nigeria now generates more revenue from taxation than from crude oil.

APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda described the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as “the best for now in Nigeria,” while Senator Magnus Abe defended the Rainbow Coalition in the state, saying its main interest was to return the president to power.

World.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
World.content:
Arsenal’s Norwegian midfielder #08 Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring the team’s first goal during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Hull City at the Emirates Stadium in London on November 7, 2026. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds.

Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match.

Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games.

Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat.

Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy.

But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up.

Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish.

Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range.

– VAR controversy –

In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run.

The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared.

Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks.

“In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat.

He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.”

Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”.

Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw.

World.title: Tinubu to Nigerian youths: Your future depends on 2027 election
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian youths to collect their Permanent Voter Cards and participate actively in the 2027 general elections, saying the outcome of the poll will have a direct bearing on their future.

Tinubu made the call on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

Addressing the youths at the rally, the president said the election should not be viewed as being about his personal ambition but about determining the future of the younger generation.

“To the youth of Nigeria, I’m looking at you. This election is about you. It’s not about me. Your future depends on this election,” he said.

Tinubu urged Nigerians who were yet to collect their PVCs to do so, describing the voter card as the means through which citizens could determine the country’s leadership.

“It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please. I beg you. “I take God, beg you,” he said.

The president also identified economic development as a key tool for young Nigerians to overcome poverty, saying his administration was working to improve the economy and ensure that prosperity was widely shared.

He said previous administrations had left behind unpaid pensions and gratuities running into billions and trillions of naira, adding that his government was clearing the outstanding obligations.

“The people that governed before left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included. We are sharing prosperity already,” Tinubu said.

He listed retired professionals, including engineers, welders, and teachers, among those benefiting from the payments.

“A retired engineer is receiving their gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving the pension right now. A retired teacher is receiving the pension right now,” he added.

World.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
World.content:
Argentina’s forward #10 Lionel Messi looks at the trophy after losing the 2026 World Cup football tournament final match between Spain and Argentina at the New York/New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford on July 19, 2026. (Photo by PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA / AFP)





Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents.

Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players.

He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19.

The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters.

Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also hit with bans and fines, as was Roberto Ayala, a member of Argentina’s coaching team.

In a statement, AFA said FIFA’s appeals body had rejected their complaint against the sanctions handed out to Paredes and the association, but had reduced Molina’s punishment from a seven-match ban and $90,000 fine to four games and $60,000.

AFA also stated it would now take its appeals against its own and Paredes’s sanctions to CAS.

World.title: Re-election: Tinubu lists economy, education, healthcare as priorities
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to give priority attention to education, economic recovery, healthcare and citizens’ welfare if given another mandate in 2027.

Tinubu made the pledge at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt on Saturday.

Speaking at the rally co-organised by the Rainbow Coalition led by Chief Nyesom Wike, the Minister, Federal Capital Territory, Tinubu also said that youth development would be given deserved attention.

The president urged Rivers people to use their Permanent Voter Cards wisely to achieve a better and more progressive Nigeria.

He expressed his administration’s commitment to promote the welfare of retirees through enhanced and prompt payment of pensions and gratuities.

He commended Wike and the people of Rivers for massively expressing their resolve to support his re-election bid.

The president thanked Wike for his commitment to reconciliation and peace-building during the political crisis that rocked the state.

Tinubu also commended Gov. Siminalayi Fubara for being a peaceful leader and lover of his state, saying, “The governor will never regret his commitment to restoring peace in the state.”

“I sincerely appreciate Wike, Fubara, APC members and the Rainbow Coalition Campaign Council for their support,” he said.

Earlier, Wike assured the president that Rivers residents would massively support his re-election bid.

He said that Tinubu had demonstrated huge support to the state by appointing no fewer than 47 Rivers people into strategic positions at the national level.

“We cannot take the president’s support for granted. Rivers people will vote massively for the president in the 2027 presidential election,” he said.

Also speaking, Fubara said that Rivers would deliver no fewer than three million votes in support of the president’s re-election bid.

“We shall continue to work together to ensure that the president wins the election; that is our promise,” he said.

He thanked the campaign team for providing an opportunity for Rivers people to demonstrate their political strength and support for the president.

Fubara thanked Tinubu for his commitment to the development of the Niger Delta Region through critical infrastructure projects, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that while in the state, Tinubu inaugurated the Bonny-Bodo Road project.

He also presented the APC governorship flag to the party’s candidate in Rivers, Mr Kingsley Chinda. (NAN)

World.title: Hope you’ll visit 33 other states after Akwa Ibom ‘sleep’ – Obi tells Tinubu
World.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to extend his visits to the remaining 33 states of the federation after spending a night in Akwa Ibom State.

Obi made the call in a post on X on Saturday, following Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom, where the president said his overnight stay would be a “second term presidential sleep” ahead of the 2027 election.

Obi congratulated Tinubu on spending a night in a state outside Lagos and Abuja, urging the president to use such visits to engage directly with Nigerians and explain the impact of his administration.

He said he hoped the Akwa Ibom visit would encourage Tinubu to travel to the other 33 states, spend time with the people and account for the resources accruing to the Federal Government.

“I sincerely hope this visit will inspire you to travel to the remaining 33 states of the federation, spend time with the people and, more importantly, explain what your administration has done with the ₦15.8 trillion saved from the removal of fuel subsidy, the over $100 billion you have borrowed, the increased revenues accruing to the government from taxing Nigerians, and the additional government revenues which your administration celebrated last year as having surpassed its target,” Obi said.

The former Anambra State governor also demanded explanations on the impact of government policies on poverty, education, healthcare and electricity.

He asked the President to state how many Nigerians had been lifted out of poverty, how many out-of-school children had returned to school and how many functional primary healthcare centres had been built.

Obi also questioned the improvement in electricity supply, recalling Tinubu’s earlier promise that Nigerians should not vote for him if his administration failed to fix the power sector.

On insecurity, he said Nigerians deserved an explanation of what the government had done to secure the country, which he noted still ranks among the world’s most terrorised countries.

“Mr President, Nigerians deserve answers. They deserve to know what has been done with the resources entrusted to your government,” Obi said.

He added that the New Nigeria he seeks to build would be founded on accountability, transparency and the measurable impact of public resources on citizens.

Tinubu had on Friday told supporters at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom, describing it as a “second term presidential sleep” and expressing confidence in securing re-election in 2027.

World.title: Tinubu: Atiku Part of Those That Created the Mess I’m Clearing
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has said that the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar was part of those that created the mess his government was cleaning up now.

Atiku was vice president between 1999 and 2007 during the administration of President Olusegun Obasanjo.

Tinubu stated this Saturday during the presidential campaign rally of the All Progressives Congress (APC) held in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

He said when he was helpless, the people of Port Harcourt supported him and gave him the mandate.

The President stated: “I look very helpless. But you stood out to support me, give me the mandate. The mandate that I used to govern till today, you are a positive contributor. I must thank you for going out there to vote and vote massively for APC. Today again, I return here to say thank you. And seek your support for the second term.

“I’m seeking that support because you believe in me. You believe that I care for you, particularly the young youth. Your education, your welfare, your skill is extremely important to me, to Nigeria. I assure you this, we have started the golden age. The prosperity is here.”

Tinbu said when he took over, 27 out of 36 states were unable to pay salaries, saying that meant a lot for the families that depend on the salaries and to many households

He stressed that ever since, his administration had reversed the ugly trend, saying the country was on the move for prosperity.

Tinubu stated: “Those people, talking of hunger, we are clearing the mess they created. Atiku was one of them.

“Ask him how he built the university while he was in office as vice president — in charge of our economy. Who built the university for you? Is it your money? Is it your effort? A man without moral integrity, latitude and ethics for the office.”

The president described the Minister of Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike as a development partner of his administration, saying he is doing a wonderful job.

He commended Wike for maintaining peace and stability during the civic crisis, created by misunderstanding in the family.

Tinubu added: “To me, I intervene on your behalf, Similayi Fubara. Your excellency, the host governor of the day. I want to thank you specifically for the maturity, understanding, and respect for the wisdom of elders.

“When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat. Fubara you will not regret what you have done. As long as all of us are alive.’

Tinubu said the 2027 elections are about the youth of Nigeria.

He stated: “This election is about you (youth). It’s not all about me. Your future depends on this election. It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it.

“The weapon you have against poverty. Is to elect progressive development of our economy. That is what I’m pursuing. The people that governed before, they left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of Naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included.

“We are sharing prosperity already. A retired engineer is receiving a gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving a pension right now, a retired teacher is receiving a pension right now.”

Also, Vice President Kashim Shetima said River state is the true definition of political alliances, it is River State.

He recalled that four years ago, Rivers people gave the ruling party their trust and they have not withdrawn it and also stood by it.

Shettima added: “Good people of Rivers State, you chose to stand by us when the easier choice was to stand elsewhere. We ask you to make that choice again. We ask you to renew your mandate again. We have traveled too far to abandon the Rivers people. We have worked too hard to surrender again.”

The vice president berated those he referred to as political charlatans on the other side of the divide making efforts to demonize President Tinubu instead of celebrating him.

Shettima said the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar and his Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) counterpart, Peter Obi are no match for Tinubu.

He described Obi’s performance as Governor of Anambra state for eight years and Chairman of a bank as mediocre.

Shettima noted: “I dare say, without any fear of equivocation, that President Bola Tinubu is a decent man. When he assumed office as President, three and a half years ago, our economy was seemingly on the verge of collapse. We were on the road to Caracas. Instead of demonizing his successor with his predecessor, the president had the moral courage, had the conviction, to take the bull by the horn.”

Speaking, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Abubakar Yari said the ruling party has set a target of 2.3 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in Rivers State.

He also expressing confidence in the state’s capacity to deliver an overwhelming victory for the President in the 2027 elections.

Yari noted that the state has approximately 3.3 million registered voters, out of which 2.8 million have collected their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

He stressed that the figures present a strong electoral opportunity, adding that Rivers State was among the states expected to deliver between 75 and 80 per cent of the votes for President Tinubu.

Yari commended the people of Rivers State, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and other stakeholders for the massive mobilisation and support for the President.

He described the emerging political alliance as a working rainbow coalition, expressing optimism that the growing unity across political divides would strengthen Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Taking a swipe at the opposition, Yari highlighted Tinubu’s record as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, particularly his foundation for sustainable revenue generation.

He recalled that Lagos State’s internally generated revenue stood at about ₦600 million when Tinubu assumed office, but has since grown to over ₦100 billion monthly under successive administrations, including the current government of Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

Yari expressed confidence that the same vision and institutional foundations that transformed Lagos State could be replicated at the national level, adding that the policies and reforms being implemented by President Tinubu would benefit future generations.

Yari urged Nigerians, particularly the people of Rivers State, to sustain their support for the President, expressing confidence in a strong electoral outing in 2027.

On his part, the National Chairman APC, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda described the Tinubu-Shettima presidential ticket as one of the most formidable political combinations in Nigeria’s democratic history.

He declared that Tinubu deserves another term to consolidate the bold reforms and transformative development initiatives of his administration.

Yilwatda noted that the Tinubu-Shettima ticket represented a combination of political experience, courage, capacity and tested leadership, capable of steering Nigeria through its current challenges towards sustainable economic growth and national prosperity.

His words: “The most formidable presidential ticket we have ever produced in Nigeria is the Tinubu-Shettima ticket. We have a candidate in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu who is fearless, courageous and determined to confront the challenges of our country.

” He has demonstrated the capacity to take difficult decisions in the national interest, and he has remained resolute in pursuing the transformation of Nigeria.

“President Tinubu has confronted enormous challenges since assuming office, and rather than surrendering to them, he has taken decisive steps to address the structural problems that have constrained our national development for decades.

“He inherited a country facing serious fiscal and economic difficulties, including unsustainable fuel subsidy expenditure, revenue constraints and mounting obligations. His administration has demonstrated the political will to confront these challenges through difficult but necessary reforms.”

Yilwatda noted that the removal of the fuel subsidy, the unification of the foreign exchange market and other economic policy adjustments were important components of the administration’s efforts to rebuild the economy, strengthen public finances and establish a more sustainable foundation for long-term growth.

He acknowledged that the reforms had come with significant adjustments for households and businesses but maintained that the administration was committed to addressing their impact through economic stabilisation measures, social interventions, infrastructure investments and policies designed to expand opportunities for Nigerians.

Yilwatda urged Nigerians not to lose sight of the long-term objectives of the Renewed Hope Agenda, insisting that the country must sustain the reform trajectory to enable the administration to consolidate its policies and deliver greater economic benefits.

He described President Tinubu as a reformer and performer whose leadership vision places national development above political convenience, adding that the 2027 election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to choose continuity, stability and the consolidation of ongoing reforms.

The chairman commended the political leaders, stakeholders and members of the Rainbow Coalition for recognising the importance of national unity, political cooperation and continuity in the pursuit of Nigeria’s development.

According to him, the emerging political consensus in Rivers State reflects a broader recognition that the success of the Tinubu administration is in the collective interest of Nigerians, irrespective of their political affiliations.

“Come 2027, we want to continue with this reformer and performer as our President. That is why the coalition and the people of Rivers State, irrespective of political party, have decided to work together for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Yilwatda said.

The chairman expressed confidence that Rivers State would deliver overwhelming electoral support for President Tinubu, predicting that the state would become a major stronghold of the President’s re-election campaign.

World.title: Navy Rescues Seven Victims of Bayelsa Boat Mishap, Uncovers 117,000 Litres of Stolen Crude Oil
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Navy, in collaboration with local divers and members of the Abedigbene Fishing Community, has rescued seven passengers following a boat mishap in the waters around Abedigbene, in Brass Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the incident involved a passenger boat travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa, which reportedly had eight people on board.

“Following a distress report from a local fisherman, personnel of Forward Operating Base (FOB) Formoso, deployed at Labrador Lagosgbene Houseboat, promptly mobilised to the scene and commenced search and rescue operations with the support of local divers and community members.

“The rescued passengers included the Bayelsa State Commissioner for Trade, Industry and Investment, Dr Ebieri Jones, an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, and five other passengers,” Captain Folorunsho said in the statement.

He said the survivors were taken to the houseboat, where they received first aid, with preliminary assessments indicating that none had sustained visible injuries.

He, however, regretted that one passenger, identified as a police officer, remained missing, while search and rescue efforts continued to locate the officer.

He said, “On 6 November 2026, the Commissioner and the six other survivors were conveyed to Yenagoa to reunite with their respective families.

The Commanding Officer of FOB Formoso commended the personnel for their prompt response and professionalism, while acknowledging the invaluable support of the local divers and host community.

Captain Folorunsho noted that the successful rescue further highlighted the importance of collaboration between security agencies and coastal communities in strengthening maritime safety and protecting lives.

Meanwhile, the Forward Operating Base (FOB) Bonny deactivated three illegal refining sites in Awokiri Community, Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State, uncovering approximately 117,000 litres of stolen crude oil.

The naval spokesperson said the operation was conducted following credible intelligence indicating the activation of new illegal refining sites in the area.

“During the operation, the naval team discovered 16 dugout pits, nine of which contained approximately 115,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil. An additional storage tank contained about 2,000 litres, bringing the total volume to approximately 117,000 litres. Four other pits contained water, while three were freshly excavated. The identified sites, pits and products were handled in accordance with extant regulations.”

Folorunsho said the operation underscored the Nigerian Navy’s sustained commitment to combating crude oil theft and illegal bunkering through intelligence-driven operations.

He added that by dismantling illegal refining infrastructure and disrupting criminal networks, the Service continued to protect critical oil and gas assets and safeguard the nation’s economic interests.

World.title: Navy Sustains Zero Piracy Incidents in One Year, Secures Nine Convictions of Crude Oil Thieves
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Navy has said that between November 2025 and November 2026, it sustained Nigeria’s zero-piracy status and secured nine convictions for offences relating to crude oil theft and pipeline vandalism.

The Service also disclosed that, within the period under review, it deactivated 168 illegal refining sites, destroyed 363 dugout pits, arrested 259 suspects and seized four vessels suspected of involvement in crude oil theft.

The Director of Naval Information, Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, in a statement marking Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abba’s first year in office, further revealed that the Service recovered over 7.48 million litres of stolen crude oil and illegally refined petroleum products within the year.

Folorunsho said the Nigerian Navy recorded significant operational, infrastructural and institutional achievements during Vice Admiral Idi Abba’s first year as Chief of the Naval Staff, strengthening its contribution to maritime security, the protection of national assets and national development.

He said, “A major operational initiative was the activation of Operation Delta Sentinel in January 2026 to strengthen efforts against crude oil theft, illegal bunkering and other maritime crimes. The Navy also commissioned three high-speed patrol vessels, NNS Oloibiri, NNS Mambila and NNS Gurara, in June 2026 to enhance maritime surveillance, operational reach and response capabilities.

“The Service also advanced infrastructure development and personnel welfare through the construction and commissioning of over 36 projects, including accommodation, medical, office and multipurpose facilities. In addition, it commenced the development of a 200-bed Reference Hospital at Navy Town, Asokoro, Abuja. Through the Chief of the Naval Staff Special Intervention Quick Impact Projects (CNS-SIQIP) and other community initiatives, the Navy completed over 93 community development projects.”

These projects, he said, included 18 solar-powered boreholes, the renovation of 11 school buildings, the construction and equipping of 11 healthcare centres, and the provision of electricity infrastructure in three communities.

“On human capacity development, the Nigerian Navy graduated and inducted its inaugural batch of 328 Nigerian Navy Marines. The personnel were deployed to reinforce ongoing operations, particularly against asymmetric threats in northern Nigeria, while training for a second batch continued,” the Naval Spokesperson said.

Furthermore, the Navy strengthened regional maritime cooperation through its participation in exercises, including Obangame Express 2026, Coastal Grip 2, Grand African Nemo 2026 and Crocodile Lift.

World.title: Nigeria Deepens Defence Ties with Germany
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), has assured the German Government that Nigeria remains committed to honouring existing military agreements and deepening strategic defence cooperation with its international partners.

General Musa gave the assurance when he received a high-level delegation led by the Ambassador of Germany to Nigeria and ECOWAS, His Excellency Stefan Rössel, at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters in Abuja.

Welcoming the Ambassador and his delegation, the minister assured them that the ministry would ensure the optimal deployment and maintenance of all defence support equipment provided to the Armed Forces of Nigeria.

According to a statement by the Minister of Defence’s Special Assistant on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, General Musa also pledged that all operational and administrative concerns raised during the meeting would be addressed expeditiously.

Reflecting on previous fruitful engagements during his tenure as Chief of Defence Staff, Musa expressed Nigeria’s profound gratitude to Germany for its sustained technical assistance, particularly the provision of critical medical facilities for Nigerian troops over the years.

Earlier, Ambassador Rössel extended his heartfelt condolences to the minister, the Armed Forces and the people of Nigeria over the recent Nigerian Air Force plane crash. He explained that his visit was aimed at reinforcing bilateral relations, strengthening security cooperation and exploring new avenues for operational support.

Both leaders reaffirmed their shared commitment to advancing a robust and mutually beneficial multilateral defence architecture.

World.title: Abia Moves to Harness AGOA’s Benefits, Hosts 1st Africando Conference in Umuahia
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

As part of efforts at harnessing the United States economic development programme, the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), the Abia State Government has announced the hosting of the 2026 African Diaspora Conference and Expo (Africando).

The conference scheduled for November 17-19, at the state capital, Umuahia, is expected to bring together African and US businessmen and women, educators, government policymakers and administrators, trade and investment experts, bankers and representatives from international organisations, with the aim of improving trade and expanding markets for African products in the international marketplace.

Speaking with journalists in Abuja yesterday, the Chief of Staff to Governor Alex Otti, Mr. Caleb Ajagba, attributed the choice of Abia State as host of the Africando, to the transformation of the state to an industrial hub, in the current administration.

He recall that Governor Otti, on assumption of office decided to prioritize the issue of infrastructure, security, power supply, manpower development and entrepreneurial capacity in other to exploit the potentials of the state and people of Abia.

According to the Chief of Staff, Abia’s manufacturing base, particularly in Aba, offered opportunities for international business partnerships and investment.

Stating that, “Aba is a place where anything can be manufactured”, Ajagba disclosed that Africando aims to provide necessary resources to small and medium scale businesses.

The Chief of Staff added that besides making funds available for acquisition of equipment, the Otti’s administration had put in place policies and programmes that would create an international market for products.

He disclosed that the government as part of measures at encouraging participation at the conference has made registration easy for those interested.

Ajagba also promised that the state government would work with the organisers to ensure the conference delivered practical economic benefits to businesses and the state.

Also speaking, the President, Foundation for Democracy in Africa, Mr. Fred Oladeinde, disclosed that plans were underway to establish a trade centre and civil society network to facilitate access to international markets, investment opportunities and business partnerships for local enterprises.

According to him, the proposed platforms would work with the Abia Global Chamber of Commerce, Nigerian-American Chamber of Commerce, Nigerian Association of Women Entrepreneurs and other partners to strengthen trade connections.

Oladeinde said manufacturers and entrepreneurs in Aba, a major commercial and manufacturing centre, stood to benefit from improved access to markets across Nigeria and West Africa.

He added that the initiative would support advocacy for a long-term extension of the AGOA, following its reported two-year extension to December 2028.

Oladeinde said the expo’s theme, ‘Deepening U.S – Africa Commercial Ties in the Area of AfCFTA and AGOA’, would provide an opportunity to examine how existing trade frameworks could translate into greater commercial opportunities for African businesses.

He said discussions would cover eight sectors, including agriculture, consumer goods, financial services, insurance and healthcare.

Meanwhile, he disclosed that outstanding Africans would also receive the Medal of Glory Award during the event.

Also, the proposed trade centre and civil society network are expected to be unveiled during the three-day expo in Umuahia.

World.title: COAS Announces Plans To Operationalise Newly Established 83 Division in Benin
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has announced plans by the Nigerian Army to operationalise the newly established 83 Division in Benin City as part of efforts to tackle kidnapping and other emerging security threats in the area.

He reaffirmed the Nigerian Army’s commitment to expanding its force structure and strengthening its operational capabilities to address emerging security challenges across the country.

Lieutenant General Shaibu announced the plan during a courtesy visit to the Governor of Edo State, Senator Monday Okpebholo, at the Government House in Benin City.

Meanwhile, troops of 18 Brigade have rescued 16 abducted persons and recovered weapons, ammunition and logistics from terrorists and kidnappers in Niger State.

A major highlight of the COAS’s visit was his assurance that the newly established 83 Division, with its headquarters in Benin City, would soon become operational.

According to a statement by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, the COAS explained that the Division forms part of the Nigerian Army’s ongoing expansion from eight to 12 divisions.

“The expansion is aimed at strengthening military presence, improving command and control, and enhancing rapid responses to security threats across the country, particularly in Edo State and the wider South-South region,” the COAS said.

The COAS added that his visit was also aimed at assessing operational activities at Headquarters 4 Brigade and commissioning key Army projects, including the Affordable Home Ownership Option for Soldiers (AHOOAS) and Civil-Military Cooperation initiatives designed to improve personnel welfare and strengthen relations with host communities.

In his remarks, Governor Okpebholo commended the Nigerian Army for its professionalism and contributions to peace and security in the state.

He assured the COAS of his administration’s continued support and collaboration in strengthening security and sustaining stability.

“The operationalisation of 83 Division represents a significant milestone in the Nigerian Army’s force expansion drive and its determination to build a more responsive and operationally effective force,” Colonel Anele said.

Meanwhile, troops of 18 Brigade have recorded operational successes in Niger State following intelligence reports on the movement of terrorists from Mashegu Local Government Area towards Rijiyan Nagwamatse in Kontagora Local Government Area.

Acting on the intelligence, the troops established an ambush along suspected terrorist routes.

In a separate statement, the Acting Assistant Director of Army Public Relations, 18 Brigade, Captain Adebayo Adewumi, said the troops made contact with the criminals, who had earlier abducted residents of the area, neutralising an unconfirmed number of them and rescuing 16 victims.

He noted that items recovered during the ambush included two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, three RPG high-explosive anti-personnel bombs, 33 motorcycles, assorted ammunition and N4,105,000 in cash.

“In a related operation on 3 November 2026, troops intercepted terrorists moving from Makuku Village in Sakaba Local Government Area of Kebbi State towards Tungan Kawo in Rijau Local Government Area of Niger State. The troops engaged the criminals in a fierce firefight, forcing them to retreat into the surrounding forest with varying degrees of gunshot wounds.

“A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of five motorcycles, a mobile phone, N644,300 and other sundry items. The 16 rescued victims have received first aid and have been handed over to the appropriate authorities for reunification with their families, while recovered items remain in military custody for further action,” the statement said.

The Commander, 18 Brigade, commended the troops for their gallantry, resilience and commitment to duty, urging them to sustain the operational momentum and intensify efforts to rid the Brigade’s Area of Responsibility of criminal elements.

The development highlights the Nigerian Army’s efforts to strengthen its operational capacity through the expansion of its formations, enhanced military presence and improved responsiveness to security threats. These measures are aimed at protecting communities and disrupting the logistics and activities of criminal networks.

World.title: After 15 Years Building Brands, Aishat Anaekwe Launches Blac Haus
World.content:
After 15 years building brands for major companies, Aishat Anaekwe is venturing into live entertainment with the launch of Blac Haus, a new events outfit aimed at creating a different nightlife experience.

Its debut event, The Frequency, is scheduled for December 15, 2026, at Muri Okunola Park, Lagos, featuring eight DJs performing over nine hours without a headline act.

Anaekwe brings considerable experience in brand management and marketing to the venture. She previously worked with Nigerian Breweries, where she managed Heineken, Life and 33 Export, overseeing major brand campaigns and partnerships. Her career also spans Johnson & Johnson, PZ Cussons and Coronation, where she most recently headed brand and communications. She is also a founding partner of TurnUp, a US-based live-events platform.

Explaining the inspiration behind Blac Haus, Anaekwe says her years working on major entertainment events exposed her to gaps in the live-event experience, particularly long queues and poor crowd management.

“I spent years on the brand side of some of the biggest nights in this country, and I kept seeing the same thing. People paid good money, then spent half the night waiting. I wanted to build the night I would want to buy a ticket for,” she says.

The Frequency will feature an eclectic lineup of DJs, including Berlin-based Kikelomo, DJ Tobzy, Azzi on the Beat, Sunrise (formerly Munachi Abii), Maze x Mxtreme, K.N.D, WeAreAllChemicals and Germany-based DJ Fabiyo.

Rather than centre the event on a headline performer, Blac Haus is placing emphasis on music, lighting and stage production. The DJs will perform from within an illuminated stage structure, with synchronised sound and lighting designed to evolve as the night progresses.

Attendance will be capped at 3,500, which Anaekwe says is a deliberate decision to preserve the experience for guests.

“3,500 is a ceiling, not a target,” she says.

Beyond its debut, she envisions Blac Haus becoming an annual Lagos entertainment event, with plans to expand the platform to international markets.

“Global money has found African artists. It hasn’t yet found African rooms. That’s the opportunity,” she says.

World.title: Nnaji Unveils $4bn Industrialisation Plan for Enugu, Targets 50,000 Jobs
World.content:
Jonathan Eze

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has unveiled an ambitious industrialisation agenda for the state, projecting more than $4 billion in foreign direct investment and the creation of over 50,000 direct and indirect jobs.

Nnaji, who disclosed the plan on Friday in Lagos, identified coal, iron ore and cement as three strategic industrial sectors that would form the foundation of his proposed economic transformation agenda, leveraging Enugu’s abundant natural resources.

He spoke at Alaba International Market, Ojo, where Igbo traders and members of the Auto Spare Parts and Machinery Dealers Association (ASPAMDA) hosted him for an engagement on his vision and development plans for Enugu State.

The PDP candidate said his administration, if elected, would prioritise the establishment of industries capable of processing the state’s natural resources locally, creating employment opportunities, generating revenue and ensuring that host communities benefit directly from the exploitation of their resources.

“My administration will focus on three industries that we expect to attract more than $4 billion in foreign direct investment. These industries will absorb more than 50,000 people in direct and indirect employment.

“We need to help our people. That is what I am interested in. I am not interested in making money as a governor or acquiring wealth. God has helped me already, and it is time for me to help my people and make Enugu work again,” he said.

Reflecting on his political journey, Nnaji recalled that he won a senatorial election in 1999 but voluntarily relinquished the mandate to former Governor of old Anambra State, Chief Jim Nwobodo, whom he considered more experienced and better positioned to serve at the time.

He said his subsequent appointment by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as a minister of the Federal Republic of Nigeria further exposed him to the possibilities of purposeful leadership and people-oriented governance.

On the proposed industrialisation drive, Nnaji identified coal as one of Enugu’s greatest economic assets, arguing that the state could generate substantially more value from the resource through local processing and the development of downstream industries.

He expressed concern over what he described as the uncontrolled extraction and transportation of raw coal from communities around Awhum, particularly the limited economic benefits accruing to the host communities.

According to him, about 100 trailer-loads of coal are transported out of the area daily, with little corresponding development for the communities from which the resource is extracted.

“If you are from Awhum or areas around Awhum where they take coal these days, they just dig our coal and take it out without care for the environment. If you go there at night, you will cry when you see the number of vehicles carrying raw coal away.

“At least 100 trailers of raw coal are trucked away every day from our land, leaving behind no benefit to the community. You can send any of your people to investigate this,” he said.

Nnaji further alleged that the government collects about N250,000 for every truck of coal taken out of the community daily, yet the host communities continue to suffer from inadequate government attention and infrastructure.

He said his administration would reverse the trend by establishing coal-based industries and ensuring that the economic benefits of resource extraction translate into development for the affected communities.

“That is why we want to pay attention to this area by creating coal-related industries, an industry that has many multipliers and added value,” he said.

Explaining the economic opportunities in coal processing, Nnaji said the resource could serve as the raw material for the production of industrial chemicals, including dimethyl ether, methanol, ammonia and urea, with opportunities for further downstream manufacturing.

He noted that the production of methanol and other industrial inputs could attract long-term commercial agreements with international buyers, while investments in ammonia and urea production could position Enugu as an important player in the fertiliser market.

Citing Indorama’s urea production operations as an example of the economic potential of large-scale industrial investments, he argued that similar ventures in Enugu could generate substantial returns for the state and its people.

He said the revenue model would also reduce the state’s dependence on monthly allocations from the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC), while providing resources for infrastructure and other development priorities.

“This is what a thinking government should know. From methanol, if you want to extend it, you can generate other products like polypropylene and polyethylene, which are among the largest-selling commodities in the world,” he added.

Beyond coal, the PDP candidate said Enugu also possessed commercially viable iron ore deposits across parts of Udi, Oji River, Nachi and Nsukka, with some deposits extending towards neighbouring areas of Anambra State.

He said the deposits presented opportunities for iron and steel-related industries, while the state’s limestone and other mineral resources could support cement production and associated manufacturing activities.

Nnaji maintained that even coal alone, if properly harnessed through industrial processing, could become a major economic asset for Enugu, potentially delivering benefits comparable to those associated with crude oil-producing economies.

He attributed his exposure to the economic possibilities of coal-based industrialisation to his ministerial engagements in Malaysia, where he said he visited industrial facilities twice and participated in the commissioning of a plant.

According to him, those experiences reinforced his conviction that Enugu could build a sustainable industrial economy by transforming its natural resources into finished and intermediate products, rather than continuing to export them in their raw form.

He said his vision was to create an economy in which industrial investments generate jobs, stimulate local businesses, expand the state’s revenue base and improve the living standards of residents.

World.title: Teen rugby prodigy dies after battle with meningitis
World.content:
Frans van der Bergh, a 13-year-old rugby prodigy from Springs, has died of suspected meningitis. His death was confirmed by his mother, Jeanine, in the Facebook group, Bid vir Frans.

The teen from Laerskool Christiaan Beyers recently took part in the U13 Craven Week in Bloemfontein.

SPRINGS RUGBY TEEN DIES OF MENINGITIS

In the Facebook group Bid vir Frans, the mother of Frans van der Bergh confirmed his passing on Wednesday, 4 November.



His school, Laerskool Christiaan Beyers, and his rugby club, Valke Laerskole Rugby, also shared a heartfelt tribute to him.

The 13-year-old reportedly contracted meningitis after developing a severe sinus infection several weeks ago.



Frans, who was treated in the ICU of Glenwood Hospital in Benoni, suffered from seizures after developing an infection near his brain. He was administered strong antibiotic medication.

Before his death, a neurosurgeon decided against performing surgery on the teen.

After his death, his mother, Jeanine, confirmed that she had decided to donate Frans’s organs, six of which went to children in dire health circumstances



Jeanine shared in the Facebook group: “Frans has always had an incredibly big love for the people around him. His heart was full of caring, love and a desire to make a difference in the lives of others.

“Even though our hearts break into a million pieces, we find comfort in knowing that our son’s love for others will live on even after his passing.

“My Frans, you always wanted to make a difference in this world. And just look, my child.. You are going to give six other children a chance at a future”



His memorial service will be held on Thursday, 12 November

In June, Frans van der Bergh and the Valke rugby club participated in U13 Craven Week in Bloemfontein. He also played on the first team at his school, Laerskool Christiaan Beyers, where he won several trophies.

WHAT ARE THE SYMPTOMS?

Meningitis in children is a serious condition involving inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It can develop rapidly, particularly bacterial meningitis, and is a medical emergency requiring urgent treatment.



The symptoms include:

High fever with cold hands and feet

Stiff neck

Severe headache

Vomiting or nausea

Confusion and lethargy

Seizures

According to the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD), there were 65 confirmed cases of invasive meningococcal [bacterial] disease recorded in South Africa in the first two quarters of 2026.

World.title: IEC confirms time for 2026 Local Government Election results announcement
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has confirmed when the official results of the 2026 Local Government Elections will be announced. Image: X @IECSouthAfrica

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has confirmed when the official results of the 2026 Local Government Elections will be announced.

The commission plans to announce the election results on Sunday, 8 November from 18:00.

ELECTIONS 2026 | Result: DA wins Nelson Mandela Bay metro



The announcement will bring the national counting process to its formal conclusion following several days of voting, counting and results capturing across the country.

South Africans are now awaiting the final outcome of an election that has delivered significant political shifts, particularly in several major metropolitan municipalities.

Latest numbers

As at the time of publishing, 99% of the votes around the country have been tallied.



The ANC are on track to record the greatest number of votes – but will receive a record low amount of around 30.84%.

In the most recent 2021 elections, the ANC garnered 45.59%.

The Democratic Alliance (DA) will finish second with around 24.6% (21.66% in 2021), with the MK Party in third with roughly 9.66%.



The MK Party were formed in 2023 and therefore did not contest the 2021 elections.

Coalition negotiations expected to follow

The 2026 elections have produced several closely contested councils, with smaller political parties potentially holding the balance of power.

The formal announcement of results will provide the basis for the next stage of negotiations as political parties seek to establish municipal administrations.



For voters, the announcement will confirm the final outcome of an election that will determine who governs South Africa’s municipalities over the next five years.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs will have something to show end of the season, says ex-Sundowns star
World.content:
Former Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder Brent Carelse feels Kaizer Chiefs will have a good season based on how they are playing currently.

Amakhosi went down 2-1 to the Buccaneers at the FNB Stadium last weekend, which saw them drop to fifth in the Betway Premiership.

The former Sundowns and Chippa United midfielder felt Kaizer Chiefs played well despite the loss in the Soweto Derby.



“I thought Chiefs were going to cause an upset because of the way they were playing. I think they did well in the first 30 minutes or so, they looked like a team that wanted to win but unfortunately Pirates came back and took their opportunities,” Carelse told KickOff.

“That was the difference between the two teams. Pirates took their opportunities and Chiefs didn’t. But it was a good game, a good  for South African football but I think Chiefs let it slip.”

Carelse feels Kaizer Chiefs are heading in the right direction

Carelse said Amakhosi are on the right track and will have something to show at the end of the season if they remain consistent.

“Look, the way they (Chiefs) played, there were a lot of positives. If they continue that way they will do well and have something to show come the end of the season, being consistent and playing the way they started the match against Pirates,” he added.

Kaizer Chiefs will play Siwelele in the Carling Knockout Cup knowing a win could get them closer to their first silverware of the season.

World.title: Disability Grant recipient reveals what SASSA still gets wrong after more than five years
World.content:
Erika Fourie has nothing left of her grant by the end of each month. The Western Cape woman, aged 45, has received the SASSA Disability Grant for more than five years.

Fourie shared her experience in The South African’s SASSA grant survey. She lives in a shared family home, where one to two people depend on her income.

Disability Grant helps, but falls short

The Old Age and Disability Grants both rose from R2 310 to R2 400 in April 2026. Fourie receives her payment through a Postbank account each month.



She uses the money for a mix of essentials, including food, transport and other household costs. Fourie says the grant helps, but it is not enough to cover her basic needs.

By month-end, nothing remains. Every rand goes towards keeping her household running until the next payment date.

Unlike many grant recipients, Fourie says no one in her household went without food in the past month. Still, the fixed amount leaves no room for savings or unexpected costs.



Late payments and poor communication

Fourie’s grant has not always arrived smoothly. She has experienced a late or missing payment in the past, a problem that hits hard when a household has no financial buffer.

She rates SASSA’s communication with recipients as poor.

When asked what one thing she would change about SASSA, Fourie chose faster and simpler applications. Her answer reflects a frustration shared by many South Africans who must navigate lengthy processes to access support.



Fourie has never applied for additional government support beyond her Disability Grant. She explained that she did not know what else was available to her.

Grant recipient searching for office work

Unemployment is her biggest financial concern. A steady income would ease the pressure on her grant and give her household more security.

For now, Fourie continues to rely on her monthly Disability Grant while she searches for a way back into the workplace.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: What Springboks’ Italy win means for Nations Championship race
World.content:
The Springboks retain their lead in the Nations Championship's Southern Hemisphere table, with New Zealand trailing on points difference. Image: Springboks (X).

The Springboks remain on course for the Nations Championship final in London.

South Africa thrashed Italy 66-7 on 7 November to bolster their lead in the Southern Hemisphere standings.

New Zealand remain in second place after a bruising 43-21 win over Scotland on Saturday.



Where the Nations Championship race stands

Before Saturday, the Springboks were level with New Zealand in the Nations Championship standings.

The only thing separating the two Southern giants was a points difference of 30.

South Africa’s win in Turin has extended their points difference to +140 after four games.



This means the All Blacks effectively need the Springboks to slip up to reach the final at Twickenham.

Rassie Erasmus’s boys face France in Paris on 13 November, according to the Nations Championship website.

They then have another tough encounter against Ireland in Dublin on 21 November.



The competition wraps up with the finals weekend in London from 27 to 29 November.

A brilliant start to the Nations Championship Northern Series in Italy 👏#Springboks #ForeverGreenForeverGold pic.twitter.com/ZBdemQyr7s — Springboks (@Springboks) November 7, 2026

How things stand in the Northern Hemisphere

Meanwhile, Ireland’s 42-12 thumping of Argentina took them to the top of the Northern Hemisphere table.



However, France can reclaim that position when they host Fiji later tonight (Saturday).

Scotland remain third, having failed to come away with a losing bonus point against the All Blacks.

Elsewhere, Wales must still host Japan, and England are set to welcome Australia.



The Wallabies are third in the Southern Hemisphere, while England are fourth in the Northern Hemisphere.

Italy remain at the bottom of the combined standings with 0 points and a massive PD of -153.

Fiji are not faring much better and are pointless after three games.

World.title: Help keep Table Mountain clean on ‘Take a Hike Day’
World.content:
Mark your calendars, hiking and nature enthusiasts! The Table Mountain Aerial Cableway Company (TMACC) is hosting its annual “Take a Hike Day” initiative next weekend.

This conservation initiative – in partnership with Table Mountain National Park – takes place annually on Table Mountain in Cape Town. The goal is for members of the public to hike up the famous landmark and pick up and dispose of litter as they do so.

Here are all the event details:



The event is slated for Saturday, 14 November 2026. Should the cableway be closed, it will then take place on Sunday, 15 November 2026.

Check-in for pre-registered participants opens at 05:30 and closes at 07:00.

Afterwards, participants will gather at the starting points of three popular hiking routes: Platteklip Gorge Trail, Kloof Corner and the Lower Station Contour Path.

TMACC strongly recommends that the Contour Path is for experienced hikers only.

TABLE MOUNTAIN CONSERVATION TAKES A HIKE

Once you’ve checked in, you will receive a bin bag, water and a wristband (you are encouraged to bring your own gloves and litter pickers). Afterwards, you can embark on your hike.

Whichever route you choose, you can pick up any litter along the way and deposit it into your bin bag.



Once you’ve completed your hike and collected enough litter, you will then head to the Twelve Apostles Terrace, just below the Shop at the Top and TEN67 Eatery. There you can exchange your bin bag for a snack pack and a free ride down the mountain in the cable car.

Take note that hand-ins will end at 12:00.

HOW TO REGISTER

If you’re looking to give back to either Mother Nature or to the Mother City’s beloved mountain – or both! – then this “Take a Hike Day” initiative is just for you.

You can register by signing up here.

In the meantime, you can familiarise yourself with some of Table Mountain’s hiking routes.

World.title: New direct international flights to Cape Town from popular destination
World.content:
Cape Town will get its first direct flights from Australia in 2027, with a new seasonal service connecting the city to Sydney. Image: Qantas

Cape Town is set for a major boost in international connections, with Qantas announcing a new route linking the Mother City to Australia.

The seasonal service will launch in 2027 and is expected to add almost 30 000 seats between South Africa and the destination.

Sydney-Cape Town flights to operate three times a week

The new service, operating as QF89, will launch on 19 October 2027, with flights running until 24 March 2028.



Qantas will operate the route three times a week on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays using its Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner aircraft.

The schedule means passengers will be able to leave Sydney in the morning and arrive in Cape Town on the same day.

Return economy fares start at AUD 2 470 (+/-R28 000).

Almost 30 000 additional seats between Australia and South Africa

The new route is expected to add almost 30 000 seats between Australia and South Africa. It will complement Qantas’ existing direct flights between Perth and Johannesburg, as well as its Sydney-Johannesburg service.

The airline said the new route was made possible by the arrival of additional Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner aircraft in late 2027. These aircraft form part of Qantas’ largest fleet renewal programme in its history.

Qantas International CEO Cam Wallace said there was strong demand for travel between Australia and Cape Town.



He noted that tens of thousands of passengers already use the airline’s Johannesburg flights to connect to Cape Town through partner airlines such as Airlink.

Growing demand from Australian travellers

The new route comes as the number of Australian visitors to South Africa continues to grow.

More than 120 000 Australians visited South Africa in 2025. In June 2026, Australia overtook Germany to become South Africa’s third-largest overseas tourism source market, with arrivals increasing by 19% year on year.

The flights will also make it easier for South Africans living in Australia to visit family and friends back home.

Almost 225 000 South African-born people live in Australia, with around a quarter of them based in New South Wales.

Wesgro CEO Wrenelle Stander said the new connection would create opportunities beyond tourism, including trade, investment and business exchanges between Australia and the Western Cape.

She also added that improved air access would support job creation and growth in the province’s visitor economy.

World.title: R450k per month: Is Percy Tau pricing himself out of the PSL?
World.content:
Former Bafana Bafana winger Percy Tau might have jeopardised his chances of returning to the PSL after revealing his salary expectations.

The 32-year-old winger has been without a club for much of this year and is still looking to revive his football career.

Speaking to Robert Marawa last year, Tau admitted that he would love to return to the PSL but insisted that he would not do so cheaply.



When asked whether he would accept a contract worth R450,000 per month on a two-year deal with an option to extend, Tau responded: “Perfect, yes.”

Percy Tau clubless after leaving Asia

After leaving Vietnam, Tau was linked with a move to Kaizer Chiefs. The former Al Ahly star, however, revealed that Amakhosi had never approached him.

“If that situation were to happen, I would pay attention to it. But there are still other clubs in the PSL. I mean, I played for Sundowns, so I cannot write them off. It’s a team that I played for, I won and I’ve got so much love for the team and the fans.

“If Sundowns were not to offer me a contract and Chiefs does, then okay, it won’t be my fault but theirs that I’ve gone to join Chiefs. But I’ll listen to anybody. Let’s not rule out Orlando Pirates or even Stellenbosch.”

Percy Tau looking for an offer

Tau added that his decision would ultimately depend on which club offers him a contract.

“People might say that (that they won’t be able to afford him), but now that I’m here I can speak up for myself. I’m very reasonable, so whenever I speak about my contract dealings, I’m not going to ask what I know you are not going to offer me.”



A monthly salary of R450,000 would likely limit Tau’s options, with only a handful of PSL heavyweights potentially able to meet such demands.

However, even clubs like Pirates, Chiefs and Sundowns might be reluctant to commit that kind of money to a 32-year-old winger whose best years could be behind him.

Many supporters believe Percy Tau needs to lower his financial expectations significantly if he wants to secure a return to South African football and get his career back on track.

What salary should Tau demand?

World.title: Nelson Mandela Bay ward councillor fatally shot
World.content:
MOTHERWELL - A 45-year-old male was shot and killed in NU9 in Motherwell on Saturday.

The man is believed to be a United Democratic Movement (UDM) councillor.

According to police, a murder case been opened.

Suspects and a motive are still under investigation.

World.title: 5 wards recounted by IEC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has ordered the recount of votes in five wards.

The affected wards are in the City of Tshwane, Mangaung Metropolitan Municipality, Thaba Chweu Local Municipality and Breede Valley Municipality.

IEC Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Mosotho Moepya says the assigned seats in the provisional results may change as a result of the recount.

ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula said on Saturday that it had lodged disputes with the IEC and was able to win back wards from their disputes. Other parties, including the MK Party have also lodged disputes with the Commission that are being investigated.

World.title: 'This has been a catastrophic outcome' - Fikile Mbalula
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - "This has been a catastrophic outcome for the ANC," says secretary-general Fikile Mbalula.

Speaking on the sidelines of the preliminary local government results on Saturday. Chief Electoral Officer Mosotho Moepya said that the IEC hope to have the final results on Sunday.

Mbalula said the interim results in the country's municipalities and metros are catastrophic for the liberation movement.

Mbalula says while the party will not be making any hasty decisions, they will put the elections outcome to the national conference in 2027.

The ANC lost control of six of the country's eight metros.
