World.title: Musokotwane presents k284.8 billion 2027 budget
World.content:
Minister of Finance and National Planning Situmbeko Musokotwane has presented a proposed National Budget of 284.8 billion kwacha for the year 2027, equivalent to 28.4 percent of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Dr Musokotwane says 2027 will be highly financed through domestic revenues of about K233.7 billion, representing 82.1 percent of the total budget.

Speaking when he presented the 2027 national budget in Parliament today, Dr Musokotwane added another source of financing will be borrowing from domestic and external sources amounting to K41.9 billion, representing 14.7 percent of the total budget.

Dr Musokotwane highlighted one of the government’s strategic focus since 2021 has been to strengthen fiscal sustainability through improved resource mobilisation and expenditure rationalisation.

Presenting the 2027 National budget expenditure, Dr Musokotwane revealed that about 90.5 billion kwachas will go towards general public services, 75.9 billion to economic affairs, while over K38.2 billion kwacha will be spent on education, a sector that has been given the highest allocation of the total budget at 13.4 percent.

Meanwhile, the health sector has been allocated K30.3 billion, representing 10.6 percent of the Budget on the health function.

To strengthen social protection and reduce vulnerability, Dr Musokotwane proposed an expenditure of K16.2 billion or 5.7 percent of the Budget, of which K10.4 billion will be spent on the Social Cash Transfer programme to support over 1.6 million beneficiary households up from 1.5 million in the 2026 Budget.

“The monthly transfer will be increased to K450 for eligible beneficiary households and K650 for households with eligible persons with disabilities. K5.2 billion will be spent on the public service pension funds to reduce waiting time from retirement to when the pension is paid,” he said.

As part of the government’s commitment to strengthen domestic revenues, Dr Musokotwane proposed adjustments in various taxation including the Value Added Tax rate that he proposed to adjust from 16 percent to 16.5.

The Minister also proposed to increase Corporate Income Tax rates by 5 percentage points on all income currently taxed at 20 percent and below.

“To rationalise the company tax regime which is currently characterised by preferential rates and arbitrage, I propose to increase Corporate Income Tax rates by 5 percentage points on all income currently taxed at 20 percent and below. This measure will ensure neutrality, fairness and alignment of the tax system,” he stated.

He also proposed to increase withholding tax on dividends paid by mining companies to 15 percent from zero percent, noting that this will align with tax treatment of dividends distributed by companies in other sectors.

Other tax adjustments by Dr Musokotwane was the proposal to introduce a top marginal rate of 39.5 percent PAYE tax for individuals earning above K37,000 per month.

He explained that those earning K37,000 per month and below will continue to be taxed under the current regime and will therefore not be affected by this measure.

Meanwhile, to lower capital costs and enhance Zambia’s competitiveness as a high value tourism destination, Dr Musokotwane proposed to suspend customs duty on safari vehicles, hospitality equipment and communications infrastructure.

The theme for the 2027 Budget is: Grow Zambia: From Stabilisation to Unlocking Opportunities, Creating Jobs and Improving Livelihoods for All.

The Budget presented provides a clear policy direction with specific interventions to achieve the Grow Zambia Agenda and will require concerted efforts from various stakeholders.

World.title: Engineers challenged to catalyze Grow Zambia Agenda
World.content:
Government has urged engineers to play a pivotal role in contributing to the achievement of the Grow Zambia Agenda through quality infrastructure development.

Ministry of Infrastructure and Urban Development Permanent Secretary

Albert Malama, said infrastructure remains a key driver of economic growth, and engineers are at the centre of delivering the projects that will transform the country.

Mr Malama said this when he officiated at the second annual public forum for the Association of Consulting Engineers of Zambia (ACEZ) on construction contracts held at Urban Hotel in Lusaka.

He said the government recognises the important role that professional bodies such as ACEZ play in supporting national development, and values their expertise and technical guidance in the infrastructure sector.

“Government recognises the important role that professional bodies such as the Association of Consulting Engineers of Zambia play in supporting national development, and values their expertise and technical guidance,” Mr Malama said.

He noted that the successful delivery of infrastructure requires collaboration, mutual understanding and clearly defined responsibilities among different stakeholders.

Mr Malama commended ACEZ for bringing together engineers, lawyers, quantity surveyors, architects, procurement specialists and contractors to discuss the distinctive nature of construction contracts.

He said challenges in the construction industry cannot be addressed by one profession in isolation, and the forum had created an opportunity for a more balanced and holistic discussion.

“A project can encounter serious challenges if the contractual arrangements are poorly understood or inadequately administered,” Mr Malama said.

He cited issues relating to risk allocation, payment obligations, variations, extensions of time, design responsibilities and dispute resolution as having significant implications on project delivery and quality.

Mr Malama urged engineers to appreciate the distinctive nature of construction contracts, as this will ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget and to the required quality key to achieving the Grow Zambia Agenda.

The forum was held under the ACEZ core values of transparency, accountability, dynamism, innovation, equity and sustainability.

Meanwhile ACEZ president Trephor Musonda appreciated government for the support shown to the association.

He said the association was encouraged to receive positive response from government to officiate the event.

World.title: Africa: CANEX Opens Doors for Gambian Fashion Entrepreneurs Seeking Global Recognition
World.content:
For Gambian fashion entrepreneur Ndey Bassin Faye, building an internationally recognised brand begins with empowering women, celebrating local culture, and embracing African-made textiles. At CANEX WKND 2026 in Lagos, she and fellow entrepreneurs are looking beyond borders to build connections that could help transform their businesses and the continent's fashion industry.

When Ndey Bassin Faye discusses her fashion brand's global expansion, she also refers to promoting Gambian culture internationally.

The founder of Bassin's Couture, established in 2016, is one of three Gambian fashion and tailoring entrepreneurs, Mariama Jallow, Ndey Bassin, and Ida, attending the Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND) 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria.Their attendance is sponsored by the Andandorr programme, with support from EU YEP – Tourism and Creative Industries.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

For entrepreneurs, the four-day gathering is more than an opportunity to showcase their work. It is a chance to meet potential partners, connect with suppliers, learn from industry experts, and explore new markets for their businesses.

At the heart of Faye's work is a commitment to women and girls. Through Bassin's Couture, she uses fashion not only as a business opportunity but also as a means of empowering women to pursue entrepreneurship while promoting Gambian culture through design.

Like many African fashion entrepreneurs, she faces challenges that extend beyond creativity and craftsmanship. One of the biggest obstacles is accessing materials.

"One of the challenges we face is the difficulty of sourcing diverse fabrics, particularly those outside of Gambian culture," says Faye.

She highlights the challenges of sourcing materials from other African countries, noting that, in some instances, it is easier to access supplies from Europe and China than from within the continent.

While the continent is home to rich textile traditions, cotton-producing countries, and a growing community of designers, connecting the different parts of the value chain remains difficult.

For Faye and her partners, CANEX offers an opportunity to help bridge some of those gaps. She hopes to use the gathering to establish relationships with suppliers, meet fellow designers, and explore collaborations that could strengthen her business and expand its reach.

"I want us to go international. I want our brand to be seen and to be known internationally," she says.

She also wishes to see more African materials incorporated into African fashion.

The Gambia has a tradition of handweaving, and Faye is proud to work with locally grown cotton. By incorporating hand-woven fabrics into her designs, she is taking practical steps towards building a fashion business that promotes local resources while celebrating the country's cultural identity.

Building a fashion industry that supports African designers

The challenges facing entrepreneurs such as Faye are part of the bigger conversations at CANEX, particularly during different masterclasses offered by experts in the textile industry. In a masterclass about how African fashion businesses could strengthen their marketing management and expand into global markets, luxury brand consultant Anita Ehui highlighted the structural difficulties that continue to affect African fashion businesses, particularly in manufacturing, textiles, sourcing, quality control, and pricing.

"I think we have a big manufacturing problem, whether in textiles or production itself, and that makes things difficult," Ehui said.

She explained that while many designers aspire to manufacture their products entirely on the continent, achieving this can be challenging due to limitations in material availability, production capacity, and quality.

Designers are often forced to make compromises, whether on quality, pricing, or design, because the necessary resources and infrastructure are not always readily available. Ehui encouraged entrepreneurs to prioritise African sourcing and production wherever possible, arguing that increasing demand for locally manufactured products could help strengthen the continent's manufacturing ecosystem.

However, she also cautioned against some common mistakes made by emerging fashion businesses.

One common mistake is overcomplicating business decisions, such as designing and selling products based solely on personal preferences rather than genuine customer demand.

For African fashion businesses aiming for growth, identifying the correct market is crucial. Instead of trying to appeal to everyone, entrepreneurs should understand their target customers, their desires, and the most effective ways to communicate the value of their products.

She highlighted how CANEX provides an important platform for designers to connect with potential customers and fosters conversations that can lead to partnerships and new ideas.

"CANEX is giving fashion designers a platform. It is also connecting some of the brands with customers," she stated.

She added that gatherings like CANEX create opportunities for collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and has potential to expose creators to new perspectives.

"When we gather at CANEX, there is always a conversation that can spark a collaboration or even open your mind to something new," she said.

Close 

From Local to Global Markets

For the three Gambian entrepreneurs, these conversations are particularly important as they plan the next phase of their businesses. Access to industry experts through masterclasses, exposure to other African brands and suppliers, and opportunities to engage with potential business partners offer valuable insights into building sustainable fashion enterprises.

Organised by the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) and hosted by the Federal Government of Nigeria, CANEX WKND brings together leading African and diaspora creatives, investors, and policymakers from various sectors including music, film, fashion, sport, publishing, gastronomy, and visual arts.

The four-day event is designed to facilitate partnerships, encourage investment, and expand access to international markets for Africa's creative industries.

For Faye, the journey towards that future is already underway. The vision is to reach international markets without losing the local identity that makes the brand distinctive. Faye and Ehui agree that African fashion can compete globally, but the continent must first make it easier for African creatives to work, source, produce, and grow together.

World.title: Africa: A Just Energy Transition Cannot Leave Water Behind
World.content:
guest column

As Africa weighs how to power its industries and expand electricity access, water must be part of the equation. Ahead of COP31, Dr Jonty Cogger and Paul Wani Lado draw on South Africa’s experience to argue that a just energy transition must test proposed fossil fuel investments against their water demands—and protect the communities whose supplies could come under pressure.

South Africa's energy debate often focuses on electricity supply, energy security and economic growth. Oil and gas infrastructure is increasingly presented as part of the answer to these challenges. This framing hides a key test for any proposed development: whether its promised benefits justify the strain it will put on scarce water, and whether affected communities will carry an unfair share of the costs.

South Africa is a water-scarce country. Local communities increasingly struggle with unreliable water services, crumbling infrastructure and growing demand for water. Given this, plans to expand fossil fuel infrastructure need far closer scrutiny than they usually get.

Climate change makes matters worse by bringing more heat, more drought and less predictable rainfall. Writing for the Endangered Wildlife Trust, Dr Ian Little warns that a strong El Niño during the 2026/2027 summer season could bring below-average rainfall, higher temperatures, lower river flows and less water reaching dams. It could also cut crop yields, strain livestock farming and increase the demand for irrigation. In a country where water and food systems are already under pressure, this combination of risks shows why water security, food security and climate policy must shape any decision to expand fossil fuels further.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Oil and gas are not just a matter of energy policy. Expanding them affects the environment, the climate, water security and the rights of local communities. Yet debates about new gas infrastructure tend to focus on the promise of energy and industrial growth, rather than taking a hard look at the environmental costs and the local communities that may pay them.

Calling gas part of a just energy transition does not make it just. More electricity or investment does not, on its own, tell us who benefits, who pays the environmental, social and economic costs, and whether those costs can be avoided. Nor does calling gas a transitional fuel solve the problems of building fossil fuel infrastructure that will last for decades.

The risk is that South Africa repeats an old development model under the banner of a new transition where powerful economic interests reap the benefits of resource-hungry industry and local communities are left to deal with the environmental costs.

Water makes this contradiction especially clear because it links national energy choices to direct local effects. A project sold as improving energy security may make others less secure if it competes with households, farmers and nature for a limited and increasingly unreliable supply of water.

Putting water at the centre of the just transition means treating it as a firm limit on development, not just one factor to consider after energy and investment decisions have been made. Government should assess from the outset how proposed fossil fuel and industrial projects would affect how much water is available, its quality, and the ability of communities and ecosystems to cope as the climate worsens.

As government considers expanding gas infrastructure and attracting energy-intensive industries, it must account for how much water these developments will need. The critical question is whether the combined demand from multiple developments, together with existing uses and worsening climate pressures, can be met without harming communities' access to water, the health of ecosystems or the needs of other lawful water users.

This scrutiny must be based on evidence that is public and can be independently checked. Decision-makers should disclose how much water proposed projects need, where that water would come from, the condition and capacity of the water systems involved, what would happen in a drought, and the combined demands of existing and likely future developments.

The same scrutiny must apply to the infrastructure needed to support these developments, including pipelines, power stations and related industrial facilities. Decisions about these projects cannot ignore the water systems and communities they depend on.

Close 

Local communities should not have to face less reliable water supply so that fossil fuel expansion and industrial growth can go ahead. If government is serious about a just energy transition, it must require open water assessments that account for climate change and the combined impact of all projects before approving new developments, and it must show that communities will continue to have enough reliable water. Economic benefits should not be assumed to outweigh environmental and social costs; they must be weighed against them.

Dr Jonty Cogger is a public interest attorney at the Centre for Environmental Rights whose work focuses on using legal strategies to challenge pollution and climate change.

Paul Wani Lado is an attorney at the Centre for Environmental Rights where his work focuses on the extractives industry, particularly mining and upstream oil and gas projects.

World.title: Somalia: Court Says President Term Extension Unlawful
World.content:
Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on Thursday that the extension of the president's term by one year, which sparked violent clashes with the opposition, was "unlawful".

President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term ended in May, but his government declared a "transition period" that gave him an extra year in office to prepare for the first nationwide democratic elections, which are due in April and May 2027.

Mohamud has argued this was legal under amendments to the constitution passed by parliament in March, but that vote was boycotted by opposition parties and regional leaders.

On Thursday, the Supreme Court ruled that the amendments did not apply to his current term, and that he should have left office in May.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Mohamud announced late Wednesday that he was dismissing the chief justice, Bashe Yusuf Ahmed, and appointing a replacement.

There were unconfirmed reports that Ahmed was under arrest on Thursday.

The presidency's statement, posted on Facebook, did not reference the imminent decision on the constitution, saying only that the dismissal was due to "concerns... about the need for an efficient and fair judiciary".

The court rejected the dismissal in a separate statement, saying the move was designed "to obstruct the administration of justice in the constitutional case filed before the Supreme Court".

"The dismissal announced in the statement published on the Presidency's Facebook page is null and void," it added.

World.title: South Africa: The Honeybadger's Revenge - Former Minister Dion George's Nuclear War Over SA's Captive Lions
World.content:
The former South African environment minister is prepared to back international economic pressure against his own country to shut down the 'disgusting' captive lion industry.

Dion George has lost his ministry, abandoned the political party he served for 30 years and returned to a career in financing that, he says, pays him three times as much for half the time.

And with more time to kill, he has decided to make life considerably more difficult for the people who fired him.

Pending George's ultimatums to current Environment Minister David Maynier, the captive lion trade would be dragged before the court of international opinion, even if the country pays an economic price.

"If they will not work together and get rid of this evil thing, I will help the lobby in the UK that is pushing hard to ban all import trophies," he warns. "I will throw myself behind that."

In an interview with Daily Maverick, the former minister not only levels previously reported accusations at the Democratic Alliance (DA) - that is, what he describes as a party cabal defending "un-African" commercial wildlife interests.

He also believes "fear" is stopping Maynier from signing off on the agreed ban on new captive lion facilities.

"If professional hunters do it, you know, and it's fair chase? Fine," George concedes. But then he hovers his crosshairs over lion-bone...

World.title: South Africa: Resident Evil - A Horror Video Game Adaptation With a Wicked Sense of Humour
World.content:
While it's probably too far removed from its source material narratively to please hardcore fans who want to see their favourite Resident Evil characters and storylines on the big screen, Zach Cregger's reboot successfully captures the spirit, the rules and the essence of the game franchise that spawned it.

It's an opinion that will probably get you cancelled - at least among ardent fans. But as much immersive fun as the Resident Evil video games are, story-wise they're pretty absurd.

Around for 30 years now, Capcom's survival horror franchise has run unconstrained with the core concept that sets it apart from other zombie media: in its universe, the undead are the product of pharmaceutical experimentation, with various virus strains (the t-Virus being the most famous) mutating some of the infected into "superior", unstoppable beings.

There have been cults, clones, vampires, babies turned to crystal, presidential rescue missions, and toxic moss, and that doesn't even count for stylised characters like absolute unit Chris Redfield, always-in-shades-and-leather Albert Wesker, and Leon S. Kennedy with his boy band hairstyle.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The point is that Resident Evil lore is ridiculous, and any attempt to faithfully translate one of its signature convoluted narratives into live-action entertainment will trip over that blocker.

It's the exact fate that befell 2021's B-grade Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City. Meanwhile, Paul W. S. Anderson chose to jettison fidelity and moody survival horror for his six Resident Evil movies, which went the gory sci-fi-infused action route instead. And the less...

World.title: Ghana/Liberia: Black Challenge Edge Liberia 1-0 in Final World Cup Friendly
World.content:
Substitute Yahaya Yussif scored the only goal of the game as the national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, defeated their Liberian counterparts 1-0 in an international friendly at the La McDan Park on Wednesday.

The match, which served as the final preparatory test for both sides ahead of the 2026 World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF) World Cup in Mexico, got off to a lively start, with the visitors showing physicality and defensive solidity to contain Ghana's attacking threat.

Six minutes into the game, skipper Richard Arthur Opentil set up Fusieni Iddi, who shot weakly into the arms of goalkeeper Frances Fallah.

Three minutes later, Liberian skipper Matthew Joe tested Ghana goalkeeper Atsu Abor with a long-range effort, which the latter handled with ease.



The first half ended with Ghana slightly on top in terms of play, but the hosts failed to find the back of the net.

After the break, Black Challenge head coach Stephen Richard Obeng introduced Mubarak Mohammed and Yahaya Yussif in the closing stages of the game to add more bite to the team's attack.

With five minutes remaining, Mohammed threaded a through ball from his own half, which found an unmarked Yahaya in front of goal. The substitute made no mistake, lobbing the ball over the onrushing Fallah to score the only goal of the game.

The Black Challenge team is expected to leave Ghana for Mexico this weekend via Turkey for the final phase of preparations ahead of the tournament, which runs from November 13 to 22.

World.title: Ghana: W Sports Int'l Donates Sports Equipment to Legon Presec
World.content:
W Sports International last Thursday donated sports kits to the Presbyterian Boys' Senior High School (PRESEC), Legon, under its sports sponsorship programme.

The items included jerseys, soccer uniforms, polo shirts and balls. The donation forms part of efforts to modernise sports in Ghana's second-cycle institutions and create opportunities for young talents to excel beyond the classroom.

PRESEC Legon is the first senior high school in the Greater Accra Region to benefit from the organisation's sports kit sponsorship programme.

The event was attended by the Minister of Sports and Recreation, Mr Kofi Adams; Dr Ernest Ofori Sarpong, Global President of Odadee and Board Chairman of PRESEC; the Headmaster of PRESEC, Mr David Odjija; members of the Odadee fraternity; teachers and students.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Presenting the items, the Chairman of W Sports International, Nana Bediako Brogya Sarpong, who is the Dompiahene of the Agogo Asante Akyem Traditional Area and a former student of Prempeh College, urged schools to look beyond traditional rivalries and support the collective development of Ghanaian students.

He acknowledged the rivalry between PRESEC Legon and Prempeh College during the National Maths and Science Quiz and sporting competitions but said such healthy competition should never become a barrier to recognising excellence or supporting one another.

World.title: Ghana: Black Rock Belongs to Nungua - Mankralo
World.content:
The Office of the Nungua Mankralo has rebuffed claims by the Tema and Sanshie clans that the location of Angmu T3 (The Meridian Rock) falls under their authority.

According to the Mankralo, available records, court rulings and customary evidence all point to the fact that the site where the rock is located falls under the jurisdiction and authority of Nungua.

The claims follow a recent outburst by the Sanshie Clan of Tema that the Gborbu Wulomo had no right to perform customary rites around the rock because it falls directly under the authority of Tema.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

However, at a press conference in Nungua on Tuesday, the Nungua Mankralo, ShwÉÉnÉtalÉ Têstê Nii Bortey Kofi Frankwa, said the Black Rock was among the 99 deities of Nungua Kple Spirituality.

He said the annual Djenten rite was an established Nungua tradition performed exclusively by the Gborbu Wulomo Shitse, the town's spiritual head, whose customary responsibilities included conducting important sacred rites for the community's deities.

The office cited Professor M.J. Field's 1937 publication, Religion and Medicine of the Ga People, which it said associated all 99 Nungua deities with the Nuumo Gorbu Temple, known locally as Koomli, in Nungua tradition.

It also relied on Field's Social Organisation of the Ga People, published in 1940 and widely cited, which identified the Gborbu Wulomo Shitse as the traditional timekeeper responsible for announcing the town's rites and festivals.

Further evidence, it said, came from Carl Christian Reindorf's 1895 publication, History of the Gold Coast and Asante, which identified Borkete Lawe as the priest of Angmu, supporting Nungua's account of its spiritual custodianship and ritual authority.

The statement also cited a Bureau of Ghana Languages publication and a book by Dr Joseph Nii Abakar Mensah as documentary records affirming the Gborbu Wulomo Shitse's association with Angmu and the annual Djenten rite.

It rejected claims that Angmu and Oshwe were the same deity, saying Angmu was known in Nungua Kple tradition as Sebrebedu, while Oshwe Yaado was a separate deity with distinct spiritual and customary responsibilities.

On the boundary dispute, the office cited an 1892 judgement by Chief Justice Hutchinson and a 1904 ruling by Crowther, which it said recognised Nungua's right of access to Angmu, historically described as the Black Rock in the sea.

Close 

It argued that the 1952 compulsory acquisition for Tema Township and Port altered administrative arrangements but did not extinguish traditional boundaries or customary rights, stressing that administrative jurisdiction did not establish traditional ownership.

The office further disputed claims that Professor Field placed the Tema-Nungua boundary at Asokplotsonaa, saying page 87 of her book contained no such statement and instead discussed Ataa Sakumo's historical connection with Nungua.

It also pointed to the 2016 Tema Port expansion, saying the Nungua Traditional Authority was consulted and its permission sought before work began, which it considered further recognition of Nungua's traditional interest in the area.

World.title: Is someone already using your identity? Check these 8 places
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

When people think about identity theft, they often start with a credit report or bank statement. Those are important places to look, but they are not the only ones. Someone using your identity may be trying to open a phone line, start utility service, use medical benefits or create a payment plan that never appears on your usual accounts.

The warning signs of identity theft can be easy to miss, especially when fraudulent activity happens outside your primary financial accounts. You do not need to investigate every record today. Start with these eight places, focusing first on accounts that could cause the most damage.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

SOMEONE COULD HAVE OPENED AN ACCOUNT IN YOUR NAME. CHECK NOW

1. Bank accounts, credit cards and payment apps

Review checking, savings, credit card, investment, retirement and payment-app activity for transactions you do not recognize. Look beyond purchases. A new external bank connection, authorized user, payment method, mailing address or phone number can also signal an unauthorized account change. Turn on transaction and security alerts wherever your financial institution offers them. If you find an unfamiliar transaction, contact the institution through its official website or the number on your statement. Do not use a number from a suspicious text or email.

2. Credit reports and new inquiries

Check all three major credit reports for accounts, hard inquiries, collections, addresses or employers you do not recognize. A fraudulent credit card, personal loan or retail-financing account may appear here even when your checking account looks normal. Use AnnualCreditReport.com to access your reports. You can currently request free online credit reports from Equifax, Experian and TransUnion once a week. An unfamiliar entry does not automatically mean fraud. Some lenders operate under different business names. Verify questionable information with the company before disputing it.

Pro tip: Consider freezing your credit with all three bureaus. Credit freezes are free, do not affect your credit score and can make it harder for someone to open new credit accounts in your name.

3. Buy now, pay later and retail accounts

Buy now, pay later services and store-financing accounts can be easy to overlook because they may not feel like traditional credit cards. Check services you have used for unfamiliar orders, payment plans, saved addresses or account-opening messages. Some buy now, pay later loans may not appear on your traditional credit reports. Reporting practices vary by provider and loan type. Search your inbox for purchase confirmations, shipping notices and payment reminders you did not expect. Open the retailer's official app or type its web address yourself rather than clicking a link in an unexpected message.

4. Phone and mobile-carrier accounts

Your phone number can provide access to other accounts because it may receive verification codes and password-reset messages. Review your carrier account for unfamiliar devices, lines, eSIMs, upgrades, address changes or changes to your account PIN. A sudden loss of cellular service can be an early warning sign of a SIM swap, although outages and equipment problems can have other explanations. Contact your carrier through an official channel if the change is unexpected.

Pro tip: Ask your carrier about account PINs, port-out protection and SIM-swap security features. These safeguards may help prevent someone from transferring your number without authorization.

5. Utilities and household services

Review electric, gas, water, internet and other household-service accounts. Someone using your name or personal information may try to start service, change an account or leave an unpaid balance behind. Utility fraud may not appear on your credit report immediately. A bill, welcome email, service appointment or shutoff notice for an account you did not request is worth investigating. You can also request a report from the National Consumer Telecom & Utilities Exchange (NCTUE). This specialty reporting service collects information from participating phone, pay-TV and utility companies. You are entitled to one free NCTUE report every 12 months upon request. It may reveal accounts or service requests missing from your traditional credit reports, although it does not cover every provider. If you find an unfamiliar account, note the date, address and service details. Then contact the company and ask which information was used to open or change the account.

6. Medical and insurance records

Look for explanations of benefits, medical bills, prescription notices or insurance communications related to care you did not receive. Medical identity theft can create an unexpected bill, but it can also place incorrect information in your medical record. For example, someone may use your insurance information to obtain treatment, leaving behind records that could affect future care or insurance claims. If something looks unfamiliar, contact the provider or insurer directly and ask for the records connected to the claim. Do not ignore a small bill simply because the amount seems insignificant. The inaccurate medical information may be a bigger concern.

7. Government, tax and employment records

Watch for notices from the IRS, Social Security Administration or a state benefits agency that do not match your situation. Examples include income reported by an unfamiliar employer, a tax return you did not file or unemployment benefits claimed in your name. You can review tax information through your IRS online account. You can also check your earnings history through your "my Social Security" account. If you notice unfamiliar earnings, contact the Social Security Administration about correcting your record.

Pro tip: Consider requesting an IRS Identity Protection PIN. This free, six-digit number helps prevent someone else from filing a federal tax return using your Social Security number. You can learn more at IRS.gov.

Always use official government websites to review or report suspicious activity. If an unexpected message claims to come from an agency, do not follow its links. Find the agency's website independently.

8. Email, social accounts and recovery settings

Your email and social accounts may not show a financial loss, but they can reveal whether someone is trying to take over your digital identity. Review recent sign-ins, sent messages, forwarding rules, recovery addresses, trusted devices and connected apps. Email deserves special attention because someone with access to your inbox may be able to reset passwords for other accounts. If you see unfamiliar access, change your password from a trusted device, sign out unfamiliar sessions and enable stronger multifactor authentication. Where available, use an authenticator app, passkey or security key rather than relying only on text-message verification codes.

IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT

How to check without making it a full-time job

Spread the review across four short sessions:

Session 1: Check email, banking and phone account settings.

Session 2: Review credit reports and buy now, pay later accounts.

Session 3: Examine utilities, phone-service records and medical claims.

Session 4: Review government records, tax information and employment history.

If nothing looks unusual, record the date of your review. The goal is to recognize unfamiliar activity, not question every legitimate bill. However, do not wait for a scheduled review if you receive a suspicious account alert or discover a potentially fraudulent transaction. Investigate those warnings immediately.

How to tell whether an alert deserves attention

An unfamiliar message does not always mean identity theft. A lender may use a business name you do not recognize, a family member may have used a shared device or a service provider may have changed its billing name. Look for related warning signs. A new account combined with an unfamiliar address, phone change or collection notice deserves immediate attention. Even a single unauthorized transaction or account opening warrants investigation. When you are unsure, compare the record with your own statements and contact the company to explain the mismatch. Do not confirm sensitive personal details to an unexpected caller. Contact the company yourself using a verified number.

What to save when you find something unusual

Keep the original bill, email or letter, but do not click links inside an unexpected message. Write down the date, company name, account or service involved and the first sign that something was wrong. If you call, record the department, case number and follow-up date. For credit issues, save relevant copies of all three reports. For phone, bank or email issues, keep account-change notices and screenshots. Store these records securely so you can refer to them when speaking with the company, a credit bureau or an identity theft recovery specialist.

If the account is old or the name looks unfamiliar

Do not assume an unfamiliar record is fraudulent simply because you do not recognize the company name. A lender, utility provider or collection agency may use a parent-company name. Contact the organization using verified contact information. Ask for the date the account was opened, the address associated with it and the steps required to confirm whether it belongs to you. If the company confirms the account is fraudulent, ask for a fraud case number and written instructions. Then add the issue to your records and check whether related activity appears elsewhere.

How identity monitoring can help protect against identity theft

Checking your accounts regularly is a smart first step, but identity theft can happen between reviews. Identity monitoring tools can help by watching for certain changes involving your personal information and alerting you when something suspicious appears.

Some services monitor credit activity, financial accounts, personal information found in data breaches and certain types of account openings. Depending on the service, you may receive alerts about unfamiliar credit inquiries, changes to your personal information or possible misuse of your identity.

What to look for in identity monitoring services

Not all identity monitoring services offer the same protection. Before signing up, consider these features:

Credit monitoring: Alerts you to certain changes to your credit reports, including new accounts and inquiries.

Financial account alerts: Helps identify unusual transactions or changes to connected financial accounts.

Personal information monitoring: Looks for certain exposures of your personal information, including data found in known breaches.

Identity restoration assistance: Some services provide specialists who can help you navigate the recovery process after identity theft.

Reimbursement coverage: Certain paid plans offer coverage for eligible identity theft expenses or stolen funds, subject to limits and exclusions.

One advantage of using an identity monitoring service is having someone keeping watch for suspicious activity even when you are not actively checking your accounts. Depending on the provider and plan, these services can monitor multiple sources of information and send alerts when something needs your attention. Some also provide dedicated restoration specialists who can help guide you through the recovery process if your identity is stolen.

A paid identity monitoring service may be worth considering if you want more comprehensive monitoring and additional support when problems arise. Look for a plan that covers the types of activity most relevant to you and offers timely alerts. While no service can catch every form of identity theft, combining professional monitoring with your existing account security settings can give you an additional layer of protection. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com

What to do if you find something unfamiliar

Contact the company: Use its official website or a verified number and ask for its fraud department.

Verify the activity: Ask which account, order, claim or service is connected to your information.

Secure your accounts: Change compromised or reused passwords, update security settings and ask the company to close or freeze fraudulent accounts.

Protect your credit: Consider freezing your credit with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. You can also place a free fraud alert by contacting one bureau, which must notify the other two.

Report identity theft: Visit IdentityTheft.gov when appropriate to file a report and receive a personalized recovery plan.

Keep documentation: Store confirmation numbers, names, relevant correspondence and follow-up dates in one secure place.

Pro tip: Start with the four highest-impact places: If you only have a few minutes, check your email, bank accounts, phone account and credit reports first. Those areas can help reveal whether someone is trying to access your information, move money, receive verification codes or open new credit. A clean credit report does not rule out identity theft, so return to the other four places when you have time.

YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES

Kurt's key takeaways

I think one of the biggest mistakes people make with identity theft is assuming that a clean credit report means they're in the clear. Someone could be using your information to open a phone line, get medical care or run up a utility bill, and you might not find out until much later. I'd start by checking your email, bank accounts and wireless carrier settings. Then pull your free credit reports and take a closer look at places you might normally overlook. I'm also a big believer in freezing your credit before there's a problem. It's free, and you can temporarily lift the freeze when you need to apply for credit. Identity monitoring can provide another layer of protection, but no service can monitor everything. That's why it's important to keep an eye on your accounts, too. The sooner you spot an unfamiliar account or transaction, the sooner you can start limiting the damage.

Have you ever discovered an unfamiliar account, bill or charge that made you suspect someone was using your identity? What tipped you off? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

World.title: Built from Scratch: How a rented kitchen and hand-squeezed fruit became a versatile mixer
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Johnna Rossbach never expected to become an entrepreneur. After spending 15 years in a career that left little room for creativity, she found the motivation to build something of her own after becoming a mother.

"I wanted to show my daughters what it looks like to be empowered, and that if you’re not happy with something, change it," Rossbach said.

Rossbach loved cocktails, but she was disappointed by the mixers on store shelves. They often featured similar flavors, contained ingredients she wanted to avoid and required too much preparation.

CEO SUNDAY: AVELO AIRLINES CEO REVEALS THE HABIT HE CREDITS FOR HIS SUCCESS

That's when she created Mixly.

Rossbach drew on her background in marketing and communications and teamed up with Megan Sather, who brought design expertise to the venture. Together, they created a line of fruit-forward cocktail mixers made with real ingredients.

A shaky start

The very first night the team began working on Mixly, just about everything that could go wrong did. They started at 4 p.m. and didn't finish until 3 a.m.

When their juicer broke, they squeezed limes by hand. Then their labeler stopped working, forcing them to apply every label themselves.

Around midnight, Rossbach remembers looking at Sather and realizing they still had hours of work ahead of them. They had a choice: Call it a night and try again the following week or push through. The answer was clear. They turned up the music and kept working.

BUILT FROM SCRATCH: HOW A FAMILY TURNED CRAFT BEER INTO A HOLIDAY TRADITION

"That was the moment we realized we made the best business partners," Rossbach said. "We had the same determination and the same willingness to roll up our sleeves and figure things out, even when nothing was going according to plan."

That night set the tone for building Mixly, which is based in New Hope, Minnesota, outside Minneapolis — and it's a big reason the co-founders have always handled their own manufacturing.

Sticking to the vision

The team began developing recipes, with help from a mixologist friend to refine the flavors. Then COVID-19 disrupted their plans, forcing the founders to figure out production as they went. In an early interview, Rossbach said they were still making the products themselves in a rented kitchen while exploring ways to scale.

"When you start a business, there is no map," she said. Rossbach described the hardest part as facing the unknown: the constant decisions, self-doubt and possibility of getting things wrong.

The company has been self-funded from the beginning, without outside equity investors. The founders were intentional about building something of their own and maintaining control of the business. But that also means every dollar matters, and the stakes feel deeply personal.

"We've put our own money, time and countless hours of work into Mixly," Rossbach said.

Built for more than cocktails

Cocktails were the founders’ entry point, but they wanted their mixers to work for people who weren’t drinking, too. Rossbach was pregnant while the company took shape, just as the sober-curious movement began to emerge.

The founders saw an opportunity to create a product that could be enjoyed with or without alcohol, so no one at the gathering had to feel left out.

"Let’s make this versatile. Let’s make this for everyone," Rossbach said, recalling their early thinking.

That’s why Mixly’s alcohol-free positioning isn’t a recent response to a trend. The mixers have always been alcohol-free. What has changed is the surrounding market: More consumers are looking for flavorful drinks without alcohol, and retailers are beginning to recognize the variety of occasions Mixly can serve.

CEO SUNDAY: ATOMIC WINGS CEO SHARES HIS JOURNEY FROM WALL STREET TO THE RESTAURANT BUSINESS

"I think the interest in drinking less extends well beyond January or October," Rossbach said. "People want a good option for an ordinary Tuesday, dinner with friends or a celebration."

The mixers are designed to work whether customers add a spirit or pour them over sparkling water. That calls for more than sweetness. Mixly builds flavor with fruit, acidity, herbs and bitter botanicals. Its Bitter Orange Cherry mixer, for example, uses gentian root to balance sweetness with a more complex bitter note.

"A good alcohol-free drink does not need to apologize for what is missing," Rossbach said. "It doesn’t have to imitate a cocktail to deliver that."

New ways to enjoy Mixly

The founders began hearing from customers who were using Mixly in ways they hadn’t initially anticipated. One customer told them she added a mixer to her children's water for extra flavor. Others mentioned using the products in cooking and marinades.

Then Rossbach’s daughters became regulars at a local dirty soda shop. After spending about $20 on two drinks, Rossbach started thinking about how Mixly’s flavors could work in dirty sodas, too. Her daughters now make the drinks at home and have even set up a neighborhood stand.

That discovery opened a new occasion for the brand. A Mixly flavor can go into a dirty soda, a mocktail or a cocktail. The drink changes; the mixer stays the same.

Growing without losing the original idea

In June 2026, the company changed its name from Mixly Cocktail Co. to Mixly Beverage Co. The broader name reflects products and occasions beyond the bar cart, including dirty soda and coffee.

The expansion has brought Mixly into major retailers. Five flavored syrups launched at 685 Walmart stores. The company expects its dirty soda products to reach nearly 4,000 stores by the end of November, and two holiday kits launched at 1,300 Target stores and online. Mixly says its products are now available in approximately 4,600 retail locations nationwide.

What you think customers want isn't always what they actually want.

For Rossbach, that growth connects back to the idea the founders had from the beginning: Make something flavorful that people can share, whether they’re drinking alcohol or not. The market is catching up to that versatility, but it took hand-squeezed fruit, a rented kitchen and plenty of decisions without a map to get Mixly here.

When she first launched Mixly, Rossbach had an ultra-premium product line and a very specific idea of what the business would look like. But she quickly learned that what you think customers want isn't always what they actually want. The team listened, made adjustments and became more comfortable pivoting as they learned what was working and what wasn't.

That willingness to change has helped refresh the brand, expand beyond cocktail mixers and grow into opportunities they never would have imagined when they were squeezing limes in a kitchen at 3 a.m.

World.title: Gunman opens fire from moving car in European tourist hotspot, leaving 6 dead and at least 11 wounded
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Małopolska Police confirmed a Polish gunman opened fire at a popular tourist destination in Kraków on Saturday, killing six people and wounding at least eleven more.

Of the six dead, four are women and two are men, according to Małopolska Police.

Shooting from a moving vehicle, the gunman allegedly targeted people at random, injuring civilians as well as police during the attack on Kraków's bustling Main Square.

Video posted on social media showed people running while gunshots rang out.

Police shot and wounded the suspect during a gunfight and the area is now secured, according to authorities.

TEEN WEARING HELMET CAMERA KILLS WORKER AT POLISH SCHOOL AMID FEARS OF COPYCAT ATTACKS

The suspect, who has only been identified by police as a "citizen of the Republic of Poland," was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-style rifle to carry out the attack, Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Kraków police, told Polish network TVN24.

Authorities also found numerous other weapons and ammunition in the suspect's car, Cisło said.

GUNMAN KILLS 6 AT YOUTH WELFARE FACILITY IN SUSPECTED CHILD CUSTODY DISPUTE: REPORTS

Małopolska Police released a statement Saturday afternoon denying reports that a police officer died and that another perpetrator is being sought.

"The only known perpetrator of the incident is in police custody," officials said.

A public train driver reported around 3 p.m. local time that his vehicle had been shot by a man in a moving car, shattering his window.

GUNFIRE SHATTERS TORONTO LATIN STREET FESTIVAL, LEAVING AT LEAST 2 DEAD AND MULTIPLE WOUNDED

Police vehicles, ambulances, and a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter surrounded the scene at Main Square, which is located in the country's second-largest city.

Polish Police said in a statement on X, "in connection with the tragic incident that occurred in Kraków, National Police Commander Inspector General Marek Boroń is heading to the scene."

Polish leaders reacted to the scene in a series of public statements on social media.

'NOT ON OUR WATCH': GLOBAL LAW ENFORCEMENT LEADERS UNITE IN POLAND AGAINST HATE

"My deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims of the tragic attack in Kraków. My highest praise for the heroic police officers who risked their lives. And a heartfelt appeal to politicians of all stripes: do not exploit this tragedy. We will establish all the circumstances of this crime," Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote in a statement posted to X.

Tusk also assured the public that police are investigating the background and details of the attack.

POLISH PRESIDENT TURNS PLANE AROUND AFTER 'COUP' AT NATION’S TOP COURT

Poland's president Karol Nawrocki also weighed in.

"I am deeply concerned by reports of the tragic events in central Kraków. My thoughts are with the victims, those injured and their families. I remain in contact with the relevant services and expect a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events," he wrote on X.

HUNGARY AND POLAND DEFEND TOUGH MIGRATION POLICIES AS FRANCE REELS FROM VIOLENT UNREST

Nawrocki also revealed that the head of Poland's National Security Bureau is on his way to the city to investigate.

The United States Ambassador to Poland, Tom Rose, shared sympathies in a post on X.

"We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Kraków, a savage and murderous attack that’s shattered the peace of Poland," Rose wrote. "America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Kraków."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the shooting as "shocking," in a statement on X, also extending condolences to the victims' loved ones.

"There can be no justification for this attack, and we trust the perpetrator will face justice," Zelenskyy wrote. "We wish strength and a speedy recovery to the injured and to everyone affected by this tragedy. Ukraine stands in solidarity with Poland and the Polish people. People have the right to safety."

Shootings are exceedingly rare in Poland, a country that ranks among the world's lowest in gun-related deaths at 0.2 to 0.4 deaths per 100,000 residents, according to a study conducted by Medical University of Gdansk researchers.

The shooting comes amidst a constitutional crisis in Poland, pitting Tusk's pro-European Union government and the national conservative opposition.

Nawrocki's election to the presidency from the opposition has tumbled the nation's Parliament into a deadlock, seeing the executive use his veto power to block the appointments of would-be tribunal leaders, resulting in a paralyzed Constitutional Tribunal

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

World.title: Big Ten coach who had an abysmal record in the SEC thinks his team would be ranked in the SEC
World.content:
Illinois head football coach Bret Bielema, who went 11-29 against the SEC during his five-year run at Arkansas, thinks his current program would be ranked ... If it were in the SEC.

Quite the spin!

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

TIM BRANDO JOINS DAN DAKICH ON 'DON'T @ ME' TO DISCUSS INDIANA COACH CURT CIGNETTI'S CFP 'BIAS' COMMENTS

Now, to be fair, Illinois is having a decent season. The Fighting Illini are coming off a 24-13 win over Nebraska Friday night, and sit at 6-3 as the regular season begins its final month. It's been a good year for Illinois up to this point. Credit where it's due, Bielema has the fellas playing well in 2026.

For some reason, though, the SEC continues to be on the brains of every Big Ten coach in America right now. Earlier this week, Curt Cignetti took a shot at the conference after the initial CFP rankings was overloaded with SEC teams.

BRET BIELEMA ROASTS NICK SABAN, SEC, AT BIG TEN MEDIA DAYS: 'THEY WANT TO LIVE IN 2005 FOREVER'

After last night's win, Bielema joined the chorus, saying his unranked Fighting Illini would be in the mix if they played in the SEC.

Take a look:

Context is important here

"But to be in this job, where we’re at right now, 6-3, we beat another 5-3 team. If we were in the SEC, we’d probably be a top-15 team."

Thoughts? First impressions?

So, Bielema is correct in the fact that if Illinois was currently 6-3 and played an SEC conference schedule, it would be ranked. Not sure it would be a top-15 team, but certainly ranked. I guess it depends who the wins/losses came against.

But also, if Illinois played in the SEC ... I'm not sure the Fighting Illini would be a 6-3 team right now. Their current wins have come against:

Michigan State (in overtime)

Maryland (by 3)

UAB

Southern Illinois

Oregon (only ranked win)

Nebraska

One ranked win probably doesn't cut it. Now, Illinois' three losses? Purdue, Duke, and Ohio State (42-19). It doesn't feel like an "SEC schedule," at least not this season. The wins aren't impressive, beyond beating an Oregon team that has no business being ranked with Dante Moore out.

As for Bielema's actual record in the conference he can't get off his brain ...

He went 11-29 against the SEC over four years at Arkansas, including 0-8 in his first season. Not saying that was completely his fault because that roster certainly wasn't his, but the numbers are still the numbers.

And the numbers say Bret Bielema's current team would be nowhere close to 6-3 in the SEC right now.

It's a down year for the Big Ten. Let's just be honest for a second.

That conference has dominated this sport for a few years now, but it's just a down year. It happens. Ohio State lost its starting QB. Oregon did, too. Penn State stinks. Michigan stinks.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Indiana is currently ranked fourth, but needed overtime to beat both Michigan AND Minnesota.

Everyone wants to complain about the committee showing "SEC bias" in the initial batch of rankings earlier this week. That's fine. That's fair.

But the options weren't great.

World.title: Six people killed, at least a dozen injured in shooting at main market square of Krakow, Poland
World.content:
Authorities in Poland are investigating a shooting that left six people dead and at least a 15 injured in the Main Market Square in Krakow, a cultural center of the historic city, according to officials.

The shooter, a Polish national, was shot by police at the scene and taken to the hospital around 3 p.m. local time. The shots were fired from a vehicle moving through the area, Krakow officials said in a series of posts X.

An earlier post from the city’s official municipal government account said that investigators were working to determine the scale of the incident.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, told TVN24 that the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and he used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many pieces of other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car.

Dramatic video posted on social media shows what appears to be an injured police officer firing at the suspect before dropping to his knees and rolling over onto his back. The officer, who did not appear to have backup nearby, is seen struggling to reload his firearm and appeared to be clutching his right arm.

That officer’s condition was not known. Małopolska Police wrote in an X post that no officer had been killed, citing what they said were incorrect reports.

Other chilling video clips taken from the scene show a black sedan racing through the square. Dozens of people began running in various directions at the sound of gunfire.

Some social media clips depict responders attempting life-saving measures on victims. Lifeless bodies could be seen scattered around the streets after the attack.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also wrote on social media that police were trying to determine the circumstances surrounding the attack.

“We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Krakow, a savage and murderous attack that’s shattered the peace of Poland,” Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X. “America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow.”

The Main Market Square sits at the heart of Krakow’s medieval Old Town. Laid out in 1257, the sprawling plaza is home to the historic Cloth Hall and St. Mary’s Basilica.

World.title: The ‘slam dunk’ that wasn’t: Promising cholesterol drug fails to prevent heart attacks or stroke
World.content:
An experimental drug that held great promise in driving down a dangerous form of cholesterol didn’t show any measurable impact on heart attack or stroke in a clinical trial. The failure of the Novartis drug pelacarsen to help people who have high levels of lipoprotein(a) stunned researchers, who called it a massive blow to preventive cardiology.

Results of the clinical trial of pelacarsen, an injection, presented Saturday at a meeting of the American Heart Association, found there were zero decreases in stroke, heart attack, cardiovascular deaths or the number of procedures to open blocked arteries or restore blood flow to the heart.

“I really thought that this was going to be a slam dunk,” said Dr. Amanda Doran, an assistant professor of medicine in the division of cardiovascular medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Vanderbilt was one of nearly 800 sites involved in the clinical trial, called Horizon. “We were pretty invested, so it obviously hurts.”

Pelacarsen targets a stealthy and particularly lethal form of cholesterol called lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a). Much like low-density lipoprotein — LDL, or the “bad” cholesterol — Lp(a) causes plaque to build up in arteries. But it also helps form blood clots, and unlike LDL, it is entirely genetic.

About 1 in 5 Americans have high Lp(a), according to the American Heart Association. Most don’t realize they’re at risk.

Because people are born with those high levels, diet and exercise have no effect. That’s why heart experts have been so keen to find a drug that would handle the problem.

The Horizon trial included 8,322 people with high Lp(a) levels and who’d already had a heart attack, stroke or other heart problem within 10 years of starting the trial.

The drug did reduce Lp(a) significantly, by 78%, compared to a placebo drug that cut levels by 13%.

But that huge reduction ultimately meant nothing in terms of cardiovascular health.

Dr. Steven Nissen, the chief academic officer of the Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute at the Cleveland Clinic, led the trial. He said the dismal results took him by “extreme surprise.”

“Everybody, me included, believed that lowering levels of lipoprotein(a) substantially would reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events,” he said. “There is simply no evidence here that people that got more reduction did better.”

The findings, also published Saturday in the New England Journal of Medicine, confounded Nissen and other cardiologists who’ve long known that controlling other markers of heart health — LDL and blood pressure, for example — provides clear benefits.

“I have not seen a more shockingly neutral trial in a while,” said Dr. Karol Watson, co-director of the UCLA Program in Preventive Cardiology and a professor at UCLA’s David Geffen School of Medicine. Watson was not involved with the research.

There are several theories as to why the drug didn’t work as anticipated. It’s possible, Watson said, that the therapy was given too late in life to make a difference. The average age of Horizon’s study participants was 60, and they were followed for an average of five years.

“Remember that Lp(a) is a genetic disorder, so from the time a baby’s conceived, their Lp(a) is high. If we just swooped in in the last five years, maybe that’s too late,” Watson said.

Study participants were also treated aggressively in other ways to drive down their LDL cholesterol and get blood pressure readings into a healthy range. Participants may have also been taking aspirin because of a history of heart attack or stroke, which could have lessened Lp(a)’s clotting risk.

“How much of the Lp(a)-associated risk was remaining? We just don’t know,” Watson said.

Does Lp(a) still matter as a marker of heart health?

Doctors have only recently begun screening for it. Earlier this year, the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association released guidelines that every adult should have their Lp(a) levels measured. It’s a blood test that’s done once because levels are fixed and don’t change over time.

Experts stress that Lp(a) remains an important and valuable indicator of heart disease risk, even though the Horizon study failed to show any health benefit to driving down Lp(a) levels.

“None of that invalidates Lp(a) as a robust marker of cardiovascular disease risk,” said Dr. John Wilkins, a cardiologist at Northwestern Medicine and a professor in the division of cardiology at Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine. Wilkins was also one of the authors of the Lp(a) guidelines.

“It’s still worth testing for Lp(a) because it can help identify individuals with a higher probability of an event, and we do have other interventions that can help reduce their risk,” Wilkins said. “It’s just that at present, at least with this particular drug in this particular group of patients, we did not see benefit. That doesn’t mean that we might not find something or some way to lower Lp(a) that reduces risk. We just need more science to figure that out.”

UCLA’s Watson and Vanderbilt’s Doran agreed. “We have really good data to show that Lp(a) levels are predictive of disease,” Doran said. “People who have high Lp(a) need to be aware of that in order to pursue aggressive prevention strategies.”

What’s next in treating Lp(a)?

No further study of pelacarsen is planned, Nissen said, but similar drugs are in the pipeline: Eli Lilly’s lepodisiran, Amgen’s olpasiran and Silence Therapeutics’ zerlasiran.

All are injections that work by blocking the liver’s ability to produce Lp(a), but use different approaches. Pelacarsen is what’s known as an antisense oligonucleotide. The others use a technology called small interfering RNA, or siRNA, and may have fewer side effects, such as injection site reactions, Nissen said, than pelacarsen.

Like pelacarsen, all reduce Lp(a). Clinical trials to show whether they have any real-world heart health effects are ongoing.

Eli Lilly is also studying an oral drug called muvalaplin, and CRISPR gene-editing technology designed to permanently switch off the gene that produces Lp(a) is in early development.

“I’m still so hopeful,” Doran said. “We’re going to get it in the end.”

World.title: We want to hear your experience with changes to student loan repayment plans
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” has transformed the sprawling federal student loan system — and student borrowers are feeling the effects of the most consequential changes.

This year, the approximately 7.5 million student borrowers under the Biden-era Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, plan had to select a new one. So far, about 2 million borrowers have done so, after the Education Department warned that the SAVE plan was “illegal” and would be discontinued. The remaining borrowers who did not select a new plan were set to start receiving notices this month informing them that they missed a final deadline and were automatically moved to a new plan.

The Trump administration has said ending the SAVE plan would help streamline repayment programs while ensuring borrowers are paying off what they owe to the federal government. But student advocacy groups fear lower-income borrowers who had benefited from smaller monthly payments — or even qualified to make no payments at all based on their income — will end up with significantly higher bills under the other available plans.

We want to hear from you, whether you’re in this situation or are facing another challenge related to the recent student loan changes. Please share your experience by filling out the form below.

World.title: South Carolina man arrested after leaving sleeping 6-year-old daughter in line for Pokémon card release, police say
World.content:
A man was arrested in Charleston, South Carolina, on Friday after leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target to hold his place in line for the release of a new Pokémon trading card set, police said.

Officers responded around 2:30 a.m. to the Target in Charleston’s West Ashley neighborhood after a report of an unattended child, the Charleston Police Department said in a news release. They found the girl alone. Police identified the father as John-Michael Dooley, 35, of Johns Island, South Carolina.

Numerous customers had gathered outside the store overnight in anticipation of the release, according to the police. The latest expansion for the bestselling Pokémon Trading Card Game, “Mega Evolution — Delta Reign,” went on sale Friday. The decades-old Japanese franchise, which began as a children’s video game, centers on fictional creatures that players collect, train and battle. Packs starts at around $5.

The release does not say whether Dooley intended to buy the cards for himself or his daughter.

Witnesses told police that Dooley gave the girl a pillow and blanket before leaving her asleep in line sometime after 1 a.m. After about an hour passed without his return, concerned customers called police, authorities said.

When Dooley came back to the store, witnesses identified him and he was arrested, according to the release. Police said he admitted that he had gone home and left his daughter unattended so he could keep his place in line.

The child was unharmed and placed in emergency protective custody with the South Carolina Department of Social Services, police said.

Dooley was charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. He is being held at the Al Cannon Detention Center, according to the release, and could not immediately be reached for comment.

World.title: Mass shooting in Polish market leaves at least 6 dead, 15 injured
World.content:
A man drove into an open market in the Polish city of Krakow and opened fire from his car, killing at least six people and injuring at least 15 others, authorities said. The shooter was shot by police and taken into custody.

The shooting happened in the Main Market Square in Krakow around 3 p.m. local time on Saturday. Krakow police said the alleged shooter began firing at random people from his car. Police said the victims were four women and two men.

A damaged store display near Krakow's Main Market Square after a shooting that killed five people and injured more than 10 others, in Krakow, Poland, on Nov. 7, 2026. Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/via REUTERS

Police officers are among the wounded. The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a confrontation with police a short distance away from the initial violence, and was taken to a hospital for treatment.

The death toll earlier stood at five, but the Malopolski regional government updated it to six in a post on X.

Marcin Kierwiński, Poland's interior minister, wrote on X that two police officers were wounded by gunfire and one is in serious condition.

"Police officers in Kraków risked their lives to intervene. Immediately. Thanks to their heroic actions, the attacker was quickly apprehended," he wrote.

The alleged black car of the suspect in a shooting stands in the historic center of Krakow, Poland, on Nov. 7, 2026 where a gunman opened fire, killing five people and wounding around a dozen. Bartosz SIEDLIK /AFP via Getty Images

In a social media post, Krakow police said the gunman is a Polish citizen and that he acted alone.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, told TVN24 that the suspected gunman was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many pieces of other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car.

Emergency responders gather after a deadly shooting on Nov. 7, 2026, in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland. Omar Marques / Getty Images

"I am being kept informed by the Minister of the Interior about the situation in Krakow following the tragic shooting," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote on social media, adding that "the police are investigating the background and all the circumstances of the attack."

He later headed to Krakow from the capital, Warsaw, a government spokesperson said.

Other details were not immediately available.

"We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Krakow, a savage and murderous attack that's shattered the peace of Poland," Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X. "America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow."

Emergency responders gather after a deadly shooting on Nov. 7, 2026, in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland. Omar Marques / Getty Images



Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland, a European Union and NATO member of 38 million people.

"I saw a man shooting at people and walking around the square," Annette, a woman in her sixties, told news wire Agence France-Presse. "It's a tragedy for Krakow; we've never seen anything like this before."

A woman reacts at the site of a shooting near the main market square of Krakow, Poland, on Nov. 7, 2026. Jakub Porzycki / REUTERS

Kaja Kallas, the European Union's top diplomat, said in a statement that the EU stands with Poland and offered her condolences.

"The tragic loss of life in the shooting in Kraków is a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland," she wrote on X. "Poland's strength lies in the resilience of its people. In this moment of grief, Poland does not stand alone."

Krakow is the second-largest city in Poland and roughly 155 miles from the capital, Warsaw.

World.title: Pope Leo calls for universal healthcare weeks after lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Montevideo - Pope Leo XIV drew on his own recent experience of illness and hospitalization after surgery for lung cancer on Friday to make an impassioned appeal for universal access to healthcare, greater social equality and a society that does not measure people's worth by their productivity or wealth.

"Recently I experienced firsthand the limitations imposed by illness and I received care for which I am grateful," the Pope said in his first speech after arriving in Uruguay, to the country's political and civic leaders.

Pope Leo XIV was released from Rome's Gemelli Hospital four days after removing a cancerous tumor from his right lung. "The experience made me think of the many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis or receive the treatment they need."

"Ensuring that healthcare is accessible to everyone, regardless of their resources, is a duty that confronts every society," he said.

Uruguay is the first stop of a 12-day trip that also includes Argentina and Peru. Leo's doctors said he needed no further treatment after his operation and was cleared to travel. The trip schedule is the longest international journey of his pontificate so far, with 19,000 travel miles, 14 flights, 36 speeches and approximately 50 events.

Vatican officials told reporters ahead of the trip that the Pope would have a medical team travel with him, as is customary on papal trips, but that no special measures were being taken. "We're speaking of a 71-year-old person in good health," the Vatican spokesman said.

The Latin America journey is Leo's first return as Pope to the country and region that has profoundly shaped his vision, and where he spent decades of his life, first as an Augustinian missionary, and then as bishop of Chiclayo, Peru. The pope holds U.S. and Peruvian citizenship.

MONTEVIDEO, URUGUAY - NOVEMBER 6: Pope Leo XIV looks on during a welcome ceremony at Plaza Independencia as part of an official visit to Uruguay. Enzo Santos / MB Media / Getty Images

Leo's remarks on caring for the sick were part of a broad appeal for a society where the most vulnerable are protected, and where economic development benefits everyone rather than just the elite.

"The creation of wealth and economic initiative…must also translate into goods and opportunities that effectively reach everyone," Leo said.

While praising Uruguay for four decades of uninterrupted democracy, he stressed that a country's success is ultimately measured by how it protects human dignity and cares for the most vulnerable in society.

Leo also spoke in defense of children, including the unborn. Abortion was legalized in Uruguay in 2012, making it one of the first Latin American countries to do so.

"Their absolute dependence on their mother does not diminish the dignity to which they are entitled or the protection they deserve," the pope said.

Children, he said, must have access to quality education and opportunities to enter the workforce and achieve personal independence. Touching on a subject close to his heart, he said that technological advances and artificial intelligence must serve human beings rather than replace workers.

Leo will remain in Uruguay until Sunday when he will continue his travels to Argentina and Peru. The Vatican spokesman said there, Leo would address a range of issues, including the environment, arms tracking and political instability.

The Pope will also hold meetings with survivors of clerical sex abuse, but no further details are available as of now.

World.title: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
World.content:
Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors

toggle caption i Federico Parra/AFP via Getty Images
